line: At least the Vulcan was doing his duty as a Starfleet officer. But you, you betrayed us for what? Freedom from prison? Latinum? What was your price this time?

title: Caretaker
line: You are speaking to a member of my crew. I expect you to treat him with the same respect as you would have me treat a member of yours. Now, we have a lot to accomplish, and I suggest we all concentrate on finding our people and getting ourselves back home.

title: Caretaker
line: Based on my initial reconnaissance, Captain, I am convinced we are dealing with a single entity in the array. I would suggest he scanned our computers in order to select a comfortable holographic environment. In effect, a waiting room to pacify us prior to biometric assessment.

title: Caretaker
line: An examination?

title: Caretaker
line: It is the most logical explanation. Why else would he have released us unharmed?

title: Caretaker
line: Not all of us were.

title: Caretaker
line: Break out the compression phaser rifles. Meet us in Transporter Room two. We're going back. We'll divide into teams. Mister Tuvok, while Chakotay and I are looking for Torres and Kim, your job is to find out as much about this array as you can. It brought us here. We have to assume it can send us home. Agreed? Mister Rollins, maintain Red alert. Keep us on constant transporter locks.

title: Caretaker
line: Captain. I'd like to go with you.

title: Caretaker
line: If this has something to do with what Chakotay said.

title: Caretaker
line: It doesn't. I'd just, I'd hate to see anything happen to Harry.

title: Caretaker
line: Come on.

title: Caretaker
line: There are no humanoid lifeforms indicated, Captain. Kim and Torres are not within tricorder range. They may not be on the array.

title: Caretaker
line: He can tell us where they are.

title: Caretaker
line: Maintain your comm. link. I don't want to lose anyone else.

title: Caretaker
line: Oh, why have you come back? You don't have what I need.

title: Caretaker
line: I don't know what you need and frankly I don't care. I just want our people back and I want us all to be sent home.

title: Caretaker
line: Oh, well now. Aren't you contentious for a minor bipedal species?

title: Caretaker
line: This minor bipedal species doesn't take kindly to being abducted.

title: Caretaker
line: Oh, it was necessary.

title: Caretaker
line: Where are our people?

title: Caretaker
line: They are no longer here.

title: Caretaker
line: What have you done to them?

title: Caretaker
line: You don't have what I need. They might. No, you'll have to leave them.

title: Caretaker
line: We won't do that.

title: Caretaker
line: We are their commanding officers. We are entrusted with their safety. They are our responsibility. That may be a concept you don't understand.

title: Caretaker
line: Oh, no, I do understand, but I have no choice. There just is not enough time left.

title: Caretaker
line: Left for what?

title: Caretaker
line: I must honor a debt that can never be repaid, but my search has not been going well.

title: Caretaker
line: Tell us what you're looking for. Maybe we can help you find it.

title: Caretaker
line: You? I've searched the galaxy with methods beyond your comprehension. No, there's nothing you can do.

title: Caretaker
line: You've taken us seventy thousand light years from our home. We have no way back unless you send us, and we won't leave without the others.

title: Caretaker
line: But sending you back is terribly complicated. Don't you understand? I don't have time. Not enough time!

title: Caretaker
line: He's regaining consciousness.

title: Caretaker
line: How do you feel?

title: Caretaker
line: What am I doing here? Where am I?

title: Caretaker
line: Please don't try to move yet. You are very ill.

title: Caretaker
line: Ill? No, no. There's some mistake. I'm not

title: Caretaker
line: No!

title: Caretaker
line: Captain's log, stardate 48315.6. We've traced the energy pulses from the array to the fifth planet of the neighboring system and believe they may have been used in some fashion to transport Kim and Torres to the planet's surface.

title: Caretaker
line: Come in.

title: Caretaker
line: Captain, I've observed something peculiar about the pulses. They're getting faster.

title: Caretaker
line: Faster.

title: Caretaker
line: The interval between each pulse has decreased by point four seven seconds since we arrived. I can offer no explanation.

title: Caretaker
line: That's only one of the mysteries we're dealing with, Mister Tuvok. Take a look at this.

title: Caretaker
line: It's virtually a desert. Not one ocean, not one river. It has all the basic characteristics of an M-class planet except there are no nucleogenic particles in the atmosphere.

title: Caretaker
line: That would mean the planet is incapable of producing rain.

title: Caretaker
line: I've studied thousands of M-class planets. I've never seen an atmosphere without nucleogenics. There must have been some kind of extraordinary environmental disaster. As soon as repairs are complete, we'll set a course for the fifth planet.

title: Caretaker
line: Captain, you require sleep.

title: Caretaker
line: Kim's mother called me just after he left her. Delightful woman. He's her only son. He'd left his clarinet behind. She wanted to know if she had time to send it. I had to tell her no. Did you know he played clarinet in the Julliard Youth Symphony?

title: Caretaker
line: I did not have the opportunity to meet Mister Kim.

title: Caretaker
line: I barely knew him. I never seem to have the chance to get to know any of them. I have to, I have to take more time to do that. It's a fine crew and I've got to get them home.

title: Caretaker
line: The crew will not benefit from the leadership of an exhausted captain.

title: Caretaker
line: You're right as usual. I've missed your counsel, Tuvok.

title: Caretaker
line: I am gratified that you came after me so I can offer it once again.

title: Caretaker
line: I spoke to your family before I left.

title: Caretaker
line: Are they well?

title: Caretaker
line: Well, but worried about you.

title: Caretaker
line: That would not be an accurate perception, Captain. Vulcans do not worry.

title: Caretaker
line: They miss you.

title: Caretaker
line: As I do them.

title: Caretaker
line: I'll get you back to them. That's a promise, Tuvok.

title: Caretaker
line: Captain's log, supplemental. The Maquis ship and Voyager have encountered a debris field where sensors have detected a small vessel. One humanoid life form is on board.

title: Caretaker
line: Hail them.

title: Caretaker
line: Whoever you are, I found this waste zone first.

title: Caretaker
line: We're not interested in this debris, Mister

title: Caretaker
line: Neelix. And since you're not interested in my debris, well, I'm delighted to know you.

title: Caretaker
line: Captain Kathryn Janeway of the Federation starship Voyager.

title: Caretaker
line: A very impressive title. I have no idea what it means, but it sounds very impressive.

title: Caretaker
line: Do you know this area of space well, Mister Neelix?

title: Caretaker
line: I am famous for knowing it well. How may I be of service?

title: Caretaker
line: Do you know anything about the array that's sending energy pulses to the fifth planet?

title: Caretaker
line: I know enough to stay as far away from it as possible. Wait. Let me guess. You were whisked away from somewhere else in the galaxy, and brought here against your will.

title: Caretaker
line: Sounds as though you've heard this story before.

title: Caretaker
line: Sadly, yes. Thousands of times. Well, hundreds of times. Maybe fifty times. But the Caretaker has been bringing ships here for months now.

title: Caretaker
line: The Caretaker?

title: Caretaker
line: That's what the Ocampa call him. They live on the fifth planet. Did he kidnap members of your crew?

title: Caretaker
line: As a matter of fact, he did.

title: Caretaker
line: It's not the first time.

title: Caretaker
line: Do you know where he might have taken them?

title: Caretaker
line: Just that they're brought to the Ocampa. Nothing more.

title: Caretaker
line: We'd appreciate any help you could give us in finding these Ocampa.

title: Caretaker
line: I really wish that I could help you, I do, but as you can see, there's just there's so much debris for me to investigate today. You'd be surprised the things of value some people abandon.

title: Caretaker
line: Of course, we'd want to compensate you for your trouble.

title: Caretaker
line: Well, there's really very little that you could offer me. Unless.

title: Caretaker
line: Yes?

title: Caretaker
line: Unless of course, you had water.

title: Caretaker
line: If you help us find our missing crew members, you can have all the water you want.

title: Caretaker
line: That sounds like a very reasonable arrangement.

title: Caretaker
line: Good. We'll beam you over and tow your ship into our shuttle bay. Mister Tuvok, go to Transporter Room two and meet our guest.

title: Caretaker
line: Beam?

title: Caretaker
line: We have a technology which can take you instantly from your ship to ours. It's quite harmless. May we?

title: Caretaker
line: Energize.

title: Caretaker
line: Astonishing! You Federations are obviously an advanced culture.

title: Caretaker
line: The Federation is made up of many cultures. I am Vulcan.

title: Caretaker
line: Neelix. Good to meet you!

title: Caretaker
line: Interesting. What, what exactly, what exactly does all this, all this do?

title: Caretaker
line: I assure you that everything in this room has a specific function. However, it would take several hours to explain it all. I suggest we proceed to your quarters. Perhaps you would care for a bath.

title: Caretaker
line: A what?

title: Caretaker
line: It's okay. It's okay.

title: Caretaker
line: Who are you?

title: Caretaker
line: My name is Kim. Harry Kim. I'm an ensign on the Starship Voyager. I was kidnapped from the array just like you were. I don't know where we are.

title: Caretaker
line: What was Starfleet doing at that array?

title: Caretaker
line: We were looking for you, actually. One minute we're in the Badlands, the next

title: Caretaker
line: You mean you were trying to capture us.

title: Caretaker
line: Yeah. Consider yourself captured. Oh, I know I have a phaser here somewhere.

title: Caretaker
line: I don't find this at all amusing, Starfleet.

title: Caretaker
line: There's no point. It's locked. Hey! Hey, hey, hey. What's that going to accomplish?

title: Caretaker
line: What are they doing to us? What are these things growing on us?

title: Caretaker
line: Look, do you want them to sedate you again?

title: Caretaker
line: You're right, Starfleet. It's the Klingon half of me. It's just it's hard to control it sometimes.

title: Caretaker
line: What's your name, Maquis?

title: Caretaker
line: B'Elanna. B'Elanna Torres.

title: Caretaker
line: I hope you're feeling better. I know how frightening all this must be for both of you. I've brought some clothes if you'd care to change.

title: Caretaker
line: Why are you holding us here?

title: Caretaker
line: You are not prisoners. In fact, we consider you honored guests. The Caretaker has sent you to us. As long as you are not violent, you are free to leave your quarters.

title: Caretaker
line: What's wrong with us? What are these things?

title: Caretaker
line: We really don't know. You must be hungry. Would you care to join me on the courtyard for a meal?

title: Caretaker
line: Our food dispensers are right this way.

title: Caretaker
line: We're underground.

title: Caretaker
line: Our society is subterranean. We've lived here for over five hundred generations.

title: Caretaker
line: But before that, you lived on the surface?

title: Caretaker
line: Until the Warming began.

title: Caretaker
line: The Warming?

title: Caretaker
line: When our surface turned into a desert and the Caretaker came to protect us. Our ancient journals tell us he opened a deep chasm in the ground and led our ancestors to this place. Since then he has provided for all our needs. Please forgive them. They know you've come from the Caretaker. None of us has ever seen him. This way, please.

title: Caretaker
line: Does the Caretaker provide your meals too?

title: Caretaker
line: In fact, he does. He designed and built this entire city for us after the Warming. The food processors dispense nutritional supplements every four point one intervals. It may not offer the exotic tastes some of our younger people crave these days, but it meets our needs.

title: Caretaker
line: Is this how the Caretaker communicates with you? (The eating area has large picture windows showing different scenes - sunset, clouds, waterfall.)

title: Caretaker
line: He never communicates directly. We try to interpret his wishes as best we can.

title: Caretaker
line: I'm curious to know how you've interpreted the Caretaker's reason for sending us here.

title: Caretaker
line: We believe he must have separated you from your own species for their protection.

title: Caretaker
line: Their protection?

title: Caretaker
line: From your illness. Perhaps he's trying to prevent a plague.

title: Caretaker
line: We weren't sick until we met your Caretaker.

title: Caretaker
line: From time to time, he asks us to care for people with this disease. It's the least we can do.

title: Caretaker
line: There have been others? Like us?

title: Caretaker
line: Yes.

title: Caretaker
line: Where are they?

title: Caretaker
line: Your condition is serious. We don't know exactly how to treat it. I'm afraid the others did not recover.

title: Caretaker
line: Sir.

title: Caretaker
line: Ah, Mister Vulcan. Come in, come in, please. I can hardly see you.

title: Caretaker
line: I want to thank you for your hospitality. I must admit, I haven't had access to a food rebel er, er, replicator before.

title: Caretaker
line: I'd never have guessed.

title: Caretaker
line: And to immerse myself in water. Oh, do you know what joy this is? No one around here wastes water in this manner. Good sand scrub, that's the best that we can hope for.

title: Caretaker
line: I am pleased you are enjoying yourself, but we are in orbit of the fifth planet. We need your assistance.

title: Caretaker
line: Oh! Could you hand me the, er, towel?

title: Caretaker
line: If you will scan the large southern continent you'll find a range of extinct volcanoes. Follow the foothills north until you discover a dry riverbed. You'll find an encampment there.

title: Caretaker
line: Do you believe our people might be at this location?

title: Caretaker
line: It's not impossible. Maybe. Perhaps not. But we'll find them. We'll need several containers of water to bring for barter. Do these, er, replicators make clothing as well?

title: Caretaker
line: Yes.

title: Caretaker
line: Will it make me a uniform like yours?

title: Caretaker
line: No, it most certainly will not.

title: Caretaker
line: Why would anyone want to live in a place like this?

title: Caretaker
line: The rich cormaline deposits are very much in demand.

title: Caretaker
line: The Ocampa use it for barter?

title: Caretaker
line: Not the Ocampa, the Kazon-Ogla.

title: Caretaker
line: The Kazon-Ogla? Who are the Kazon-Ogla?

title: Caretaker
line: They are. Kazon sects control this part of the quadrant. Some have food, some have ore, some have water. They all trade and they all kill each other for it.

title: Caretaker
line: I thought you said the Ocampa had our people.

title: Caretaker
line: My friends, it's good to see you again!

title: Caretaker
line: I must speak with your Maje, the ever-wise Jabin!

title: Caretaker
line: Very amusing.

title: Caretaker
line: Destroy him.

title: Caretaker
line: Very amusing. I, I enjoy a joke as much as the next man. Jabin! My old friend! Water. Water, Jabin. I have water to replace all that I borrowed. Show them, Mister Paris. Their ship has technology that makes water out of thin air!

title: Caretaker
line: You have more?

title: Caretaker
line: Janeway to Voyager. Energize.

title: Caretaker
line: There's more where that came from, if you can help us.

title: Caretaker
line: How can we help someone so powerful they can create water out of thin air?

title: Caretaker
line: This man led us here suggesting we might find a people called the Ocampa. Do you know where they are?

title: Caretaker
line: Ocampa. She is Ocampa.

title: Caretaker
line: Why would you be interested in such worthless creatures? They live only nine years. They make poor servants. We caught her when she wandered to the surface.

title: Caretaker
line: To the surface? You mean they live underground?

title: Caretaker
line: The entity in space that gives them food and power also gives them sole access to the only water on this world, two miles below the surface.

title: Caretaker
line: This same entity has abducted two of our people. We believe they might be with the Ocampa.

title: Caretaker
line: There's no way to get to them. We tried. The entity has established some kind of subterranean barrier we can not penetrate.

title: Caretaker
line: But she got out.

title: Caretaker
line: Occasionally, some of them do find their way to the surface. We don't know how, but the Ocampa seal the tunnels afterwards.

title: Caretaker
line: Maybe she can help these good people find a way down.

title: Caretaker
line: You'd be wasting your time. I've used every method of persuasion I know to get her to help us. She won't.

title: Caretaker
line: Then she's worthless to you. Let us trade you water for this scrawny little thing.

title: Caretaker
line: I'd be more interested in acquiring this technology that allows you to create water from thin air.

title: Caretaker
line: That would be difficult. It's integrated into our ship's systems.

title: Caretaker
line: Tell them to drop their weapons. Drop them, my friends, or he dies in an instant.

title: Caretaker
line: Do it. Do it!

title: Caretaker
line: Step aside.

title: Caretaker
line: Come on!

title: Caretaker
line: I strongly suggest you get us out of here.

title: Caretaker
line: Six to beam up.

title: Caretaker
line: My dearest. Didn't I promise I'd save you?

title: Caretaker
line: Look, I'm sure Captain Janeway is doing everything she can to find us.

title: Caretaker
line: What makes you think any of them are still alive?

title: Caretaker
line: Should I call for some help?

title: Caretaker
line: No.

title: Caretaker
line: Are you in pain?

title: Caretaker
line: Are you watching us? I thought we weren't supposed to be your prisoners.

title: Caretaker
line: I wasn't watching you. I was coming to give you something. I don't know if it'll help. It's a medicine. There are people who have broken from tradition and left the city. Their colony grows fruits and vegetables. They discovered quite by accident that the moss that grows on certain fruit trees has healing properties. I'm sorry for what has happened to you.

title: Caretaker
line: Appreciate this, but the only way we're going to survive is if we can get to the surface and find our own people.

title: Caretaker
line: The elders would say that's against the Caretaker's wishes.

title: Caretaker
line: What do you say?

title: Caretaker
line: The Caretaker's been behaving strangely for the past several months. Abducting people, increasing the power supply.

title: Caretaker
line: Power supply.

title: Caretaker
line: He's tripled the energy he sends us. They say we have enough stored now to run the city for five years.

title: Caretaker
line: Nobody knows why?

title: Caretaker
line: When we ask, we're told to trust the Caretaker's decisions. One person I knew did get to the surface. We never saw her again.

title: Caretaker
line: How?

title: Caretaker
line: The ancient tunnels that brought us here still exist. Over the years, small breaches in security barriers have appeared just large enough for someone to get through. But it still requires digging through meters of rock to get out.

title: Caretaker
line: Can you get us tools to dig with?

title: Caretaker
line: It would take days, maybe even weeks to break through. You have to rest. Conserve your strength.

title: Caretaker
line: Please. It's our only chance.

title: Caretaker
line: If you had told us what you had planned, we might have anticipated your irrational behavior.

title: Caretaker
line: Irrational? We got out of there, didn't we?

title: Caretaker
line: Excuse me. Don't blame Neelix.

title: Caretaker
line: That's enough. This is a sickbay, not a conference room. Visiting hours are over. Everyone except my patient is to leave immediately.

title: Caretaker
line: Computer, end Medical Holographic Program.

title: Caretaker
line: I never should have gone to the surface. I'm too curious. I'm told it's my worst failing.

title: Caretaker
line: No, no, it's a wonderful quality. Your most endearing.

title: Caretaker
line: Would you be willing to take us underground to look for our missing crew?

title: Caretaker
line: I'm afraid Jabin was right. There's no way to get down. The tunnel I came out has been sealed.

title: Caretaker
line: We don't need a tunnel. We have the ability to transport there directly.

title: Caretaker
line: Captain, our sensors did not pick up any indication of an underground civilization. The subterranean barrier Jabin described may be responsible. It might also block our transporter.

title: Caretaker
line: There are breaches in the security barrier where it's begun to decay. That's how I got out.

title: Caretaker
line: Have the transporter room begin a sweep for any breaches we might be able to beam through.

title: Caretaker
line: Kes can tell you where to go. But now that she's free, we're leaving this system together.

title: Caretaker
line: Neelix, these people rescued me.

title: Caretaker
line: I rescued you.

title: Caretaker
line: With their help. It would be wrong not to help them now.

title: Caretaker
line: Captain, the pulses from the array continue to accelerate. The intervals between them have decreased another point eight seconds.

title: Caretaker
line: Kes.

title: Caretaker
line: Hello, Daggin.

title: Caretaker
line: We thought we'd never see you again. How did you get back?

title: Caretaker
line: These people rescued me from the Kazon. I'm trying to help them find two of their crewmen. Does anyone know where the aliens are kept? The ones the Caretaker sends here?

title: Caretaker
line: I think they're at the central clinic.

title: Caretaker
line: Can you take us there?

title: Caretaker
line: No, she cannot.

title: Caretaker
line: They can't speak telepathically, Toscat. Please talk aloud.

title: Caretaker
line: I didn't meant to be rude but you should not be here.

title: Caretaker
line: We'll be glad to leave once we find our crewmen.

title: Caretaker
line: That won't be possible. We cannot interfere with the Caretaker's wishes.

title: Caretaker
line: Maybe you can't, but we can.

title: Caretaker
line: You don't understand.

title: Caretaker
line: That's right. They don't understand. They have no way of knowing that the Ocampa have been dependent on the Caretaker for so long, we can't even think for ourselves any more. They don't understand we were once a people who had full command of our mind's abilities.

title: Caretaker
line: The stories of our ancestor's cognitive abilities are apocryphal. At the very least exaggerated.

title: Caretaker
line: We lost those abilities because we stopped using them.

title: Caretaker
line: We should not dwell on what's been lost but on all that's been gained.

title: Caretaker
line: We've gained a talent for dependence, for simply taking what we're given. I'm going to help them, Toscat, whether you like it or not, and I think my friends will join me.

title: Caretaker
line: You defied the Caretaker by going to the surface, Kes. Learn from the experience. Follow the path he has set for us.

title: Caretaker
line: I've learned very well, Toscat. I saw the sunlight. I can't believe that our Caretaker would forbid us to open our eyes and see the sky. Come with me. We'll find your people.

title: Caretaker
line: Come on. Don't let it beat you, Starfleet. Come on.

title: Caretaker
line: I'm sorry.

title: Caretaker
line: All right. It's all right. We'll rest a minute.

title: Caretaker
line: Maybe I'd do better if I had a little Klingon blood in me.

title: Caretaker
line: Trust me, it's more trouble than it's worth.

title: Caretaker
line: You know, I spent my whole life getting ready for Starfleet. And on my very first mission, I'm going to die.

title: Caretaker
line: We're not finished yet. I know a few things that old Sneezy didn't teach in his survival course.

title: Caretaker
line: Sneezy?

title: Caretaker
line: Commander Zakarian, remember? He must have been allergic to everything.

title: Caretaker
line: You went to the Academy.

title: Caretaker
line: Actually made it into the second year before we, er, we mutually agreed that it wasn't the place for me.

title: Caretaker
line: You know, I never really liked Zakarian.

title: Caretaker
line: Shush. Listen. They're getting faster.

title: Caretaker
line: Away team to Voyager.

title: Caretaker
line: Voyager here.

title: Caretaker
line: What's going on with the array?

title: Caretaker
line: It's no longer sending out pulses, Captain, and it appears to be realigning its position.

title: Caretaker
line: Keep me informed. Janeway out.

title: Caretaker
line: They haven't been at the clinic for hours.

title: Caretaker
line: We can search the city. Ask if anyone's seen them.

title: Caretaker
line: If they were trying to get to the surface, how would they go?

title: Caretaker
line: Probably the same way I did. Up one of the ancient tunnels.

title: Caretaker
line: Mister Paris, you and Neelix go with her and start checking them out. We need to talk to every doctor and nurse at this hospital, see what they can tell about Torres and Kim.

title: Caretaker
line: Voyager to Janeway.

title: Caretaker
line: Go ahead.

title: Caretaker
line: Captain, the array is firing some kind of weapon at the surface. It seems to be trying to seal the energy conduits.

title: Caretaker
line: Understood. Keep a channel open.

title: Caretaker
line: If the array is the Ocampa's sole source of energy, why would the Caretaker seal the conduits?

title: Caretaker
line: He would seal them if he no longer intended to use them, to protect the Ocampa from their enemies. Captain, there is now enough evidence to form a reasonable hypothesis. I believe that the Caretaker is dying.

title: Caretaker
line: Explain.

title: Caretaker
line: First, he increases the energy supply to provide the city with a surplus to last at least five years. Then he seals the conduits. The logical conclusion is that he does not intend to continue his role as Caretaker.

title: Caretaker
line: That doesn't necessarily mean he's dying. He could be leaving.

title: Caretaker
line: Doubtful. Not after a millennium of providing for these people. I believe that the Caretaker owes something to the Ocampa. I believe the debt that can never repaid is very likely a debt to them. In addition, there were his frequent references to running out of time. I think he knew his death was imminent.

title: Caretaker
line: If he dies, how the hell are we supposed to get home?

title: Caretaker
line: They're in this one. Harry! Paris to Janeway.

title: Caretaker
line: Go ahead.

title: Caretaker

title: Phage
line: Neelix

line: You should just let me die.

line: Visiting hours are over. He needs rest.

line: Seventeen hundred hours. Not a minute before.

line: I'll see you then.

title: Phage
line: Captain! We've completed our diagnostic on the alien device. It appears to be more than a weapon. It's also a very sophisticated medical scanner and surgical instrument.

title: Phage

line: So it sounds like we're dealing with aliens who've developed a technology specifically designed to locate and extract organs from other beings. Why?

title: Phage
line: Captain! The alien ship has dropped out of warp. It's approaching a large asteroid.

line: On screen.

title: Phage
line: Hold position here. Mister Kim?

line: I can't scan the interior. The surface stratum is made up of some sort of neutronium alloy. It doesn't look like a natural formation.

line: Are you saying some one built this asteroid?

line: It's possible.

title: Phage

line: I think I've located where the alien ship entered. There's an open crater on the limb of the asteroid.

line: Captain, may I suggest you consider carefully what you are about to do.

line: You're on the Starship Voyager. I'm Captain Kathryn Janeway of the United Federation of Planets.

line: Yes, it attacked our people over two millennia ago. It consumes our bodies, destroys our genetic codes and cellular structures.

title: Phage
line: Our immuno-technology cannot keep up. The phage adapts. It resists all attempts to destroy it. Our society has been ravaged. Thousands die each day. There is no other way for us to survive.

title: Phage
line: I have a great sympathy for what your race has endured, but I cannot allow you to keep the organs you removed from one of our crew members. We need them back immediately.

title: Phage
line: I'm afraid that isn't possible. I have already bio-chemically altered the air-breathing organs and grafted them into Motura's body. They are a part of him now.

title: Phage
line: He is my honatta. His task is to find the organs I need for survival. We, we try to extract them from the dead

title: Phage

title: Phage
line: So now I am left with the same choice you made. Whether to commit murder to save a life, or to allow my own crewman to die while you breath air through his lungs.

title: Phage
line: It must be impossible for you to understand how any civilized people could come to this. Before the phage began, we were known as educators and explorers, a people whose greatest achievements were artistic. I myself am a sculptor of note on my world. All I can say is that when your entire existence is at stake

line: You don't have to explain yourself, Motura.

title: Phage
line: If the consequence of this act is a death sentence, so be it. At least it will put an end to my suffering.

title: Phage
line: I can't begin to understand what your people have gone through. They may have found a way to ignore the moral implications of what you are doing, but I have no such luxury. If we were closer to home I would lock you up and turn you over to my authorities for trial, but I don't even have that ability here, and I am not prepared to carry you forever in our brig. So I see no other alternative but to let you go. Take a message to your people. title: Phage
line: Quite.

title: Phage
line: Wait. I want to see this crewman of yours.

title: Phage
line: That can serve no useful purpose.

title: Phage
line: Maybe it can. Our medical technologies may be superior to theirs.

title: Phage
line: I can tell you, from what we've observed of them, that they are considerably superior.

title: Phage
line: She spared my life. Our lives. We owe it to them to see if there's anything we can do to help him.

title: Phage
line: I'll take you to him.

title: Phage
line: His simulated organs are primitive. It's amazing he is still alive.

title: Phage
line: This is set to scan only.

title: Phage

title: Phage
line: Strange. According to my readings, you are not here.

title: Phage
line: Believe me, I wish I weren't.

title: Phage
line: The rest of you are healthy. You are compatible for organ transplant.

title: Phage
line: Wait a minute. We've already considered this. Talaxian physiology is different from that of anyone else on this ship. His immune system would reject their lungs immediately.

title: Phage
line: Your surgical knowledge is inferior. We will simply adapt his immunogenicity. It won't be a problem. Which of you will donate a lung?

title: Phage
line: Me.

title: Phage
line: No, absolutely not. It's too dangerous. Let someone else do it.

title: Phage
line: No, I want to do it, Neelix. I'm willing to take the risk. Besides, you've done so much for me, let me give you something this once. Just for once

title: Phage
line: All right.

title: Phage
line: I look forward to sampling your cooking, Mister Neelix.

title: Phage
line: You mean I can keep my kitchen?

title: Phage
line: Well, at least until we get the replicators back online.

title: Phage
line: Thank you, Captain. And Captain? I'll see you at breakfast.

line: Captain's log, supplemental. The aliens have successfully transplanted one of Kes' lungs into Neelix. The dampening field has been deactivated, and I have allowed them to beam back to their vessel. We are resuming a course home.

title: Phage
line: It's all right. The operation was a success. Neelix is asleep and breathing on his own now. With your lung.

title: Phage
line: I feel a little light-headed.

title: Phage
line: That will pass. You'll soon adapt to diminished lung capacity. I spoke to the Captain about you. She's given me permission to begin training you as a medical assistant. You'll be a back-up for Mister Paris, or possibly a replacement. That is, assuming you're interested.

title: Phage
line: We'll begin your lessons as soon as you've fully recovered.

title: Phage
line: Thank you, Doctor.

title: Phage
line: Thank you. You've given me a lot to think about.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Captain's log, stardate 48579.4. The crew has been scanning constantly for anomalies that might help us shorten our journey home. Ensign Kim has reported an exciting discovery. A subspace disturbance which may be a wormhole.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Let's see what you have, Mister Kim.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: There. It's registering only on subspace bands. We don't even have it on long range sensors yet.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Verteron emanations. Tunneling secondary particles. It certainly looks like a wormhole.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: But is it stable enough for us to enter, and if it is, where does it lead?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: There is, of course, a seventy five percent chance the wormhole will not lead to the Alpha Quadrant.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Very true. But you can also say there's a one in four chance it will. Those aren't bad odds. Any analysis yet, Ensign?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Too far away. We'd have to be within a thousand kilometers to get a detailed analysis. That would mean a significant course change.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Well, Mister Kim, if there's even the possibility of finding a wormhole, I think we can afford a detour. Lieutenant, input the coordinates and change course.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Aye, Captain. And may I suggest, if this works, we petition the Federation Astronomical Committee to officially designate this the Harry Kim Wormhole.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Captain, we're approaching the coordinates of the wormhole.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: On screen. Are we in visual range?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Affirmative, Captain, and the anomaly is still registering on subspace bands.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Sensors also indicate it's there.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Magnify. Increase to highest magnification.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: If that's a wormhole, it must be the smallest one on record.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Mister Kim, are you able to analyze it?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Aye Captain. It's virtually microscopic. The aperture is only about thirty centimeters in diameter.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I guess it's a little too small for us to fly through.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: However, it might be large enough to act as a conduit for a message.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: That's right. It could carry a compressed data transmission to Federation space in minutes.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: We still have to find out if it goes anywhere near the Alpha Quadrant. Can you trace it's subspace bearing?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I can't get any directional readings at all. The aperture is too small.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I recommend we launch a microprobe into the wormhole.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Agreed. Do it, Lieutenant.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Aye, Captain.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: We're receiving telemetry.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: It doesn't look like any wormhole I've ever studied.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Microscopic gravitational eddies, extremely constricted spatial dimensions. The pathway's barely wider than the probe itself.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I think what we're seeing is a wormhole in an advanced state of decay. Must be ancient. Probably been collapsing for centuries.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Does that mean we can't send a message through it?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: No, I can do it. Maybe it'll take longer to get through, but the wormhole's still stable enough to carry a transmission.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Any idea yet where that message would end up, Ensign?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I'll try extrapolating the verteron exit vector. No, I can't get it. There's a strange phase variance in the radiation stream. We'll have to wait until the probe exits.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: That shouldn't take long.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Captain, I'm getting a distorted energy reading.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: The probe's telemetry has changed.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: It's stuck.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Stuck?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: It's mired in a gravitational eddy, and because the wormhole's in a state of collapse, those eddies are incredibly dense. That probe will never break free, Captain, and we'll have no way of finding out where the wormhole ends.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Let's give it some time. Maybe it will work itself loose.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Captain?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: What is it, Ensign.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Our probe was just scanned. There's somebody on the other side of the wormhole.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: It started acting up a couple of days ago. I'd been working out in the gym, maybe I overdid it.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Is it sore here?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Yes.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Localized tenderness to the ulna bone, no epidermal damage, moderate oedema. What are the possible diagnoses?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Epicondylitis, strained ligament, torn muscle and hairline fracture.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: That's exactly right.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I've studied all the material you gave me. I'm ready for more.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Good. There's a great deal more for you to learn. The tricorder indicates this is a small stress fracture.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Can this guy do everything a real doctor does?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Yes, he can. Activate it and direct the beam here. That's it. Not quite so fast.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: If I had to get treatment for something serious, if I needed surgery for instance, would he be performing it?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Of course, and quite expertly too.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I don't know. I'd have to think twice about that.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Fine. And if you were lucky you wouldn't die on the table while you were making up your mind. That should do it. How does it feel?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Not bad. Thanks.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Doctor, did you notice how rudely that officer treated you?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Not more so than most.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: You mean others act that way too.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Let's just say I've become accustomed to being treated like a hypospray. Now, here's some material on first aid for burns.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Doctor, I think I'd like to do more than study first aid. I'd be interested in knowing more about anatomy and physiology.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: You're intellectually curious. I like that. These deal with human anatomy and physiology, but they weren't written for the layman. They're quite technical.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I understand. I'll do my best. And I really appreciate your help.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: We've analyzed the data. So far our sensors have detected four separate scans of the microprobe, each one on a progressively narrower band. Someone on the other end of that wormhole is definitely interested in that probe.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: We cannot preclude the possibility that there is a microscopic entity within the wormhole curious about an intruder.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: That's possible, but you'd think our probe would have detected something like that.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: What's the condition of the probe now?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I've been monitoring it from Engineering. It's still embedded in a gravitational eddy, but within seventy two hours it will be crushed.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: But until then it should continue to transmit telemetry.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: If we're reading scans from the other side, it's possible the probe is acting as a relay. If that's true, we should be able to use it to transmit a message to whoever is executing the scan.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Yes. I can modify our subspace communications band to accept the probe as a booster.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Let's try it, Mister Kim.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I'll give you a hand.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I fear Mister Kim's exuberance may turn into an equally intense disappointment if his efforts prove in vain.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: You may be right, but I'd rather assume that he's going to be successful.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Okay, I've boosted power to the communications bandwidth. Now all we have to do reconfigure the signal generator so it's compatible with the probe's long range sensors.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I'm on it. Just a few minutes more.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: This has to work. It'll mean so much to people back home to know we're alive and headed for Federation space.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: We haven't been gone that long. People won't give up on us so soon. They probably just think we're lost.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: It's still going to be hard on my folks. I always called them once a week, even when I was on my training missions. I've never been out of contact for so long.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Well, it is going to work, Starfleet, so pretty soon they're going to know you're all right.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: How about you? Any family?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I haven't seen my father since I was five. He and my mother separated. He went back to Earth and that was the last I saw of him.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: And your mom?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I think she's on the Klingon Homeworld.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: You think?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: We didn't get along very well. Okay, the signal generator should be tuned to the probe's long range sensors.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Isn't there anyone back home who'll be worried about you?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: The Maquis are as to a close family as I've ever had. Most of my friends are here, on the ship, so no, there's no one back home who's going to care one way or the other whether I'm alive. We're ready to transmit.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Engineering to Bridge.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Janeway here.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: We have a communications link with the microprobe. We're going to try sending a preliminary test signal, a series of sub-harmonic pulses.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: They stand the best chance of transmission through the wormhole.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Acknowledged.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Proceed.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Aye, Captain.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I'm reading transmission of the test signal. The probe has received it and relayed it.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: How will we know if the signal reaches somebody?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: The only way is if that somebody answers.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: There's no response.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: It's too soon. Remember, we have no idea how long it takes to reach the other side.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Are you reading anything, Mister Tuvok?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Negative Captain. There is nothing that would suggest a response.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Even if someone receives our signal, it might take them some time to figure out how to return it.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: You're right. Janeway to Kim. Continue transmitting.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Aye Captain.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: How long shall we keep it up?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Until I tell you otherwise.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: You have the bridge, Commander.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Captain.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Mister Tuvok.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I'm getting something, Captain.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I'm getting it too. A subspace signal relayed through the probe.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: That signal is being transmitted at exactly the same frequency and amplitude as our signal. It's a response. Someone received our transmission and sent one back, and their signal originated in the Alpha Quadrant.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Captain's log, supplemental. Encouraged by his success in transmitting a signal to the Alpha Quadrant, Mister Kim is investigating the possibility of establishing a voice link with whoever is at the other end of the wormhole.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Come in. Kes, this is a surprise.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Am I interrupting?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Not at all. I was just going to have a cup of soup. Would you like anything?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Ah, spinach juice with a touch of pear, please. Tom Paris introduced me to it, it's very nutritious.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I'm sure. Computer, one spinach juice with a touch of pear and one cup of vegetable bouillon. What can I do for you?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: If there were a member of the crew whose needs weren't being met, would you want to know about it?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Of course. Kes, do you and Neelix feel that your needs are being ignored?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Of course not, we're very happy here. I'm referring to the Doctor.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: The Doctor?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I don't understand why people treat him the way they do.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: How do people treat him?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: As though he doesn't exist. They talk about him while he's standing right there. They ignore him. They insult him.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Well as a matter of fact, I've been hearing the other side of the coin. Many of the crew have complained that the Doctor is brusque, even rude, that he lacks any bedside manner. We've been talking about reprogramming him.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: You can do that? It doesn't seem right.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Kes, he's only a hologram.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: He's your Medical Officer. He's alive.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: No he's not.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: He's self aware, he's communicative, he has the ability to learn.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Because he's been programmed to do that.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: So because he's a hologram he doesn't have to be treated with respect or any consideration at all?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Very well, I'll look into it.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Thank you, Captain.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Okay, we'll be ready to go online in a couple of minutes.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I'm still worried about the gravitational interference. I don't think the co-variant isolator will be effective with a vocal transmission.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Let's try inverting the narrow band filter.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Progress report, Ensign.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I think we're ready to give it a try, though we're pushing through some pretty heavy gravitational interference. I can't guarantee the clarity of the transmission.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Let's see what happens. This is Captain Kathryn Janeway of the Federation Starship Voyager. Do you read?

line: I'll narrow the filter bandpass some more. Try again, Captain.

line: This is Kathryn Janeway of the Federation ship Voyager. Is anyone receiving this communication?

line: This is Janeway. Please repeat your last transmission.

line: Cargo vessel, we're still trying to clear up your last transmission. Please repeat one more time.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I am Captain of the cargo vessel Talvath, location Alpha Quadrant, sector one three eight five. What is your location?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: We're in the Delta Quadrant, but since this quadrant hasn't been charted I can't specify our exact location.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Please confirm. You said Delta Quadrant?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Correct.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: In a Federation starship?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Yes. We were on a mission and we got pulled into this quadrant.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Pulled in? How?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: It's a complicated story. Please, if you would just try deconstructing the phase shift of our hailing frequency you could verify.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: You are undoubtedly still in the Alpha quadrant. What are your coordinates?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I assure you I am telling you the truth. We are in the Delta quadrant, seventy thousand light years from you.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: This is preposterous. You are obviously lying. I am terminating communication.

line: No, no, wait! Kim! Hail them again.

line: No response, Captain.

line: Why would he have broken off transmission?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Perhaps I can offer an explanation. The comm. link signature of his transmission indicates the message originated from a Romulan ship. Further, there are no known shipping lanes in the sector he identified. Given the precise calibration of his signal I would suggest that he is in fact on board a science vessel.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Why would he pretend to be a cargo captain.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: If he's engaged in some kind of secret research he might want to conceal that fact.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Precisely. When we claimed to be transmitting from the Delta quadrant, an impossibility so far as he knows, he may have feared we were Federation spies.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Just our luck. We raise one ship from the Alpha quadrant and it has to be Romulan.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: That Romulan still has the ability to get a message to Starfleet. Mister Kim, hail the Talvath repeatedly. Call me the minute you re-establish contact. Commander, you have the bridge.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Aye, Captain.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Computer, initiate Emergency Medical Holographic Program.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Please state the nature of the medical emergency.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: There is no emergency, Doctor.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Well, that's good. I was right in the middle of preparing a culture to test Lieutenant Hargrove for Arethian flu when Ensign Kyoto deactivated me.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I'm sure she didn't realize you were busy.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: What is it you want, Captain.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Actually, I thought we might just talk for a moment.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: About what?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Doctor, you were originally programmed to serve in a limited fashion during an emergency. Now you're being asked to do much more.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: That's certainly true. I'm providing full time medical service for the entire ship's crew, functioning both as doctor and nurse, and now as an instructor as well.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: You don't have the luxury of thinking of yourself as am Emergency Medical Program any more. You've become a full-fledged member of the crew.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I see. Are you suggesting that I be re-programmed?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: No. I'm asking if there's anything I can do to help you.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Help me?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: If there's anything you need, or want, I'd like to see that you get it.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: What I'd like is to be turned off when people leave. I spend hours here with absolutely nothing to do. When someone does remember to deactivate me they do so without asking if it's convenient. It's extremely irritating.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: What if I gave you control over your deactivation sequence?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I beg your pardon?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I'm sure we can make it possible for you to turn yourself off, or to prevent being turned off.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I, I might like that.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I'll have someone look into it. Anything else?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I'm not sure, I'll have to give it some thought.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: You do that.

title: Eye of the Needle

line: Janeway here.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Captain, we've got him back. The Romulan.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Good work. Put him through to my quarters.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: This is Kathryn Janeway.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: This is the cargo vessel Talvath.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Thank you for answering our hail, Captain. What is your name? How may I address you?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I'd prefer not to give my name.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Very well, I understand that you must have been skeptical when I told you where we are. I hope you've been able to verify our position.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: My analysis of your hailing frequency seems to indicate that it originates in the Delta quadrant, but I am not precluding the possibility that you've been able to create that illusion somehow.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: To what end?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I'm not sure. That doesn't negate the possibility.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: How can I assure you of my truthfulness?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: You say you are a Federation ship. Are you a Starfleet vessel?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Yes, we are.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: And your mission in the Delta quadrant?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Our mission was originally in the Alpha quadrant. We were pulled against our will to our present location. Now we're trying to get home.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Aren't you in fact Starfleet spies on a surveillance mission?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Captain, I understand your concern. Naturally the Romulan Empire doesn't want Starfleet spying on it's science vessels, but since we're seventy thousand light years from Romulan space and a subspace message to Starfleet would take years, I think you have to admit that we can't be much of a threat to you. You have nothing to fear from us.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Soothing words, Captain, but they are only words.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: If we were spies, we wouldn't be asking what I'm going to ask you now. We have no way of communicating with Starfleet, with our friends and families. We're hoping you might be able to relay a message for us. Our crew is not large. Each of them could write a short personal message. You'd be welcome to read them all before passing them on. I think you'd be convinced that they're nothing more than the heartfelt words of some very lonely people.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Captain, it would ease my apprehension if I could see that you are who you say you are. I have a signal amplifier on board. I've been working to reconfigure the protocols to penetrate the radiation stream of the wormhole. I think it might be possible to establish a visual link between us.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I have no objection. When that's done, will you help us?

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I make no promises. Let us proceed one step at a time. Have your officers contact me in order to attempt the visual link. Goodnight.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Goodnight.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: We're ready to try a visual link with the Romulan ship, Captain.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Good work.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: We didn't have any trouble configuring the protocols, but that phase variance in the radiation stream gave us a few problems. Torres is going to balance it manually from Engineering.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Okay, we've got the communications frequency locked in.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: On screen.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I presume you are Captain Janeway.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: Yes. I want to thank you, Captain, for maintaining contact with us. It means a great deal to me and to my crew.

title: Eye of the Needle
line: I am not familiar with this class of ship.

title: Eye of the Needle
