title: Cathexis
line: Captain's log, stardate 48734.2. Sometimes it's a good idea to get away from being a Captain for a while. To that end, I've started participating in a new holonovel. The setting is ancient England.

title: Cathexis
line: The drawing room is in here.

title: Cathexis
line: Bridget, take Mrs Davenport's cape, and tell Lord Burleigh that she's here.

title: Cathexis
line: Yes, ma'am.

title: Cathexis
line: There's tea.

title: Cathexis
line: That would be lovely. Thank you.

title: Cathexis
line: Tea is usually served at five thirty and dinner's at eight thirty. His lordship doesn't appreciate being kept waiting.

title: Cathexis
line: I'll be sure to be prompt.

title: Cathexis
line: Let's make something clear, Mrs Davenport. My job is to make sure that this household runs smoothly. I have been with Lord Burleigh for nearly twenty years because this household runs smoothly. He has come to trust me, and I will not brook any behavior that might jeopardize that trust, so you will be expected to follow the rules that I have set down.

title: Cathexis
line: Mrs Templeton, I have no wish to do anything that might disrupt this household but let me make something perfectly clear. I've been hired by Lord Burleigh, and it's his orders I will follow, not yours.

title: Cathexis
line: You would be wise not to make an enemy of me. I can make sure we have another governess by next week.

title: Cathexis
line: I suggest we try to get along, Mrs Templeton. Surely there's room here for both of us?

title: Cathexis
line: One lump or two?

title: Cathexis
line: Two, please.

title: Cathexis
line: Lord Burleigh will be here directly.

title: Cathexis
line: Forgive me. I've startled you.

title: Cathexis
line: I'm sorry. I didn't here you come in.

title: Cathexis
line: Mrs Davenport, I'll come to the point. I am not an easy man to live with. Since my wife died I'm told I'm even worse. She was a buffer for me.

title: Cathexis
line: I understand.

title: Cathexis
line: The children are the ones who've suffered. I've not been much of a father to them, and God knows I can't be a mother. I'm not asking that you replace their mother, but I think that they'll respond to a woman's sensibilities. You might fill a void in their lives.

title: Cathexis
line: I'll certainly try, your Grace.

title: Cathexis
line: Young Henry is sometimes a bit stubborn and little Beatrice misses her mother terribly. I hope they won't make things difficult for you. One thing above all I must demand. You are never, under any circumstances, to go onto the fourth floor. Is that clear?

title: Cathexis
line: Bridge to Captain Janeway.

title: Cathexis
line: Go ahead, Mister Kim.

title: Cathexis
line: I've got Commander Chakotay and

title: Cathexis
line: Mister Tuvok's shuttlecraft on long range sensors, but they're not responding to our hails. The shuttle's been badly damaged. I'm reading multiple hull fractures.

title: Cathexis
line: Life signs?

title: Cathexis
line: Two, but they're very faint.

title: Cathexis
line: Beam them to Sickbay as soon as they're in range. I'm on my way.

title: Cathexis
line: Aye, Captain.

title: Cathexis
line: Doctor.

title: Cathexis
line: They've each taken a blast to the head by some kind of energy discharge. Cardiostimulator. Mister Tuvok has a serious concussion, but it's nothing I can't handle. As for Commander Chakotay, all of the bioneural energy has been extracted from his brain.

title: Cathexis
line: Extracted?

title: Cathexis
line: Yes. From the looks of it, someone drained the energy from every single axon and dendrite right down to the synapses. I can keep his heart beating and I can keep him breathing, but other than that there's nothing I can do. He's brain dead.

title: Cathexis
line: The attack lasted no more than a few seconds, but it was highly effective. I feel Commander Chakotay and I are fortunate to be alive.

title: Cathexis
line: What happened, Lieutenant?

title: Cathexis
line: We had completed our trade mission with the Ilidarians and were on course to the rendezvous point when we encountered a dark matter nebula. As we began a routine analysis, an unidentified ship emerged and attacked our shuttle.

title: Cathexis
line: Any idea why?

title: Cathexis
line: No. They would not respond to our hails. We were hit by an energy discharge which penetrated our shields and filled the cabin. Commander Chakotay lost consciousness immediately, and I was barely able to activate the autopilot before I was overcome as well.

title: Cathexis
line: And the alien ship?

title: Cathexis
line: The last image I saw was the ship flying back into the nebula, but the details are difficult to remember.

title: Cathexis
line: Can you tell me anything about the energy discharge? Its modulation or phase distribution?

title: Cathexis
line: No. There was no time for a detailed analysis. However, the shuttle's sensors may have recorded information that could be helpful. I will download the sensor logs.

title: Cathexis
line: Why would someone want to extract his bioneural energy?

title: Cathexis
line: I don't know, but if I'm to have any hope of reviving him, I must know precisely how his neurons were depleted. It would be a great help if I could examine the weapon.

title: Cathexis
line: We're going back to that nebula to try to find the ship that attacked you. Janeway to Bridge. Prepare to lay in a new course. Mister Tuvok will provide you with the coordinates.

title: Cathexis
line: Aye, Captain.

title: Cathexis
line: We'll keep you posted, Doctor.

title: Cathexis
line: The energy discharge overloaded the shuttlecraft's central computer core. All sensor data have been erased.

title: Cathexis
line: Lieutenant Torres is in Sickbay now. When she reports, tell her to go over those damaged sensor logs with a fine tooth comb to see if she can reconstruct any of the data.

title: Cathexis
line: Aye, Captain.

title: Cathexis
line: Well, this is going to make things a little more difficult. I've been using the long range sensors to analyze the nebula you discovered. It's sending out strong electromagnetic radiation. We won't be able to scan inside it. You know, it sounds to me like a perfect hiding place.

title: Cathexis
line: I agree.

title: Cathexis
line: I don't like the idea of going in there blind. Let me see if I can reconfigure the sensors to a multiphasic bandwidth.

title: Cathexis
line: Is there a problem?

title: Cathexis
line: I've lost all sensor contact with the nebula. I don't understand. Wait a minute, we've altered course. Mister Paris?

title: Cathexis
line: Our new heading is one twenty one mark six. We've completely come about, Captain, but it wasn't me.

title: Cathexis
line: Mister Kim, check the navigational computer. Who ordered the course change?

title: Cathexis
line: According to my readings, the command was issued from the conn.

title: Cathexis
line: I'm telling you, it wasn't me, and the helm controls are working perfectly. No sign of a malfunction.

title: Cathexis
line: Ensign, transfer helm control to your station and reset our original course.

title: Cathexis
line: Course laid in.

title: Cathexis
line: Mister Paris, I want you to run a full diagnostic on the conn station. See if you can isolate the problem.

title: Cathexis
line: Aye, Captain.

title: Cathexis
line: You might have asked before adorning my Sickbay with animal remains.

title: Cathexis
line: It's a medicine wheel, a talisman used by Chakotay's tribe. He once showed me how it works. He said if anything ever happened to him, that I should perform a special healing ritual.

title: Cathexis
line: Ah.

title: Cathexis
line: The wheel represents both the universe outside and the universe inside our minds as well. They believe each is a reflection of the other. When a person is sleeping, or on a vision quest, it's said that his soul is walking the wheel. But if he's in a coma or near death, it means that he's gotten lost. These stones are signposts to help point the way back. Not exactly standard medical procedure, I know, but

title: Cathexis
line: You've placed the Coyote Stone at the crossroads of the fifth and sixth realms, which would divert Commander Chakotay's soul, that is his consciousness, into the Mountains of the Antelope Women. According to his tradition, an extremely attractive locale. He might not want to leave.

title: Cathexis
line: How do you know about the medicine wheel?

title: Cathexis
line: It's my business to know about a variety of medical treatments, including those based on psycho-spiritual beliefs. Unfortunately, in this case, the medicine wheel won't be much help. There's just not enough of his mind left to work with.

title: Cathexis
line: Find your way home, Commander.

title: Cathexis
line: Hello? Is someone here?

title: Cathexis
line: It's like sensing some kind of presence, as if someone else were here.

title: Cathexis
line: Your telepathic senses again. Is this like last week, when you went into Sickbay and you knew Lieutenant Hargrove had been there, only he'd left hours before?

title: Cathexis
line: It's not the same. That was like, like hearing faint music from a faraway place. When I was in my quarters just now

title: Cathexis
line: Mmm hmm?

title: Cathexis
line: It was almost tangible. I felt like there was someone in the room with me.

title: Cathexis
line: Who was it?

title: Cathexis
line: I don't know. A presence, that's all I can say.

title: Cathexis
line: Warp engines still within normal parameters, Captain.

title: Cathexis
line: We just changed course again. Mister Kim?

title: Cathexis
line: Our new heading is one twenty one mark six.

title: Cathexis
line: Get us back on course.

title: Cathexis
line: The helm's not responding. I'm locked out.

title: Cathexis
line: This command station has been blocked.

title: Cathexis
line: From where?

title: Cathexis
line: The lockout originated on deck twelve, section B seven, navigational control.

title: Cathexis
line: See if you can re-establish control.

title: Cathexis
line: I've checked every ODN junction in the helm control network, and I still can't find the problem.

title: Cathexis
line: It seems we've developed a new problem while you were gone.

title: Cathexis
line: Helm control re-established.

title: Cathexis
line: Get us back on course for the nebula. Janeway to Torres.

title: Cathexis
line: Torres here.

title: Cathexis
line: Who's in the navigational control?

title: Cathexis
line: No one right now. I was there this morning, and Lieutenant Paris was in there just a few minutes ago.

title: Cathexis
line: That's not true.

title: Cathexis
line: Are you certain about that, B'Elanna?

title: Cathexis
line: Positive. I just saw him leave about five minutes ago.

title: Cathexis
line: Janeway out. Explanation, Mister Paris?

title: Cathexis
line: I passed by the navigational control on my way back from the Jefferies tube, but that's all. Am I being accused of something here?

title: Cathexis
line: We are merely following a line of deductive reasoning, Lieutenant. Both deviations from our course were apparently issued from locations where you were working.

title: Cathexis
line: I'm telling you, I didn't do it.

title: Cathexis
line: Well, I'm willing to rule out mutiny for time being. I believe you, Mister Paris, but we have to consider the possibility that you might be having a problem with your memory. I want you to go down to Sickbay. Have the doctor check you out.

title: Cathexis
line: All right.

title: Cathexis
line: Lieutenant Durst.

title: Cathexis
line: Neurotransmitters at normal. Synaptic functions stable. Hold still. This is an extremely sensitive scan.

title: Cathexis
line: What I wouldn't give to see good old Doc Brown right now.

title: Cathexis
line: What?

title: Cathexis
line: Doc Brown. Lollipops in the waiting room, no holocomic books more than six months old, house calls. I caught a bad cold one time when I was nine years old. The doctor whipped up a pot of garlic soup and brought it over himself.

title: Cathexis
line: Your report, Doctor?

title: Cathexis
line: I still have a series of tests to perform, but other than his irritating lapses into nostalgia, I see nothing wrong with him.

title: Cathexis
line: I guess you're going to have to round up another suspect, Tuvok.

title: Cathexis
line: On the contrary, Lieutenant. I ran a forensic sweep of the navigational control. I found traces of your DNA on the console.

title: Cathexis
line: That's impossible.

title: Cathexis
line: The cellular residue you left behind is less than twelve hours old. Do you still wish to maintain your innocence?

title: Cathexis
line: To be honest, I don't know what to think.

title: Cathexis
line: Perhaps my biomolecular scan will reveal something.

title: Cathexis
line: Keep me informed, Doctor.

title: Cathexis
line: I believe I have found the ion trail of the ship that attacked us. It leads directly into the dark matter nebula. This is the nebula, and this is the ion trail. As you can see, their flight path is highly erratic.

title: Cathexis
line: These planetoids inside the nebula, they may be generating a dangerous gravitational effect, like storm currents. Chances are they've mapped those currents and they're taking the only safe way through.

title: Cathexis
line: A reasonable assumption. I recommend we follow their exact flight path.

title: Cathexis
line: Agreed. Lay in a course to the

title: Cathexis
line: Captain, we're dropping to impulse power. I'm reading a massive energy drain all over the ship, and the warp core is shutting down.

title: Cathexis
line: Bridge to Engineering. Report. Lieutenant Torres, please respond. Mister Kim, take the Bridge. Tuvok, you're with me.

title: Cathexis
line: Torres, what's going on?

title: Cathexis
line: Captain?

title: Cathexis
line: You've initiated an emergency warp core shutdown.

title: Cathexis
line: What?

title: Cathexis
line: Too late. The warp core is offline. It'll take at least two hours to regenerate the dilithium matrix. Ensign, get the rest of the systems back online. Apparently, you've just crashed the main computer, locked out the Bridge and stopped this ship cold. Do you want to tell me why?

title: Cathexis
line: Captain, I don't know what you're talking about.

title: Cathexis
line: What the hell is going on here?

title: Cathexis
line: I found something, and you're not going to like it. This is Mister Paris' memory engram for the last twenty four hours. As you can see, it has a very consistent and distinctive modulation, except at thirteen fifty hours. For one minute forty seven seconds, a different memory pattern appeared. Thirteen fifty hours is also the exact moment when Mister Paris presumably tampered with navigational control. It gets worse. In addition to that, there is another disruption at twelve oh two hours, the moment when he allegedly entered the new course at the helm. I also found there's an identical disruption in Lieutenant Torres's pattern at the moment she shut down warp power. I should point out that this is a neuroelectrical signature, what I believe to be another brain wave that was superimposed on their own.

title: Cathexis
line: Another brain wave? Whose?

title: Cathexis
line: I don't know. It has an unusual energy signature, one I've never seen before.

title: Cathexis
line: Doctor, what are you saying?

title: Cathexis
line: One possible explanation, and the only one I can think of at the moment, is that an unknown alien entity momentarily took control of their minds.

title: Cathexis
line: Intruder alert. All security personnel, go to Condition Four. Captain, it is possible the intruder returned with us in the shuttlecraft.

title: Cathexis
line: If we're right and there is an alien here, it seems intent on preventing us from going back to the nebula. What's more, it seems to have the ability to jump from person to person. If that's true, it could be in any one of us, controlling our actions without us realizing it.

title: Cathexis
line: Well, except for me.

title: Cathexis
line: That's true. So far it's only affected organic beings. If it could control the computer and navigational systems directly, it probably would've done it already.

title: Cathexis
line: Which means the doctor is the only person on board we can trust at this moment. Doctor, until we have eliminated this alien presence, I can't take the risk that it could take over any of the senior officers. I'd like to transfer all command codes to you until further notice.

title: Cathexis
line: What would that mean? That I am in command?

title: Cathexis
line: No, but you will act as a failsafe. If you feel at any time that any one of us are under the influence of the alien, you can countermand our orders and take control of the ship. Do you feel up to it?

title: Cathexis
line: Well, of course. I make life and death decisions every day.

title: Cathexis
line: I feel better already.

title: Cathexis
line: Computer, transfer all command codes to the holographic doctor. Authorisation Janeway eight four one alpha six five.

title: Cathexis
line: Command code transfer complete.

title: Cathexis
line: Let's see if we can get the warp core back online ahead of schedule.

title: Cathexis
line: Aye, Captain.

title: Cathexis
line: Captain, I heard what's happened. I think you're right. There is an alien presence here, I've been sensing something unusual all day. I don't know how to describe it, but I know there's something here.

title: Cathexis
line: Do you know where?

title: Cathexis
line: No, just that it's on the ship.

title: Cathexis
line: Captain, Kes's telepathic abilities are undisciplined. If I could initiate a Vulcan mind-meld with her, I may be able to help her focus those abilities to detect the alien more accurately.

title: Cathexis
line: I'm willing to do that.

title: Cathexis
line: Very well. Proceed, Mister Tuvok.

title: Cathexis
line: The captain wants to seal off all critical areas of the ship. Make sure the access hatch of Jefferies tube A-seventeen is secured.

title: Cathexis
line: So what exactly are we securing against?

title: Cathexis
line: We're not sure yet, but we think it's some kind of noncorporeal alien.

title: Cathexis
line: Noncorporeal? That means it can probably move through a bulk

title: Cathexis
line: Medical emergency. Deck seven, section thirteen alpha.

title: Cathexis
line: Captain's log, supplemental. It appears that Mister Tuvok and Kes were both hit by an unidentified energy discharge. Tuvok was not badly hurt, but Kes is in a coma.

title: Cathexis
line: It was similar to the attack on the shuttlecraft. An energy discharge came through the bulkhead, filled the turbolift and hit both of us.

title: Cathexis
line: We didn't pick up a discharge of any kind on the internal sensors.

title: Cathexis
line: Perhaps this type of energy is beyond our sensor bandwidth.

title: Cathexis
line: Perhaps, but that discharge had to come from somewhere.

title: Cathexis
line: The most thorough scanning device we have on board is a magneton scanner. We could search the ship centimeter by centimeter, but that wouldn't do much good. This alien could be anywhere at any time.

title: Cathexis
line: But what if we could perform a magneton scan on the entire ship all at once?

title: Cathexis
line: What do you suggest?

title: Cathexis
line: A magneton flash scan. We could reconfigure every sensor array on the ship to emit a single burst. It might be enough to illuminate any anomalous energy. Harry, what do you think?

title: Cathexis
line: Whoa. What did I do?

title: Cathexis
line: Stay where you are, Mister Kim.

title: Cathexis
line: I don't see anything unusual, but that doesn't mean anything.

title: Cathexis
line: Mister Kim, what were you doing just now?

title: Cathexis
line: I was just thinking. I was remembering an old study I saw about magneton scanners. I guess my mind started to wander a bit.

title: Cathexis
line: I'm very disturbed by what just happened here. We don't have any idea what occurs when someone is occupied by this alien presence. If we start pointing a finger every time someone gets distracted, it won't be long before outright paranoia starts sweeping the ship. Tuvok, B'Elanna, I want you to get started on that magneton flash scan. It's worth a try. Dismissed.

title: Cathexis
line: And that's not all. Ensign Parsons ordered his pejuta cold.

title: Cathexis
line: So?

title: Cathexis
line: He always drinks it hot. Hot! With lemon. But not today. Today it's cold pejuta, hold the lemon.

title: Cathexis
line: Mister Neelix, just because a man changes his drink order doesn't mean he's possessed by an alien.

title: Cathexis
line: Nevertheless, don't you think you should scan him or dissect him or something, just to make sure?

title: Cathexis
line: I could examine every crew member you've mentioned so far, every person on board, for that matter and it wouldn't do any good. From what we can tell, the alien can jump from person to person at will.

title: Cathexis
line: It sounds to me like you're defending Ensign Parsons.

title: Cathexis
line: I'm not defending him, I'm just pointing out that you're acting a little paranoid. In fact, one could say you're acting a little too paranoid.

title: Cathexis
line: Are you suggesting that I, that I could possibly? Doctor, I can assure you, not even an alien intruder could make me do anything to hurt Kes.

title: Cathexis
line: All I'm suggesting, Mister Neelix, is that paranoia is only going to aggravate your already precarious emotional condition. Try to relax. I don't think Kes has suffered any permanent neurological damage. I'll let you know the moment I've had any success in reviving her.

title: Cathexis
line: I'll be back as soon as you wake, dearest. And don't worry, you're in good hands. Thank you, Doctor.

title: Cathexis
line: What are you doing?

title: Cathexis
line: I am reconfiguring the sensor relays on the ship. This will only take a minute.

title: Cathexis
line: Must you do it now? I'm in the middle of a treatment.

title: Cathexis
line: I am sorry, Doctor. Captain's orders. How is she?

title: Cathexis
line: No irreparable damage. In fact, her injuries are quite different from Commander Chakotay's. Her bioneural energy is completely intact, and I'm curious about these contusions on her neck and shoulder. They're not consistent with an energy discharge. They look more like wounds sustained during a physical struggle.

title: Cathexis
line: Odd. There was no physical struggle that I can recall.

title: Cathexis
line: I just don't understand it. The only thing these injuries come close to resembling is an extreme trauma to the trapezius nerve bundle. It's as though her nerve fibers have been ruptured.

title: Cathexis
line: Come in.

title: Cathexis
line: Lieutenant Torres and I will be ready to initiate the magneton scan in approximately two hours. You should be aware that it will be a high-intensity burst. It will cause dizziness and disorientation in all crew members, including myself, for several seconds.

title: Cathexis
line: Make a ship-wide announcement before you initiate the scan.

title: Cathexis
line: Aye, Captain. There is another matter of some concern. It appears that Kes's injuries were not caused by an energy discharge. The doctor has found evidence that she was physically assaulted.

title: Cathexis
line: Assaulted? But you weren't physically assaulted.

title: Cathexis
line: That is correct.

title: Cathexis
line: Is it possible that you inflicted her wounds?

title: Cathexis
line: Me?

title: Cathexis
line: Maybe you were inhabited by the alien at that moment.

title: Cathexis
line: It is possible. Perhaps we should have the doctor run a neurological scan to see if I show a memory disruption.

title: Cathexis
line: Agreed. Janeway to Sickbay. Computer, activate Emergency Medical Holographic System.

title: Cathexis
line: Unable to comply. The EMH program has been disabled.

title: Cathexis
line: Disabled? By whom?

title: Cathexis
line: Unknown.

title: Cathexis
line: The Doctor's initialisation routine has been locked out. It's encrypted. I can't reactivate the program.

title: Cathexis
line: It appears the lockout originated somewhere above deck four.

title: Cathexis
line: Why would someone deactivate the Doctor?

title: Cathexis
line: The Doctor does hold the command codes to Voyager.

title: Cathexis
line: Yes, but once he was deactivated the codes automatically reverted back to me.

title: Cathexis
line: If we assume the alien could not take over the holographic doctor, then logically it would try to force the command codes back into a humanoid host.

title: Cathexis
line: Me. It's too dangerous for one person to retain the command codes at this point. I suggest we divide my command protocols into two code groupings.

title: Cathexis
line: A sensible precaution.

title: Cathexis
line: You would be the reasonable choice to hold the second grouping, if there's any such thing as a reasonable choice right now. The alien could occupy either one of us at any time.

title: Cathexis
line: But presumably not both of us at the same time.

title: Cathexis
line: I'll tell the bridge crew the plan. We'll all have to act as checks and balances for each other.

title: Cathexis
line: I want you all to be aware of something that has happened, something I must assume was due to the alien. The Doctor has been deactivated, and we can't get him back online. I have decided to divide my command protocols.

title: Cathexis
line: Captain?

title: Cathexis
line: Stun her! She's the alien!

title: Cathexis
line: That should do it, Captain.

title: Cathexis
line: Thank you, Mister Paris. I feel better already. Any luck getting the Doctor back online?

title: Cathexis
line: Not yet. Whoever did this put up one hell of a roadblock. I'm going to have to break through at least six levels of encryption to access the holo-emitters.

title: Cathexis
line: How long is it going to take?

title: Cathexis
line: Two, maybe three hours.

title: Cathexis
line: Torres to Janeway.

title: Cathexis
line: Go ahead.

title: Cathexis
line: Captain, can you come down to Engineering? There's something here I think you should see.

title: Cathexis
line: I'm on my way. Mister Paris, you're our temporary medic until the Doctor returns.

title: Cathexis
line: Right.

title: Cathexis
line: Ensign, I need you on the Bridge.

title: Cathexis
line: I've been trying to reconstruct the damaged sensor logs from Tuvok and Chakotay's shuttlecraft. I didn't have any luck until I ran a parity trace scan. Captain, the sensor logs weren't destroyed by an energy discharge. Someone erased them, and then overloaded the sensor matrix to make it look like they'd been damaged. It gets worse. There was enough information left in the backup logs for me to reconstruct what happened during the attack. They were near a dark matter nebula and an energy discharge did breach the hull, but there was no other ship.

title: Cathexis
line: No ship?

title: Cathexis
line: I'm certain of it. From what I can tell, the energy discharge came from the nebula itself.

title: Cathexis
line: Why would Tuvok lie about an attack?

title: Cathexis
line: He must have been under the alien's influence.

title: Cathexis
line: Bridge to Janeway. We're approaching the dark matter nebula.

title: Cathexis
line: Acknowledged. How long until the magneton flash scan is ready to go?

title: Cathexis
line: The sensor arrays are charging now. Fifteen, maybe twenty minutes.

title: Cathexis
line: When it's ready, transfer control of the scan to the Bridge. In the meantime, I think we should take a look at exactly what it is we're not supposed to see.

title: Cathexis
line: Mister Tuvok, can you locate the ion trail of the alien ship that attacked you?

title: Cathexis
line: I believe so. Mister Kim, lay in that course. Shields are at maximum, Captain. All preparations for entering the nebula are complete.

title: Cathexis
line: Captain, I've finished the bioanalysis the doctor was running on Kes before he was deactivated. I think he was on to something. If I'm interpreting his data correctly, the bruises on Kes's neck and shoulders were the result of a Vulcan neck pinch.

title: Cathexis
line: Lieutenant?

title: Cathexis
line: I have no memory of injuring Kes. Perhaps I was occupied by the alien at that time.

title: Cathexis
line: Perhaps so, but then, why does it keep attacking you? In three separate instances now, it's assaulted you.

title: Cathexis
line: I am the Chief of Security. It may see me as a particular threat.

title: Cathexis
line: So far, you've posed no greater threat than anyone else, and yet it keeps going after you.

title: Cathexis
line: Captain, I believe you are having a typically human response to circumstances which are frightening and inexplicable, commonly known as paranoia.

title: Cathexis
line: Maybe, but I don't think it's paranoia that's keeping me from picking up this ion trail of yours. What bandwidth are you on?

title: Cathexis
line: I'm using a multiphasic scan. If you examine the alpha K band, you will see it.

title: Cathexis
line: Yes, here it is. A very interesting ion trail. There's no sign of any subspace distortions in its wake. According to these readings, it's a ship without engines. You're lying, Tuvok. There is no alien ship, and there never was. We're not going inside that nebula until we get some answers. Mister Kim, reverse course and

title: Cathexis
line: Belay that order. That is exactly what the alien has been trying to do, keep us from entering the nebula. I suspect the captain has been occupied. I am relieving her of command. Ensign, proceed into the nebula, one half impulse.

title: Cathexis
line: Don't do it, Harry.

title: Cathexis
line: Now, Ensign.

title: Cathexis
line: No sir, I won't do it.

title: Cathexis
line: I must inform you this phaser is on wide beam dispersal and set to kill. I am taking command of this Bridge. I must ask you all to stand together where I can see you. Step away from the console, Ensign.

title: Cathexis
line: Captain, we're entering the nebula.

title: Cathexis
line: Captain, I'm picking up some kind of energy pulses in the nebula, highly coherent, with a biomatrix.

title: Cathexis
line: Life forms.

title: Cathexis
line: And they're heading this way.

title: Cathexis
line: Those beings out there, are they your people?

title: Cathexis
line: We are the Komar. This is our domain.

title: Cathexis
line: What's happening?

title: Cathexis
line: The warp core's been ejected.

title: Cathexis
line: No. No! We must continue.

title: Cathexis
line: Torres to Bridge. Captain

title: Cathexis
line: I think I was just taken over by the alien. One second I was working the plasma relays and the next thing I knew, I was ejecting

title: Cathexis
line: The warp core.

title: Cathexis
line: Acknowledged, Lieutenant. Stand by.

title: Cathexis
line: I don't get it. If the alien's in Tuvok, how could it be down in Engineering at the same time?

title: Cathexis
line: I don't know. Unless there are two aliens.

title: Cathexis
line: Two?

title: Cathexis
line: Wait a minute. Lieutenant Torres isn't authorized to eject the warp core on her own. That requires a command code authorisation. Computer, who authorized the ejection of the warp core?

title: Cathexis
line: The authorisation was entered by Commander Chakotay.

title: Cathexis
line: Chakotay.

title: Cathexis
line: How is that possible?

title: Cathexis
line: The alien in Tuvok wants us in that nebula, but there's another presence that's been trying to keep us out. It doesn't make sense, unless it's Chakotay and he knows we'll be in danger if we go in there.

title: Cathexis
line: But he's in Sickbay. He's brain dead.

title: Cathexis
line: Maybe not. Maybe his neural energy was displaced somehow and he's able to move from person to person.

title: Cathexis
line: Tuvok's engaged emergency thrusters. We're moving again, Captain.

title: Cathexis
line: You brought us here, for what? To extract our neural energy?

title: Cathexis
line: Very perceptive, Captain. The collective neural energy of your crew will sustain my people for years to come.

title: Cathexis
line: You don't have to do this. Maybe we can help you find another source of energy.

title: Cathexis
line: Captain, we're under attack. We're being bombarded by the energy beings.

title: Cathexis
line: The magneton scan identified the entity before it left the ship. It was a trianic-based energy being.

title: Cathexis
line: Looks like he's joined his friends outside.

title: Cathexis
line: Shields are holding, but they won't last long at this rate, and the electromagnetic radiation is blinding our sensors. I can't find a way out.

title: Cathexis
line: Come about. Maybe if we reverse course, we can just backtrack.

title: Cathexis
line: Yes, ma'am.

title: Cathexis
line: I don't know if that'll work, Captain. Tuvok was navigating a complicated course. We could be going deeper into the nebula.

title: Cathexis
line: Mister Kim, maybe you can reconstruct Tuvok's navigational logs.

title: Cathexis
line: I'm on it, Captain.

title: Cathexis
line: Shields down to sixty five percent, Captain! The energy beings are starting to penetrate our defenses.

title: Cathexis
line: I'm not having any luck. Tuvok deleted the navigational logs as he went along. He wanted to make sure we didn't get out of here.

title: Cathexis
line: Neelix to Bridge.

title: Cathexis
line: Go ahead.

title: Cathexis
line: Captain, I can't be sure but

title: Cathexis
line: I think I was just taken over by the alien.

title: Cathexis
line: And I've done something very strange. I've rearranged the stones on the medicine wheel.

title: Cathexis
line: If it's Chakotay, maybe he's trying to tell us something. Mister Kim, activate Sickbay visual relay sixteen and put it on the view screen.

title: Cathexis
line: Aye, Captain.

title: Cathexis
line: What is it? What does it mean? Is it a code, a message?

title: Cathexis
line: Or a map.

title: Cathexis
line: Computer, overlay a star map of the nebula on the current viewscreen image.

title: Cathexis
line: The stones are in the same position as those three planetoids. Chakotay must be using them to point a way out.

title: Cathexis
line: Mister Kim, lay in a course that takes us along a line connecting those three planetoids. Engage.

title: Cathexis
line: Shields failing. The aliens are penetrating the hull.

title: Cathexis
line: Mister Kim, report.

title: Cathexis
line: We're passing the third planetoid now, Captain. The dark matter density is thinning. Reading normal space ahead.

title: Cathexis
line: Bridge to Torres. Transfer all remaining power to the thrusters, including life support.

title: Cathexis
line: We've cleared the nebula, Captain. Main power coming back online. Shields at full strength, hull integrity normal. The alien beings are not pursuing.

title: Cathexis
line: Captain's log, stardate 48735.9. We have returned to the co-ordinates where we ejected the warp core and have successfully retrieved it. Now we're hoping the Doctor will be able to successfully reintegrate Commander Chakotay's consciousness.

title: Cathexis
line: Did it work?

title: Cathexis
line: It appears so. Commander. Can you hear me?

title: Cathexis
line: Yes. I'm a little dizzy, but I think I'm all here.

title: Cathexis
line: How did you manage to reintegrate his consciousness?

title: Cathexis
line: It involved three neural transceivers, two cortical stimulators and fifty gigaquads of computer memory. I would be happy to take you through the process, but it would take at least ten hours to explain it all to you. Needless to say, it was a remarkable procedure. I would consider writing a paper about it if there were a convenient forum in which to publish it.

title: Cathexis
line: What happened, Commander?

title: Cathexis
line: After the attack on the shuttle, I had the sensation of floating above my own body. I thought I was dead.

title: Cathexis
line: And when the shuttle returned to Voyager you were still disembodied?

title: Cathexis
line: Yes. I couldn't speak, I couldn't touch anything. But then I found if I concentrated on someone who was in the room with me, I could share their consciousness. At first I could only do little things with the host's body. Push buttons, work a console. As time went on, it became easier to do more. I'm sorry I had to knock you around, Tuvok.

title: Cathexis
line: No apology is necessary.

title: Cathexis
line: Good job, Commander, and welcome back.

title: Cathexis
line: To be honest, I feel like I never left.

title: Faces
line: Regeneration phase completed. Deactivate the genitron. Shut down the biomatrix. B'Elanna? B'Elanna Torres, wake up.

title: Faces
line: Captain's log, stardate 48784.2. We have completed our survey of the Avery system and are returning to retrieve Lieutenants Paris, Torres and Durst. By now, they should have concluded their inspection of the magnesite formations on the third planet.

title: Faces
line: Here we are Mister Tuvok, one bowl of authentic Vulcan plomeek soup.

title: Faces
line: As I have told you, Mister Neelix, this is an unnecessary indulgence. I am quite content to eat whatever the rest of the crew is eating.

title: Faces
line: Nonsense. Everyone aboard this ship deserves a little taste of home every now and then.

title: Faces
line: Very well then, thank you.

title: Faces
line: Don't thank me, I'm having a marvelous time experimenting with the native dishes of the entire crew. So far I've learned to make corn salad for Mister Chakotay, and peanut butter and jelly sandwiches for Mister Paris. He calls it comfort food. Isn't that charming? What are you waiting for, it's no good cold.

title: Faces
line: Well?

title: Faces
line: It is rather piquant.

title: Faces
line: It is zesty, isn't it. I tried following the recipe in the computer's databank but it seemed so bland, so I took the liberty of spicing it up a bit. Call it plomeek soup a la Neelix.

title: Faces
line: I must point out that if you take the liberty of changing a time-honored recipe you are hardly presenting a taste of home.

title: Faces
line: Senior officers please report to the bridge.

title: Faces
line: But your soup?

title: Faces
line: Please, enjoy it.

title: Faces
line: Ah, there's no place like home.

title: Faces
line: The away team hasn't arrived at the pre-arranged coordinates, Captain, and they've failed to respond to our hails.

title: Faces
line: Have you tried locking on to their comm. signals?

title: Faces
line: We scanned the entire surface. No sign of them. They must still be underground, but I can't locate them there either.

title: Faces
line: Then as we suspected, the dense magnesite formations in the planet's crust are blocking our sensors.

title: Faces
line: Take a look at this. This is the cave system nearest the beam-in coordinates as it appeared in our initial geological scan. And this is the same system now. This tunnel here has shifted to the west by almost seventy five degrees.

title: Faces
line: Are you saying walls of solid rock have changed shape in the two days since the away team was deployed?

title: Faces
line: Apparently so, Captain, but our initial scans didn't indicate tectonic activity of anywhere near that magnitude.

title: Faces
line: In any case, it's possible that Torres and the others haven't returned to the beam-out site because they were trapped by these geological shifts. I'd like to lead a team down to investigate, Captain.

title: Faces
line: And what is to prevent us from losing you as well, Commander?

title: Faces
line: Breadcrumbs.

title: Faces
line: Ensign?

title: Faces
line: I'm sorry, Captain. What I mean to say is I think I can modify some subspace transponders which could be deployed along the Commander's path, kind of like

title: Faces
line: Breadcrumbs. Got it.

title: Faces
line: If they're placed at regular intervals I believe they'll maintain a signal link with the ship and they could serve as a transporter relay in case we need to stage an emergency beam-out.

title: Faces
line: Very well, Commander, take a team with you, but I want a transporter lock on you at all times.

title: Faces
line: Aye Captain. Tuvok, Kim, you're with me.

title: Faces
line: I apologize for the restraints, but your presence here is very important to us. Do you understand?

title: Faces
line: Who are you?

title: Faces
line: I am Sulan, chief surgeon of the Vidiian Sodality.

title: Faces
line: I demand to know what is happening here.

title: Faces
line: You've surgically altered my face. I look like a Klingon.

title: Faces
line: I've performed no surgery as you understand the term. There are several questions I need to ask you before we proceed.

title: Faces
line: You can't possibly believe I'm going to cooperate with you.

title: Faces
line: Perhaps I was in error to leave your consciousness and memory intact.

title: Faces
line: Durst. Paris. What have you done with them?

title: Faces
line: What is your exact age, Klingon.

title: Faces
line: If you want me to answer your question, you will have to answer one of mine first.

title: Faces
line: Very well.

title: Faces
line: What exactly have you done to me.

title: Faces
line: I have reconstituted your genome. You are now purely Klingon.

title: Faces
line: That's not possible.

title: Faces
line: I assure you it is. I have developed a procedure to stimulate cell division. A kind of enhanced mitosis. Your Klingon genetic material was extracted. It was then converted from matter to energy by our genetron. Finally you were rematerialized as the purified Klingon specimen that you are now.

title: Faces
line: Why? Why have you done this?

title: Faces
line: For generations my people have been searching the quadrant for a species immune to our disease in the hope that it would lead us to a cure.

title: Faces
line: And you think Klingons are immune to this phage?

title: Faces
line: I believe your genetic structure has phage-resistant nucleotide sequences, yes. But I needed a pure specimen to be certain. My people do not know it yet, but you are their greatest hope.

title: Faces
line: I will never help you.

title: Faces
line: You are very strong. I can only hope that you will be truly resistant to the phage.

title: Faces
line: And how will you know that?

title: Faces
line: I have infected you.

title: Faces
line: They're the ones with the guns, remember?

title: Faces
line: We've got to find a way out of this place.

title: Faces
line: Agreed. But I don't want to do anything until we find out what they've done with B'Elanna. In the meantime, we have to keep track of the guards movements. How long are their shifts, when do they eat, when do they sleep?

title: Faces
line: There don't seem to be many of them. I guess they figure we're all so exhausted we don't have any fight left.

title: Faces
line: We'll find an opening, Pete, and when the time is right we'll make our move.

title: Faces
line: Something funny, friend?

title: Faces
line: You.

title: Faces
line: Really. How's that?

title: Faces
line: Nobody ever escapes from this place. Those Vidiian leeches can yank the beating heart out of you in a heartbeat. Heart out of you in a heartbeat. Now that's funny.

title: Faces
line: Hilarious.

title: Faces
line: Seems like you know this place pretty well.

title: Faces
line: I should, I've been here six years.

title: Faces
line: Then tell me something. I thought those Vidiians were in the business of harvesting organs. How come we're all still in one piece?

title: Faces
line: The disease makes them weak. They need somebody to dig their tunnels. That's us. Best way to keep alive around here is to stay strong.

title: Faces
line: Thanks for the advice.

title: Faces
line: Don't worry, they're always in need of replacement body parts. They'll get around to gutting you eventually. There were twenty three of us from my ship. I'm the only one left.

title: Faces
line: Listen. When they grabbed us there was a woman with us. B'Elanna Torres. Any idea what might have happened to her?

title: Faces
line: If she's not here, she's been taken to organ processing.

title: Faces
line: I've deployed the transponders, Commander. The relay signal is coming through clearly.

title: Faces
line: Good work.

title: Faces
line: Any sign of them?

title: Faces
line: According to my tricorder readings they definitely came this way. The question is, where did they go from here?

title: Faces
line: Delightful spot to get lost.

title: Faces
line: Commander, Ensign. Over here.

title: Faces
line: What is it.

title: Faces
line: I detect traces of at least five humanoid lifeforms.

title: Faces
line: Five? There were only three in the away team.

title: Faces
line: Evidently they did not enter this cavern alone.

title: Faces
line: Are you in pain?

title: Faces
line: It's nothing.

title: Faces
line: Remarkable. One of the symptoms of the early stages of the phage is excruciating joint pain. I find it extraordinary that you can endure it. Some who have been infected have been known to die from the agony itself.

title: Faces
line: It's going to take more than an infection to kill me.

title: Faces
line: It appears you are correct. Your body's successfully fighting off the phage. I am overjoyed.

title: Faces
line: How delightful for you.

title: Faces
line: Soon we will begin a series of procedures replicating your genetic code and attempting various methods of integrating your DNA with our own. In time we'll be successful and eliminate the phage forever. When that time comes you will be honored as a hero by my people.

title: Faces
line: I know I'm the first Klingon you've ever seen, so I'll tell you that Klingons find honor as warriors on the battlefield, not as guinea pigs in a laboratory.

title: Faces
line: Earlier you accused me of mutilating you. Now you sound positively proud to be Klingon. You have me to thank for that, B'Elanna.

title: Faces
line: You'll get no gratitude from me.

title: Faces
line: Perhaps you'll feel different in time, but I don't blame you for your obstinacy. I would be proud too, with a form as handsome as yours. I believe Klingons are the most impressive species I have ever seen.

title: Faces
line: Tom? Tom, wake up.

title: Faces
line: B'Elanna?

title: Faces
line: Yeah, it's me.

title: Faces
line: B'Elanna, what have they done to you?

title: Faces
line: I remember them grabbing us outside the caves and then I, I guess I just blacked out.

title: Faces
line: Yes, they stunned all of us.

title: Faces
line: The next thing I knew, they were waking me up in some kind of laboratory. I was so groggy I couldn't see. I asked them what they had done to me and then one of them said that they had completely extracted my Klingon DNA.

title: Faces
line: It doesn't seem possible, but you look human.

title: Faces
line: I feel so weak, sick to my stomach.

title: Faces
line: Considering what they've done to you, I'm not surprised.

title: Faces
line: So strange.

title: Faces
line: What?

title: Faces
line: When I was a child, I did everything I could to hide my forehead. Hats, scarves, you name it.

title: Faces
line: When I was a kid, I wore a cap to cover the haircuts my father used to make me get first day of every summer.

title: Faces
line: I grew up on a colony on Kessik Four. My mother and I were the only Klingons there, and that was a time when relations between the Homeworld and the Federation weren't too cordial. Nobody ever said anything, but we were different and I didn't like that feeling. Then my father left when I was five years old. One day he was there and the next he wasn't. I cried myself to sleep every night for months. Of course I never told anybody. And then I finally decided that he'd left because I look like a Klingon. And so I tried to look human.

title: Faces
line: Looks like you finally got what you wanted.

title: Faces
line: Strange.

title: Faces
line: What is?

title: Faces
line: According to our last geological scan this cave should continue straight ahead for another eight kilometers.

title: Faces
line: This is solid granite, more than fifty meters.

title: Faces
line: If these caves were changing configuration while we were here, we certainly would have felt it.

title: Faces
line: True, Commander, but I do not believe there has been any tectonic activity. I believe this wall is merely an illusion, a disguised force field.

title: Faces
line: Away team to Voyager.

title: Faces
line: Go ahead Commander.

title: Faces
line: We've run into some type of force field, Captain.

title: Faces
line: One minute we were reading an empty tunnel, and the next we walked

title: Faces
line: Right into a solid wall of rock.

title: Faces
line: Captain, the energy configuration of the force field matrix is virtually identical to those used by the Vidiians.

title: Faces
line: Mister Ayala, scan for any alien vessels in the sector. Commander, we know from past experience that our phasers can disrupt that forcefield. I want to find out what's in there.

title: Faces
line: Aye, Captain.

title: Faces
line: But I don't want you taking any unnecessary risks. We'll be

title: Faces
line: Standing by to implement an emergency beam out.

title: Faces
line: Acknowledged.

title: Faces
line: It's not working, Captain.

title: Faces
line: Try reconfiguring your phaser to match the band width modulation.

title: Faces
line: Commander!

title: Faces
line: Three to beam up!

title: Faces
line: B'Elanna? How are you feeling today?

title: Faces
line: I feel strong. It's very frustrating to be restrained like this.

title: Faces
line: I sympathize.

title: Faces
line: I don't like being chained up like an animal.

title: Faces
line: I'm sorry, I wish there was some

title: Faces
line: I've been thinking about what you said. It's because of you that I am Klingon and I do like this feeling. In a strange way I suppose I am grateful. Did you know that Klingon females are renowned in the Alpha Quadrant not only for their physical prowess but for their voracious sexual appetites as well? Why not let your creation out of her harness. Study her in action.

title: Faces
line: I wish it were possible, B'Elanna, but I'm afraid I can't risk releasing you just yet.

title: Faces
line: Forgive me.

title: Faces
line: For what?

title: Faces
line: Please, don't condescend. I may have a grotesque appearance but I assure you my instincts are finely honed, and I do have feelings. Hard as it may be for you to imagine, B'Elanna, my people were once handsome and vigorous like yours, and with your help we will be again. Perhaps when that time comes I will not disgust you quite so much as I do now.

title: Faces
line: They're coming to take us to the work detail. You can't let them see how sick you are.

title: Faces
line: Maybe if they think I'm too weak they'll leave me behind. I could try to get my hands on that console over there.

title: Faces
line: Or maybe they'll skip the preliminaries and take you straight to organ processing.

title: Faces
line: You. Come with me.

title: Faces
line: What for?

title: Faces
line: You asked to contact your ship. The Prefect wishes to discuss your request.

title: Faces
line: I'm the senior officer here. If your superiors want to talk with one of us, it should be me. He's not going anywhere without me.

title: Faces
line: Tom, don't. They'll kill you.

title: Faces
line: Stop!

title: Faces
line: It's okay, Tom. They're the ones with the guns, remember?

title: Faces
line: What is it?

title: Faces
line: Now that the Vidiians know we're here, we have to be prepared for the possibility they'll call in reinforcements.

title: Faces
line: So far long range sensors haven't located any alien vessels near here.

title: Faces
line: However, it is possible that the same technology that disguises their forcefields, cloaks their ships.

title: Faces
line: The other thing we have to consider is that the prisoners may be at greater risk now.

title: Faces
line: Captain, take a look at this. Using our tricorder data I've been able to scan the entire planet for the forcefield signature, and it looks like the field surrounds an area more than six hundred kilometers in circumference.

title: Faces
line: Is there any way to scan inside it?

title: Faces
line: Every reconfiguration I've tried has failed.

title: Faces
line: If it's the same kind of forcefield that the Vidiians used the last time we ran into them, why didn't our phasers breach it?

title: Faces
line: Apparently it has been adapted to repulse phaser fire.

title: Faces
line: If the Vidiians can move in and out of there, so can we. Start setting up simulations. Find a way to get through that forcefield.

title: Faces
line: B'Elanna? I have something I want to show you.

title: Faces
line: Durst.

title: Faces
line: I thought perhaps this new face would make you more comfortable with me.

title: Faces
line: You've killed him.

title: Faces
line: Yes, B'Elanna, but his organs will save more than a dozen lives.

title: Faces
line: Deep level scans have revealed a network of microfissures, miniscule openings that develop each time the field matrix remodulates.

title: Faces
line: Just how small are these microfissures?

title: Faces
line: Less than one micron. And they close up within a few seconds.

title: Faces
line: Would it be possible to use our phasers to expand one of these openings as it's forming?

title: Faces
line: That was our first thought. But we realized such an attempt would have to be at close range and would carry the risk of alerting the Vidiians to our presence.

title: Faces

title: Faces
line: Of course, timing the transport to the precise moment of an opening would be critical.

title: Faces
line: But if we could get someone inside, we might be able to find our people, and also deactivate the forcefield.

title: Faces
line: And then, presumably, we could beam everyone back to the ship.

title: Faces
line: Precisely. But you should be aware that because we are incapable of scanning beyond the forcefield we will have no way of communicating with whoever transports inside it. Nor will we be able to verify that the transport has been successfully completed.

title: Faces
line: Moreover, what's to prevent whoever goes in from being captured by the Vidiians.

title: Faces
line: I have an idea about that, Captain.

title: Faces
line: Dermal stimulator, please.

title: Faces
line: Remarkable work, Doctor.

title: Faces
line: If you think this is remarkable, you should see me remove a bunion.

title: Faces
line: I have done my best to replicate Vidiian attire. I trust it will prove sufficiently convincing.

title: Faces
line: It's a fine piece of work, Mister Tuvok. Next time I need a tailor, I'll know just where to look.

title: Faces
line: Quickly, now. In there!

title: Faces
line: Here, B'Elanna. Sit down.

title: Faces
line: Here. It's water.

title: Faces
line: Thanks.

title: Faces
line: Rest while you can. The guard won't be back right away. Keep it.

title: Faces
line: Tom, I've been thinking. When they did this thing to me, I think it changed more than just the way I look.

title: Faces
line: What do you mean?

title: Faces
line: Back there, when they took Durst away, I was terrified.

title: Faces
line: No one could blame you for that.

title: Faces
line: You don't understand. I've been in worse situations but I've never felt like that before. Never. I mean, my heart was pounding and my hands were shaking. I didn't even try to help you.

title: Faces
line: B'Elanna, I'm no doctor, but I have to believe that what ever they did to you has seriously depleted your strength. There's nothing you could have done.

title: Faces
line: No, that's not it. I think that when they extracted my Klingon DNA, they turned me into some kind of a coward.

title: Faces
line: Sometimes fear can be a good thing. Keeps you from taking unnecessary chances. Courage doesn't mean that you don't have fear. It means that you've learnt to overcome it. And I know that you can find the courage to hold on until we can find a way out of this place.

title: Faces
line: What's going on here?

title: Faces
line: She's ill. She needed a rest.

title: Faces
line: If she's too weak, I'll take her back to the barracks.

title: Faces
line: That's okay, Tom. Maybe if I'm there I can try to make contact with the ship.

line: The emitter array has been initialized, Captain.

line: Initiating auto sequence.

title: Faces
line: On my mark, Mister Kim. Energize. Well, now we wait.

title: Faces
line: Make a sound and I'll break your neck, understand? I'm looking for my friend, Tom Paris, a human male. Have you seen him?

title: Faces
line: He was here, but they sent him to another tunnel.

title: Faces
line: Which one?

title: Faces
line: Back that way. There was another human with him, but they took her back to the barracks.

title: Faces

line: I need your help here.

title: Faces

title: Faces

title: Faces

title: Faces

title: Faces

title: Faces

title: Faces

title: Faces
line: If I hadn't come along, were you just going to waste away in that prison camp until they killed you for your body parts? Were you too frightened to act?

title: Faces
line: I was looking for a way to escape.

title: Faces
line: Looking! I'll show you the way to escape! This and this.

title: Faces
line: That's the way you respond every situation, isn't it? If it doesn't work, hit it. If it's in your way, knock it down. No wonder I got kicked out of the Academy.

title: Faces

title: Faces

title: Faces

title: Faces

title: Faces

title: Faces

title: Faces

title: Faces

title: Faces
line: So. You need me.

title: Faces
line: I can't get back to that computer without you. And you'll have to cover for me while I work.

title: Faces
line: We can't go to the prison barracks. There are too many guards there. In the lab where they were holding me, there was a security console. That's the last place they would expect us to be.

title: Faces

title: Faces
line: Tell me how to get there.

title: Faces
line: Keep your hands off me!

title: Faces
line: Whatever you say, Paris, but I thought you might like to get out of this place.

title: Faces

title: Faces

title: Faces

title: Faces

title: Faces

title: Faces
line: I've never seen you before.

title: Faces

title: Faces
line: Very well, take him. But from now on I expect to be notified in advance of all transfers.

title: Faces

title: Faces

title: Faces
line: I have to bypass the security code so I can access the force field grid. Then I'll have a better idea of what we're dealing with. That should do it. There! That's what we're up against, and I think we're here.

title: Faces
line: Can you shut it down?

title: Faces
line: I'm working on it.

title: Faces
line: What now?

title: Faces
line: If they didn't know we were here before, they do now. Take it easy. I'll be done in a minute.

title: Faces
line: You're not frightened any more, are you?

title: Faces
line: Maybe I just don't have time to think about it.

title: Faces
line: Are you hurt?

title: Faces
line: Keep working.

title: Faces
line: B'Elanna, stop.

title: Faces
line: You're not going to hurt me. You need me.

title: Faces
line: You're right. But if you do not surrender, I will kill her.

title: Faces
line: Drop it!

title: Faces
line: Who are you?

title: Faces
line: That's what I want to know.

title: Faces
line: It's Chakotay!

title: Faces
line: I think I've just about accessed the forcefield.

title: Faces
line: Hurry!

title: Faces
line: Got it! There!

title: Faces
line: Captain, the forcefield has been disrupted.

title: Faces
line: Mister Kim, can you get a lock on Commander Chakotay?

title: Faces
line: Chakotay to Voyager, do you read?

title: Faces
line: Loud and clear, Commander.

title: Faces
line: I've found them, Captain.

title: Faces
line: No!

title: Faces
line: No!

title: Faces
line: Three humans and one Klingon to beam up.

title: Faces
line: She's badly wounded, Captain.

title: Faces
line: Beam her to Sickbay!

title: Faces
line: Don't. No time. You showed true courage. It makes my death an honorable one.

title: Faces
line: Using tissue from your counterpart, I can replicate the Klingon DNA, then over the course of several days, I'll reintegrate that genetic material into your cellular structure.

title: Faces
line: Wait a minute. You're not saying that you're going to change me back?

title: Faces
line: That's precisely what I'm saying. Your cell's ability to synthesis proteins has been severely compromised. You need the Klingon genes to survive.

title: Faces
line: So she's saving my life again.

title: Faces
line: I'll get started on the DNA.

title: Faces
line: How are you doing?

title: Faces
line: I'm not sure. It's been a pretty strange experience. I do know that right now, the way I am, I'm more at peace with myself than I've ever been before. And that's a good feeling.

title: Faces
line: But?

title: Faces
line: I'm incomplete. It doesn't feel like me. I guess I've had someone else living inside of me for too long to feel right without her.

title: Faces
line: I'd have to say that you two made quite a team down there.

title: Faces
line: I know. I came to admire a lot of things about her. Her strength, her bravery. I guess I just have to accept the fact that I'll spend the rest of my life fighting with her.

line: You wanted to see me, Captain.

title: Jetrel
line: Yes, Neelix. We've received a subspace message from an approaching vessel. They're asking for you.

title: Jetrel
line: Me?

title: Jetrel
line: The alien ship is entering visual range, Captain.

title: Jetrel
line: Slow to impulse. On screen. Do you recognize it?

title: Jetrel
line: That's a Haarkonian shuttle.

title: Jetrel
line: Haarkonian?

title: Jetrel
line: My people were at war with them for the better part of a decade. They conquered my homeworld more than fifteen years ago.

title: Jetrel
line: Any idea what the Haarkonians want with you now?

title: Jetrel
line: None at all.

title: Jetrel
line: The shuttle is hailing us, Captain.

title: Jetrel
line: Open a channel.

title: Jetrel
line: Channel open.

title: Jetrel
line: I'm Captain Katherine Janeway of the Federation Starship Voyager. What can we do for you.

title: Jetrel
line: As I stated in my message, Captain, I understand you have a Talaxian called Neelix aboard your vessel.

title: Jetrel
line: I'm Neelix. What do you want?

title: Jetrel
line: It is a matter of utmost urgency. However, I would prefer to speak with you privately. Your life may very well depend on it.

title: Jetrel
line: Who are you?

title: Jetrel
line: Forgive me. I am Jetrel. Doctor Ma'bor Jetrel.

title: Jetrel
line: Neelix.

title: Jetrel
line: He's a mass murderer! When I was much younger my family and I lived on a moon called Rinax, a colony with the most temperate climate in the entire Talaxian system. Warm days, balmy nights. Until the Meteron Cascade. A melodic name, isn't it? Especially for a weapon of mass destruction.

title: Jetrel
line: And Jetrel was somehow involved with this weapon?

title: Jetrel
line: Doctor Jetrel was the scientist who conceived the Meteron Cascade, then he led the team of scientists who built it.

title: Jetrel
line: I see.

title: Jetrel
line: In the blink of an eye Rinax was enveloped by a deadly cloud, and those lovely days were turned into one endless frigid night. More than three hundred thousand were killed.

title: Jetrel
line: But you survived.

title: Jetrel
line: I had the good fortune to be on Talax at the time with our defense forces, preparing for an invasion that never came. It wasn't necessary. The day after the Cascade was deployed, Talax surrendered unconditionally to the Haarkonian Order.

title: Jetrel
line: And your family?

title: Jetrel
line: I am so sorry.

title: Jetrel
line: Doctor Jetrel. Lieutenant Tuvok, my chief of security.

title: Jetrel
line: I have heard of your transporter technology, Captain, but, to experience it first hand is truly remarkable.

title: Jetrel
line: Mister Neelix has declined to meet with you.

title: Jetrel
line: That's not surprising. I'm afraid I am not a very popular figure among the Talaxian people.

title: Jetrel
line: May we show you to your quarters?

title: Jetrel
line: Mister Neelix has given me permission to speak on his behalf. You indicated that he may be in some kind of danger?

title: Jetrel
line: Yes. It's imperative that he undergo a compete medical examination.

title: Jetrel
line: For what purpose?

title: Jetrel
line: Our war records show that he was part of the team that returned to Rinax after the Cascade in order to evacuate survivors. He was exposed to high concentrations of Meteron isotopes. In recent years several of the rescuers have developed a degenerative blood disease called metermia.

title: Jetrel
line: Is it serious?

title: Jetrel
line: I am afraid that it's fatal. The disease attacks its victims on a molecular level. It may lay dormant for years, but once it manifests itself, it will cause the body's atomic structure to undergo fission. The cells will begin to disintegrate. My equipment is specifically designed to detect the sub-atomic signature of the disorder.

title: Jetrel
line: May I ask, Doctor, why you've taken it upon yourself to examine Mister Neelix?

title: Jetrel
line: I've evaluated as many members of the team as possible, collecting data, in hopes that one day my research may lead to a cure for metermia. Please, try to persuade Mister Neelix to see me. Each Talaxian I screen brings me one step closer to a cure.

title: Jetrel
line: Neelix, why didn't you ever tell me about the war?

title: Jetrel
line: Maybe this is one experience that can't be shared. It's too hard to describe how I feel to someone who didn't see what I saw. I'm sorry.

title: Jetrel
line: You've nothing to be sorry about, Neelix.

title: Jetrel
line: Excuse me.

title: Jetrel
line: Captain! Back from your doctor's appointment already?

title: Jetrel
line: I'm afraid I have some disturbing news, Neelix.

title: Jetrel
line: Nothing you tell me can make this day more disturbing than it's already been.

title: Jetrel
line: According to Jetrel, you were exposed to dangerous levels of Meteron poisoning, and may be at risk of developing a fatal blood disorder. He wants to screen you for the disease.

title: Jetrel
line: Er, Captain, please tell Doctor Jetrel that I am touched by his tender concern for my state of health, but that I'd rather be immersed in a pit of Kraylinnian eels than examined by him.

title: Jetrel
line: Neelix, if there's something wrong with you we should find out.

title: Jetrel
line: I don't want that man within ten parsecs of me!

title: Jetrel
line: I understand your feelings, but this is your life we're talking about.

title: Jetrel
line: Don't either of you find it the slightest bit strange that a man who has made it his life's work to develop a weapon to destroy as many Talaxians as possible should suddenly be concerned with this Talaxian's health.

title: Jetrel
line: I don't know what his motives are. Maybe he's trying to undo some of the damage his weapon caused? But he seems sincere, Neelix, and at this point I have no reason to doubt him.

title: Jetrel
line: If the disease is fatal, what's the point of knowing whether I have it or not?

title: Jetrel
line: Our doctor is the most skilled physician either of us has ever met. If you have this disease he won't stop until he's found some way to treat it.

title: Jetrel
line: And if Jetrel discovers you don't have the disease, at least you'll have peace of mind.

title: Jetrel
line: Peace of mind is a relative thing, Captain.

title: Jetrel
line: I simply want you to hear what he has to say. Then, if you still don't want him to examine you, no one will force you.

title: Jetrel
line: Outnumbered and outflanked. All right then, I surrender.

title: Jetrel
line: The Meteron isotopes are unique. The rate of decay is highly variable. We have found that it's sometimes years before Metermia sets in, and unfortunately

title: Jetrel
line: Why are you doing this?

title: Jetrel
line: I beg your pardon?

title: Jetrel
line: Is it all just scientific curiosity, Meterons and isotopes. Or do you feel guilty about what you did.

title: Jetrel
line: Guilty? I do not regret it. I did what had to be done.

title: Jetrel
line: Really? It was necessary to vaporize more than a quarter of a million people and to leave thousands of others to be eaten away by Meteron poisoning.

title: Jetrel
line: Would it make any difference if I told you we never thought there would be any radiation poisoning. That anyone close enough to be exposed would be killed by the initial blast. It was unfortunate we were wrong.

title: Jetrel
line: Unfortunate? Did you hear that, Captain? It was unfortunate.

line: Neelix, I think what Doctor Jetrel is trying

title: Jetrel
line: No, Captain, that's all right. I'm used to it. I'm simply a scientist. Yes, I developed the weapon, but it was the government and the military leaders who decided to use it, not I.

title: Jetrel
line: That must be a very convenient distinction for you. Does it help you sleep at night?

title: Jetrel
line: I slept no worse last night than I have any other night for the past fifteen years.

title: Jetrel
line: What is that supposed to mean?

title: Jetrel
line: It means I must live with my conscience, as you who must live with yours. How many did you kill during the war?

title: Jetrel
line: Gentlemen, please. This is obviously very difficult for both of you but we are not here to debate history. We are here to talk about Neelix's condition.

title: Jetrel
line: Don't worry about it, Captain, because Doctor Jetrel will have to find himself another laboratory rodent to help his experiments. Because I would rather die than help you ease your conscience.

title: Jetrel
line: I do not expect you to like me, Mister Neelix, nor do I hope to allay your obvious pain with moral arguments, but I do believe I can help you. If not you, then others of your race. Isn't that more important than punishing me?

title: Jetrel
line: Are you sure you can't do this?

title: Jetrel
line: You're new found confidence in me is flattering, Mister Neelix, but Doctor Jetrel has instruments designed specifically to analyze Talaxian physiology.

title: Jetrel
line: Just get it over with.

title: Jetrel
line: Did I ever tell you about the notorious two-tailed talchoks of Rinax?

title: Jetrel
line: I don't think so.

title: Jetrel
line: Nasty little vermin. Sharp claws, dripping fangs. Ugh. It was quite a nuisance. So one summer when I was a boy, I decided to do something about them. I spent weeks tinkering, creating a fool-proof talchok trap. Once I'd perfected it I set it in the garden. And the next day I found one of those beasts pinned at the neck. But it wasn't dead, it was squirming, squealing in agony. And suddenly it didn't look so fiendish any more. It looked like a poor innocent animal.

title: Jetrel
line: What a horrible story.

title: Jetrel
line: You see, I had become so fascinated with my invention that I never really thought about how that poor creature would suffer.

title: Jetrel
line: Are you finished?

title: Jetrel
line: Sorry? Why are you sorry?

title: Jetrel
line: I'm afraid you have incipient metermia.

title: Jetrel

title: Jetrel
line: How are you feeling?

title: Jetrel
line: Kes, my sweet, I'll have you know this is not the first time I have gazed into the gaping maw of death. Why once, during the battle of the Pyrithian Gorge I faced down an entire battery of Haarkonian artillery. There I was, with only a small crevice for cover

title: Jetrel
line: Neelix, you're protecting me again. I can understand your not wanting to talk about Rinax. I wasn't there, you're right. But I'm here now with you. We have to face this together.

title: Jetrel
line: Well, there's one good thing that will come from all this. When I first met you I didn't know that your species lived only eight or nine years. I fell in love with you without knowing how lonely it would be to live without you after you're gone. Now that I'm going to die first, I don't have to worry about it.

title: Jetrel
line: Before I met you, eight or nine years seemed like an eternity. It never occurred to me that anyone could live longer. title: Jetrel
line: Captain, I must tell you, your ship is simply astounding. I have been studying your transporter systems.

title: Jetrel

title: Jetrel
line: Forgive me, but that is what I am here to talk about. I believe, with a relatively few minor modifications, the transporter system could be used to retrieve a sample of the Meteron cloud surrounding Rinax.

title: Jetrel

title: Jetrel
line: I've always believed that if I could isolate the free isotope that causes metermia, it could be used to synthesis an antibody.

title: Jetrel

title: Jetrel
line: Yes, Captain, and your transporter system makes it all possible.

title: Jetrel

title: Jetrel
line: I believe so.

title: Jetrel
line: We could construct a containment field to prevent any contamination of the ship, and I could have our Doctor assist you with synthesizing the antibody.

title: Jetrel
line: My thoughts exactly.

title: Jetrel

title: Jetrel

title: Jetrel
line: I'm aware of that, Commander.

title: Jetrel

title: Jetrel
line: Understood.

title: Jetrel
line: I'll send a message to Talax requesting permission to transport material from the cloud. In the meantime, Lieutenant Torres in Engineering can give you a hand with the transporter modifications.

line: Maybe this is one of those decisions that the captain has to make for the entire ship.

title: The 37's
line: You may have a problem if a lot of people want to stay.

title: The 37's
line: I know that, but at the same time I can't take a vote every time there's a major decision to be made. And yet, we're a long way from Starfleet, and a lot of the rules and regulations I've learnt to uphold seem distant as well. Am I the only one who's so intent on getting home? Is it just me? Am I leading the crew on a forlorn mission with no real hope of success?

title: The 37's
line: You're not alone. I want to get home, too. And there's not a day that goes by when I don't hear someone mention Earth.

title: The 37's
line: The people here have built a new Earth. We could stay, help them build a human civilization in the Delta Quadrant. Isn't that an exciting prospect? Shouldn't we be grateful for the opportunity they're giving us?

title: The 37's
line: It is a tempting prospect, but when I hold it up against the prospect of seeing the sun rise over the Arizona desert, or swimming in the Gulf of Mexico on a summers day, there's just no comparison. I want to go home.

title: The 37's
line: We have one hundred and fifty two men and women on this ship. What happens if half of them decide to stay on the planet? Could we operate Voyager with seventy five crew members?

title: The 37's
line: I doubt it. In fact I don't think we could operate the ship with fewer than one hundred. If too many of the crew choose to stay behind, we could all be stranded here.

title: The 37's
line: Tell all hands to prepare for an announcement from the Captain at fourteen hundred hours. They deserve to make the choice for themselves.

title: The 37's
line: Aye, Captain.

title: The 37's
line: Here we are! My research on twentieth century Earth is a little thin, but I've done what I can. Pot roast, green beans and something called Jell-O.

title: The 37's
line: You know how to make Jell-O?

title: The 37's
line: I even put in fruit cocktail.

title: The 37's
line: You don't say.

title: The 37's
line: I don't know about the rest of you, but I've made up my mind. There is land here that goes begging, and I could have a big farm, just like I always dreamed.

title: The 37's
line: And for you, rice with a little fish. I even replicated some ginger for seasoning.

title: The 37's
line: Very nice, thank you.

title: The 37's
line: I have to admit, life here looks a lot better than what we left on Earth.

title: The 37's
line: It's paradise by comparison. And there are many Japanese here. I could be very happy.

title: The 37's
line: We all could. Right?

title: The 37's
line: I'm just not sure. What about you, Mister Neelix? Have you made your decision?

title: The 37's
line: Oh yes, indeed. I'm staying right here with Captain Janeway. She'd be lost without me. She's come to depend on me a great deal.

title: The 37's
line: What about the rest of the crew? Do you think many of them will stay here?

title: The 37's
line: Oh, I don't think so. At least, not many. Well, that is, there's a good chance. Well, now that you ask, I honestly don't know.

title: The 37's
line: You? You'd stay here on the planet?

title: The 37's
line: I didn't say I was going to, I just said I could understand why people would want to. The people here remind me of home. I haven't felt like that since I left Earth.

title: The 37's
line: But you're Starfleet. You've always wanted a life in space.

title: The 37's
line: I know, but, my whole life on a starship, day after day, with no end in sight? That's not exactly what I had in mind.

title: The 37's
line: You're not the first person I've heard talk like this. A lot of people are thinking about staying.

title: The 37's
line: What about you? Don't you have some of those feelings?

title: The 37's
line: I'd be lying if I said I didn't.

title: The 37's
line: Captain. I was told I'd find you here. Am I intruding?

title: The 37's
line: Not at all. Please join me.

title: The 37's
line: I wanted you to know that the group you brought out of stasis, we've all decided to stay here on the planet.

title: The 37's
line: I understand.

title: The 37's
line: I must admit the thought of traveling through space, maybe even learning to fly this ship, was very appealing to me.

title: The 37's
line: And I'd looked forward to getting to know you better. I suspect we have a lot in common.

title: The 37's
line: At first I didn't know what to do. We talked about it for quite some time. Finally I realized the people here on this planet are part of us. We're their ancestors in a way. It made us feel close to them.

title: The 37's
line: The remarkable thing about the humans on this planet is that they evolved very much like the people on Earth. Tens of thousands of light years apart, both civilizations managed to create a world they could be proud of. One where war and poverty simply don't exist. I certainly can't blame you for wanting to be part of it, any more than I can blame members of my crew if they make the same decision.

title: The 37's
line: When will you find out?

title: The 37's
line: In half an hour. Any one who wants to stay behind is to report to the cargo bay at fifteen hundred hours.

title: The 37's
line: I expect Jarvin will stay on the planet. In fact, I'd bet on it.

title: The 37's
line: Why Jarvin?

title: The 37's
line: He's been more uncomfortable about being on a Starfleet ship than most of the Maquis, and he's gotten involved with a young woman in Quantum Mechanics. I think they'd like to settle down, raise a family.

title: The 37's
line: The person I expect to see is Baxter.

title: The 37's
line: Baxter? Walter Baxter?

title: The 37's
line: He's adventurous, a risk taker. I can see him wanting to take on the challenge of building a new life on this planet.

title: The 37's
line: I'd hate to loose Baxter. He's a good man.

title: The 37's
line: I'd hate to loose Jarvin. I don't want to loose anyone. We've all been through so much together, it just wouldn't seem right. But I couldn't blame anyone, anyone for staying behind. I'm not sure I want to go in.
