title: Elogium
line: They seem to be pulling us toward them.

title: Elogium
line: Sensors indicate an EM resonance field. The creatures seem to be creating their own magnetic wake. That is what is pulling the ship.

title: Elogium
line: We're getting closer.

title: Elogium
line: Mister Paris, reverse thrusters.

title: Elogium
line: Helm controls aren't responding, Captain.

title: Elogium
line: Mister Tuvok, raise shields.

title: Elogium
line: Non-functional, Captain.

title: Elogium
line: They're pulling us in.

title: Elogium
line: Damage report.

title: Elogium
line: Life support's functioning normally, Captain, but there's a huge fluctuation in the EPS grids. It's wreaking havoc with the impulse engines.

title: Elogium
line: Warp drive's still online. One burst and we'd be out of here.

title: Elogium
line: But our exhaust could seriously harm the creatures.

title: Elogium
line: Janeway to Torres. Do you have any thoughts about how to get us out of this swarm without engaging warp engines?

title: Elogium
line: We might try something like a targ scoop.

title: Elogium
line: Can you enlighten us, Lieutenant?

title: Elogium
line: Klingons put them on the front of ground assault vehicles. They emit a high frequency tone that disperses targ herds in their path. I can modify the

title: Elogium
line: Main deflector to create an inverted magnetic pulse.

title: Elogium
line: Project it toward the swarm. It might be enough to nudge the creatures out of the way.

title: Elogium
line: Good idea, Lieutenant. Proceed.

title: Elogium
line: You're sure the beetles weren't poisonous? Or the flowers?

title: Elogium
line: There are no toxins present in her system.

title: Elogium
line: Doctor, why is she eating all these strange things? What's wrong with her?

title: Elogium
line: I am conducting an examination in order to determine that.

title: Elogium
line: But don't you have any ideas?

title: Elogium
line: Her unusual appetite may merely indicate a nutrient deficiency. It is not unusual for humanoids to crave foods that are rich in the very vitamins and minerals that their bodies are lacking.

title: Elogium
line: You can't mean my body lacks dirt?

title: Elogium
line: Her body temperature is elevated three point nine degrees.

title: Elogium
line: She's burning up!

title: Elogium
line: And I'm detecting elevated levels of electrophoretic activity in her nervous system.

title: Elogium
line: You have to bring them down!

title: Elogium
line: There is increased electrophoretic activity in the ship's atmosphere, probably created by the creatures we're studying.

title: Elogium
line: You mean there's a connection between what's happening to Kes and those creatures? Well, you have to do something about it!

title: Elogium
line: You are making it impossible for me to think, much less treat my patient. You must leave.

title: Elogium
line: Well, I won't. Kes needs me.

title: Elogium
line: Leave now or I will call security.

title: Elogium
line: You can't talk to me that way.

title: Elogium
line: This is my Sickbay, and I will decide what goes on here.

title: Elogium
line: But

title: Elogium
line: Get out!

title: Elogium
line: I'll be back. Don't worry about a thing.

title: Elogium
line: Captain, may I speak with you? It's a matter of some urgency.

title: Elogium
line: What is it, Neelix?

title: Elogium
line: I have been thrown out of Sickbay, and I'm just wondering if you feel it's appropriate for a hologram to banish a flesh and blood person who should have the right to be at the bedside of his loved one who is extremely ill?

title: Elogium
line: Kes is extremely ill?

title: Elogium
line: The hologram doesn't have a clue as to what's wrong with her, though it may have something to do with these creatures. But he still won't let me offer comfort to the woman I love at a time when my place is clearly by her side.

title: Elogium
line: Just how is Kes being affected by the swarm?

title: Elogium
line: That's what I wanted to know. But before I got any answers, I was summarily dismissed!

title: Elogium
line: Sickbay to bridge.

title: Elogium
line: Janeway here.

title: Elogium
line: Captain, I think you'd better come down here. There's a bit of a problem.

title: Elogium
line: I'm on my way. Commander, you have the bridge. Notify me immediately of any change in our status.

title: Elogium
line: Aye, Captain.

title: Elogium
line: I was conducting tests. She was none too cooperative, let me assure you. Then suddenly she screeched and shoved me out of the way, went into my office and proceeded to erect a force field at the door. I can't lower it. She's keeping me out of my own office.

title: Elogium
line: Sweeting. What's wrong? Please come out.

title: Elogium
line: I was able to complete several tests before she became delirious. Her fever has increased, and her pulse and blood pressure are dangerously high.

title: Elogium
line: Do you have any idea what's causing these symptoms?

title: Elogium
line: I suspect it's the electrophoretic levels being created by the swarm. We should leave. Immediately.

title: Elogium
line: Unfortunately, that's not an option at the moment, but we're working on it.

title: Elogium
line: There's one more thing. I discovered a strange growth on her back. It's unlike any other tumorous substance I've ever seen or studied before, and it was not there the last time I examined her.

title: Elogium
line: I'll try to talk to her.

title: Elogium
line: Kes, please come out. You can eat anything you want. Captain?

title: Elogium
line: Why don't you let me try? Kes, please listen to me. We think you're being affected by a swarm of space dwelling life forms. We're doing everything we can to get away from them. And when we do, you'll probably start feeling better.

title: Elogium
line: Are you saying that's not what's wrong with you? Kes, please let me come in. Tell me what it is. Maybe I can help.

title: Elogium
line: Oh. Shush. It's going to be all right. Now, tell me. What is happening to you?

title: Elogium
line: Did the Doctor tell you he found something growing on my back?

title: Elogium
line: Yes, a growth of some kind.

title: Elogium
line: It's, it's the mitral sac. It's, it's where my child would grow. I'm going through the elogium, the time of change, when, when my body prepares for fertilization.

title: Elogium
line: Humans go through the same kind of process. It's called puberty.

title: Elogium
line: But I'm too young. Much too young. It usually happens between the ages of four and five. I'm not even two yet.

title: Elogium
line: Listen to me. All your body's metabolic activity has increased. It's possible your reproductive processes are being accelerated as a result.

title: Elogium
line: I'm not ready.

title: Elogium
line: We're going to get you through this, Kes. The Doctor will monitor you constantly.

title: Elogium
line: But you, you don't understand. The elogium occurs only once. If I am ever going to have a child, it has to be now!

title: Elogium
line: No change, Captain. We're still being pulled along with the swarm.

title: Elogium
line: Heading one twenty one mark seven. Speed now six thousand kilometers per second.

title: Elogium
line: All systems are functioning within normal parameters.

title: Elogium
line: How is Torres coming with the modifications to the main deflector?

title: Elogium
line: Her last report estimated they'd be finished in another half hour.

title: Elogium
line: Let me know as soon as she's ready. Join me, Commander?

title: Elogium
line: Kes is terribly frightened. She's had no time to prepare for this. And the decision has to be made in the next forty or fifty hours. She's going to discuss it with Neelix, but there are so many unknowns. There might be risks in procreating this early. And of course, there's no guarantee they're genetically compatible, or that Neelix has any interest in becoming a father. It seems your concerns about fraternization were prophetic.

title: Elogium
line: I wasn't even thinking about procreation, but I suppose it's the inevitable outcome. We should consider the fact that it might be necessary for the crew to start having children.

title: Elogium
line: It might take us a long time to get home.

title: Elogium
line: If it does take seventy five years, we're going to need a replacement crew in about half that time.

title: Elogium
line: Who'd have thought we'd be considering a generational ship when we were ordered on a three week mission.

title: Elogium
line: I know, but it's a problem we have to face now.

title: Elogium
line: What would that mean for the children? What kind of life would we be giving them aboard a starship, traveling through a potentially hostile part of space? And are we equipped to provide for their needs? Child care, educational facilities. We'd be building an entire community on board this ship. That's a massive commitment.

title: Elogium
line: Are you prepared to tell them they can't have children?

title: Elogium
line: I can't do that. And I've made it clear to Kes that it's her choice whether to have a child or not, but. There aren't any easy answers here. For any of us.

title: Elogium
line: Are you saying that unless you conceive now, you'll never be able to?

title: Elogium
line: Yes. And I need you to help me decide, because I would want you to mate with me.

title: Elogium
line: Oh. I'm, I'm, I'm, I'm, I'm, I'm honored, but are you entirely certain it would be safe?

title: Elogium
line: Safe?

title: Elogium
line: Well, you're so young. Is it dangerous for you to conceive a child at your age?

title: Elogium
line: I don't know. I've never known anyone as young as I am who had a baby.

title: Elogium
line: If you never had a child, would you be terribly unhappy?

title: Elogium
line: Yes! I mean, I think so. I don't know. I always assumed I'd be a mother someday. Just not so soon. What about you? Didn't you think you'd be a father someday?

title: Elogium
line: Well, to be honest, I've never given it much thought. Until now, my life has been so itinerant. There's no way I could have provided the stability a child would need.

title: Elogium
line: But now it's different, isn't it?

title: Elogium
line: Well, yes. but raising a child on a starship? That's hardly what I would call the ideal environment.

title: Elogium
line: You don't want a child, do you?

title: Elogium
line: No, that's not it at all. I'm just trying to look at all sides of the issue. Bringing a child into the world. It's a huge responsibility. I know you'd want to be sure we're both up to the task. I mean, somebody would have to keep their eye on the little guy all the time or he'd be off sticking his finger into an EM conduit or playing with the plasma injectors.

title: Elogium
line: That's right. That's called being a parent.

title: Elogium
line: What about your medical studies? You wouldn't be able to continue them if you had a child.

title: Elogium
line: Of course I would. You're just making excuses. All you're thinking about is yourself, how much trouble a child would be for you. Look!

title: Elogium
line: What's that?

title: Elogium
line: The ipasaphor. It makes the mating bond possible.

title: Elogium
line: It does?

title: Elogium
line: If we begin, we must stay bonded for six days.

title: Elogium
line: Six days?

title: Elogium
line: In order to ensure conception. And after the ipasaphor appears, we only have fifty hours to begin the process. So I need to know your answer.

title: Elogium
line: Well, er, fifty hours? That's good. That's good. We can sleep on it. I'll get back to you.

title: Elogium
line: Sorry. I swear I heard you say lots of pepper sauce.

title: Elogium
line: What is the lunch special today?

title: Elogium
line: Well, actually, I didn't get around to making a lunch special. But we have some lovely gabosti stew left over from last night.

title: Elogium
line: Very well. It will do.

title: Elogium
line: I've had quite a run on it, as a matter of fact. It seems very popular.

title: Elogium
line: If it is all you are serving, that would stand to reason.

title: Elogium
line: You can have it with or without pepper sauce.

title: Elogium
line: Without.

title: Elogium
line: Mister Tuvok, I was wondering. You have children, don't you?

title: Elogium
line: I have four.

title: Elogium
line: Four! My, that's certainly quite a family. Tell me, what's it like, being a father?

title: Elogium
line: The question is so broad, it is difficult to respond.

title: Elogium
line: Well, I mean, it's a lot of responsibility, isn't it? Watching them, caring for them, keeping them safe, giving them an education.

title: Elogium
line: That is certainly true.

title: Elogium
line: Sounds like it's a lot more trouble than it's worth.

title: Elogium
line: Mister Neelix, I am aware of your situation. It appears you are in some doubt as to the wisdom of becoming a parent.

title: Elogium
line: It's just all happening so fast. I don't know what to think.

title: Elogium
line: I can only tell you that if you have considerable doubts about fatherhood, it would not be wise to enter into the process. It is so much more overwhelming than one expects, that I believe only the most committed should become parents.

title: Elogium
line: Ah. that's what I thought.

title: Elogium
line: However, I must point out that, as illogical as it seems, being a father can have infinite rewards. Far more than would seem possible. My children occupy a significant portion of my thoughts. Now more than ever.

title: Elogium
line: I-I-I've heard it said that children can bring a lot of joy into one's life.

title: Elogium
line: I experienced neither joy nor sorrow, but I do believe it is possible.

title: Elogium
line: Now that I think about it, it might be fun to have a little guy around. We could do a lot together. I've got quite a bit I could teach a boy, you know. Survival methods, piloting skills, romantic techniques.

title: Elogium
line: If you say so. But I must point out that there is an equal chance that you would have a daughter.

title: Elogium
line: A daughter? I don't have anything to teach a daughter.

title: Elogium
line: Why would it be any different from what you would teach a son?

title: Elogium
line: It just would. She'd learn more from her mother.

title: Elogium
line: I have three sons and one daughter. I can assure you she benefits as much from my presence and guidance as my sons do. It is unfortunate that I must be so far removed from all of them now.

title: Elogium
line: I understand. We'll get there, Mister Vulcan. I'm sure of it. Thank you. You've given me a lot to think about.

title: Elogium
line: We're ready to generate the inverted magnetic pulse, Captain.

title: Elogium
line: Proceed.

title: Elogium
line: Initiating the field. It's working.

title: Elogium
line: Are the creatures all right, Commander?

title: Elogium
line: Yes, Captain. They seem to be fine.

title: Elogium
line: Let's try to keep it that way. Thrusters at two hundred kph, Mister Paris. Ease us out of here.

title: Elogium
line: Aye, Captain.

title: Elogium
line: What are they doing?

title: Elogium
line: Hard to know what's prompting that behavior. Maybe they think we're making a hostile move.

title: Elogium
line: Report.

title: Elogium
line: I'm reading a massive energy drain in all ship's systems.

title: Elogium
line: Impulse engines are losing power.

title: Elogium
line: Captain, some of the life forms have attached themselves to the warp nacelles.

title: Elogium
line: Guidance, navigational and tactical systems are failing.

title: Elogium
line: How soon will we clear the swarm, Lieutenant?

title: Elogium
line: In a few seconds. We're almost out.

title: Elogium
line: Captain, I am detecting a substantial magnetic mass moving rapidly toward the port bow.

title: Elogium
line: It's physiologically similar to the smaller creatures, just a lot bigger.

title: Elogium
line: Perhaps it is the parent.

title: Elogium
line: Or it could be a difference in gender. It's hard to say without further observation.

title: Elogium
line: With all due respect, Captain, haven't we done enough observing? These creatures have attacked the ship's key systems. For all we know, they were setting us up for an attack.

title: Elogium
line: It's possible. Mister Paris, let's keep moving. If we can put some distance between us and the swarm, maybe the ones on our nacelles will drop off and rejoin their friends.

title: Elogium
line: Aye, Captain. Two hundred kph.

title: Elogium
line: The larger creature is moving with us.

title: Elogium
line: Now what?

title: Elogium
line: The creature has emitted an electrically charged plasma stream.

title: Elogium
line: All stop. Damage report.

title: Elogium
line: No significant damage, Captain. Shields are holding.

title: Elogium
line: A plasma blast is a hostile move. Shouldn't we be thinking about responding?

title: Elogium
line: If the creature threatens serious damage to the ship, I'll consider it an enemy. Until then, they're all to be treated as indigenous life forms behaving normally in their natural habitat. We're the intruders here.

title: Elogium
line: Captain, look at this. They're attaching themselves to the large creature the same way they did to us.

title: Elogium
line: And I think I know why. That plasma stream it ejected has almost the same subspace signature as our warp nacelles.

title: Elogium
line: Then the smaller creatures are attracted to our subspace emissions.

title: Elogium
line: Perhaps in the same way some species are attracted to pheromones.

title: Elogium
line: Pheromones? You think it's a sexual attraction?

title: Elogium
line: Color change and provocative movement are frequently associated with mating rituals.

title: Elogium
line: Then these guys think we're one of them?

title: Elogium
line: Well, their behavior toward us and the large creature is similar. It's possible they've mistaken us for a potential mate.

title: Elogium
line: Yes?

title: Elogium
line: Well, order the diapers. We're about to become parents.

title: Elogium
line: You mean you want to mate with me?

title: Elogium
line: More than anything.

title: Elogium
line: But you were making excuses. I didn't think you wanted to be a father.

title: Elogium
line: I just hadn't thought it through. Now that I have, I swear to you I want to do this. And I'll be the best possible father to our child.

title: Elogium
line: I know you will.

title: Elogium
line: So, what comes next?

title: Elogium
line: Before we begin the mating process, I have to go through a certain ritual called the rolisisin.

title: Elogium
line: What does that involve?

title: Elogium
line: One of my parents has to massage my feet until my tongue begins to swell.

title: Elogium
line: Er, where do you plan to find a parent?

title: Elogium
line: If Captain Janeway weren't so busy, I'd ask her, but I'm sure the Doctor would do it.

title: Elogium
line: Will that work, since he's not a real person?

title: Elogium
line: The Doctor is very real to me.

title: Elogium
line: I don't know how I feel about him massaging your feet.

title: Elogium
line: It's a ritual. Someone has to do it.

title: Elogium
line: Okay. Okay, fine. How long will that take?

title: Elogium
line: About an hour. Then I'll be back.

title: Elogium
line: Fascinating. The stimulation to the sympathetic nerves must set off a hormonal reaction, which activates glandular activity in the tissues of the tongue. I've never seen this response before. Although in a species known as the Gree, stimulating follicles on the proboscis results in a swelling of the auricular canal.

title: Elogium
line: Doctor?

title: Elogium
line: Yes?

title: Elogium
line: Am I doing the right thing?

title: Elogium
line: You'll have to tell me. I know nothing of this ritual.

title: Elogium
line: No. I mean am I doing the right thing by conceiving a child? If I were at home now, my father would be performing the rolisisin with me. It's time when parent and child move into a new kind of relationship. As the child has her own child, the parent must acknowledge her true adulthood.

title: Elogium
line: I see.

title: Elogium
line: My father and I were very close. He was such a wise man. I miss him. Sometimes I think I hear his voice in my head. It's almost as though he were here, helping to guide me. I'm sorry. I must be feeling lonely for home. It's probably a result of the elogium. But I really would appreciate your advice, your help. I need someone's guidance.

title: Elogium
line: I can discuss delivery methods or pediatric situations. I'm afraid I don't have much perspective to offer about becoming a parent.

title: Elogium
line: Neither do I. As long as Neelix was opposed to the idea, trying to get out of it, I was certain that I wanted to have a child. But when he said that he wanted one too, suddenly I was very frightened.

title: Elogium
line: Perhaps a statistical survey will offer a context. Among the Breen, pregnancy at a young age is a common event. The Breen, of course, is one the most warlike of species. And then there are the Scathos. Any woman who conceives a child before her fourth decade is summarily executed.

title: Elogium
line: Maybe I just felt I should have a child because I could.

title: Elogium
line: There is a powerful biological drive, at times almost impossible to resist. Species are driven by these urges in order to survive.

title: Elogium
line: But isn't that why we have minds? To look beyond biological urges, to consider their consequences? If I'm going to ask myself to look at those consequences, then I have to ask myself some questions. Am I really ready to have a child? Am I prepared to give that child the attention and devotion it deserves? Am I capable of taking on such a huge responsibility? There's so much I haven't done. There's so much I want to study and learn. I'm not sure I'm finished growing. How can I help a child grow?

title: Elogium
line: If the smaller creatures are sexually attracted to our subspace emissions, then the large one may perceive us as a rival. That plasma burst it sent out might have been aggressive posturing.

title: Elogium
line: Then you'd think it would be happy to see us leave. Lieutenant, is there any way we could generate a short burst at impulse, enough to get us away from this swarm?

title: Elogium
line: I could try releasing power from the impulse capacitance cells straight into the driver coils.

title: Elogium
line: Do it.

title: Elogium
line: All right. I've accessed the capacitance cells. I think I can give you enough for a short burst at impulse. We've got one shot, Captain.

title: Elogium
line: You heard her, Mister Paris. Make the best of it.

title: Elogium
line: Aye, Captain. Initiating impulse burst, now.

title: Elogium
line: Captain, the creature is reacting. It is approaching rapidly on a collision course.

title: Elogium
line: Evasive maneuvers, Lieutenant.

title: Elogium
line: We don't have the power for that.

title: Elogium
line: The creature is accelerating.

title: Elogium
line: I'm losing power. Can't shake him.

title: Elogium
line: All hands brace for impact.

title: Elogium
line: Structural integrity down to eight six percent.

title: Elogium
line: I'm beginning to share Lieutenant Torres' views, Captain. Retaliation may become necessary.

title: Elogium
line: It's not my intention to harm the creature.

title: Elogium
line: The feeling definitely isn't mutual.

title: Elogium
line: Mister Tuvok, launch a Class Four probe. Maybe that will distract the creature long enough for us to get away.

title: Elogium
line: Aye, Captain. Probe launched.

title: Elogium
line: Another plasma burst. Shields are down to sixty four percent. Looks like the probe just made him angry.

title: Elogium
line: This is an aggressive life form, Captain. He's only going to respond to an aggressive stance from us.

title: Elogium
line: Treating the creature as it is treating us might be an appropriate response.

title: Elogium
line: We ram him.

title: Elogium
line: Precisely.

title: Elogium
line: It's probably the response he expects.

title: Elogium
line: Captain, shields are at forty seven percent. Any more of this and the hull will start to buckle.

title: Elogium
line: Mister Paris, use maneuvering thrusters. Set a course toward the creature. Give him a bump to get his attention.

title: Elogium
line: Aye, Captain. Engaging thrusters.

title: Elogium
line: The creature is not retreating, Captain.

title: Elogium
line: He's just hitting us back harder!

title: Elogium
line: Let's try this. Detonate a field of photon charges between Voyager and the creature. Maybe the shock wave will let him know we mean business.

title: Elogium
line: Captain, if I may. Maybe we're going about this backwards.

title: Elogium
line: Yes, Commander?

title: Elogium
line: Every aggressive move we make results in a more aggressive move by the creature. If we're not prepared to use extreme force to destroy him, we need to rethink our actions.

title: Elogium
line: I'm listening.

title: Elogium
line: If we're right that the creature is responding to us as a sexual rival, we might try behaving in a submissive way. That may appease him. We'd be acknowledging that he's dominant and that we're no match for him.

title: Elogium
line: How do we do that? We tried to move away slowly. He wouldn't let us leave.

title: Elogium
line: Maybe we need to mimic the behavior of the smaller creatures. We saw them rolling over and changing color.

title: Elogium
line: If we vent plasma residue, that might make us look blue.

title: Elogium
line: Mister Paris, do we have enough power to take Voyager into a roll?

title: Elogium
line: I think so.

title: Elogium
line: All right. Let's give this a try. Mister Kim, start venting plasma residue. Mister Paris, roll the ship.

title: Elogium
line: Full power to inertial dampers.

title: Elogium
line: He's not responding at all. It's not working.

title: Elogium
line: Wait a minute, Captain.

title: Elogium
line: What is it?

title: Elogium
line: One of the small creatures is detaching from the starboard nacelle. And another one. They're all letting go.

title: Elogium
line: It appears we have lost our sex appeal, Captain.

title: Elogium
line: Good piloting, Lieutenant. Now let's see if we can move away without any interference.

title: Elogium
line: I can give you enough thruster power to sustain a speed of one hundred kph.

title: Elogium
line: Acknowledged.

title: Elogium
line: Good work, Commander. In the future, if I have any questions about mating behavior, I'll know where to go.

title: Elogium
line: Can I help?

title: Elogium
line: No. Thanks.

title: Elogium
line: Is something wrong?

title: Elogium
line: No. No, nothing.

title: Elogium
line: You've been very quiet ever since I decided not to conceive.

title: Elogium
line: It was your choice. I respect that.

title: Elogium
line: Neelix, I think you're disappointed.

title: Elogium
line: I think, once I decided to become a father, I was looking forward to it. But I'll get over it.

title: Elogium
line: Maybe you won't have to get over it. Just wait a little longer.

title: Elogium
line: But I thought this was the only time.

title: Elogium
line: The Doctor believes the elogium was false, brought on by the electrophoretic field that those life forms created. So there's a possibility that I might be able to go through it again at the right age.

title: Elogium
line: You mean, we might still be able to have a daughter?

title: Elogium
line: Or a son.

title: Elogium

line: Mister Tuvok, do a multiphasic scan on those ships. I want any evidence of defensive weakness. And prepare the forward photon torpedoes for launch. Tuvok.

line: I do not understand how this can be.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Don't try to understand, Tuvok. Just accept it. We're together again.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: No. You are not my wife.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Of course I am. I am T'Pel. And there, right in front of you, is your lute. The one you used to play for me. And look. Look around you. You're back home, on Vulcan.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Tuvok? Tuvok, answer me. Tuvok!

line: Captain, I'll do it. Running a multiphasic scan.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Janeway here.

line: We're having problems down here.

line: People are becoming delusional.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: It's happening her too.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I think I know why. There's a massive energy field coming from those ships. It's bioelectric, modulating on a delta wave frequency. It has psionic properties, and it's permeating the hull.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: A psionic field has a psychoactive effect. That would explain the hallucinations.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: You can try remodulating

title: Persistence of Vision
line: The shields, but in the meantime, I'm going to set up a resonance burst from the warp core. That will probably block the field, but it'll take a while to set up.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Notify the Doctor. If the field is bioelectric, he might have some ideas how to neutralize it. Commander, give Lieutenant Torres a hand in Engineering. Mister Neelix, if the crew ever needed a morale officer, now's the time. See if you can help.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Aye, Captain.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Kath, do you always have to be the captain? Can't you relax for a minute? I want to talk to you.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Mister Kim, remodulate the shields on a rotating frequency.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Janeway to Kes.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Yes, Captain?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Can you come to the Bridge? I think we could use you.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Right away.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Paris, are you still with me?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Sure am, Captain. I'm running the scans on those ships.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I'll work on the shields. I suggest you don't look at the viewscreen.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Oh, it's not even tempting.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: How's it going down here?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Not good. I can't get a response from anybody. It's like they're catatonic.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: It's the same all over the ship. On my way here, I must have seen fifty people just sitting, staring.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: A few minutes ago, there was a momentary interruption in the psionic field. Were there any indications that the alien somehow came on board?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I'll find out. Chakotay to Janeway. Chakotay to the Captain. Please respond. Chakotay to anyone on the Bridge. Kim, Paris, anybody. We may be the last ones left.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: What do we do?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I think we should take an escape pod. We passed an M Class planet yesterday. The pod should get us there in a week. We can try to get help.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: A week? That might be too late.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: It may be our only hope. If we stay here, we'll end up like the others.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: No, I have to keep trying to set up the resonance burst.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Do I have to give you an order?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I can't believe you're saying this. You know we have to stay here and try to help the others.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I want you with me.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: You aren't Chakotay.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I'm the Chakotay you want me to be. The one who loves you. This is what you want, isn't it? The secret you've been keeping? You want us to be together. And we can be.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I have to help the others.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I want you. I've always wanted you. You feel the same way too.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Yes.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Captain, I'm getting results from the scans. No apparent defensive weaknesses. Metallurgical analysis is inconclusive.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I can't remodulate the shields. Try moving us out of here. If we can get some distance between us and those ships, we might be able to block the effects.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Yes, ma'am.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: This time let's see if you can do it without causing an accident. You usually manage to make a mess of everything you do.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Let me say something I've always wanted to say. Get out of my life.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I'm just telling you what you already know. When the going gets tough, you crumble.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Not any more. Not any more.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: You don't really believe that. In your heart, you believe you'll fail again. And of course you will. You can't do anything right. You'll fail. Why even try?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Tom? Tom? Janeway to Engineering. Janeway to Torres. Are you there? Engineering respond. If anyone in Engineering can hear me, I'm on my way. Computer, put the Bridge controls on security lockout.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Deck eleven.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Now, maybe you have time to talk to me. You're so strong, Kath. That's one of the things I always loved in you.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: What's the matter? You used to love it when I kissed you there.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I don't know who you are, what you are, but I won't let you touch me.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: What about the man on the holodeck? You didn't seem to mind him touching you, did you? In fact, I think you liked it. Now I ask you, Kath, is that fair to me? I've stayed faithful to you. I've vowed to wait for you no matter how long it takes. Shouldn't you do the same?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I haven't been unfaithful.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Oh, Kath.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Sickbay to Engineering. Lieutenant Torres, please respond. Doctor to the mess hall. Mister Neelix, are you there? This is the doctor to anyone on the ship. If you can hear me, please reply. Either the communication system is malfunctioning or everyone on board has succumbed to a delusional state.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Except you and me.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: It would appear that if the psionic field is to be blocked and the crew restored to normal, it's up to us.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: You will have to go to Engineering and complete Lieutenant Torres's efforts to create a resonance burst.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I don't know how to do that.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I will assist you from here.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Do you know how to do it?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I discussed the matter with Lieutenant Torres. I think I understand the basic principle behind her plan. How hard can it be?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: All right.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Go to Engineering immediately. I'll contact you there.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Tom, what happened?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: A plasma leak caught me in the face. Help me.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Can you get to Sickbay? The Doctor is there.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Come with me.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I can't. I have to get to Engineering.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: You can't leave me like this. It hurts.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Tom, you can walk. You have to get to Sickbay on your own.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Kes, please. I can't.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: You don't want me to get to Engineering.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: No.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I'm hallucinating.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Kes, wait. Come back. Don't leave me! Come back!

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Finally. What took you so long?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Doctor, we have to set up this resonance burst as quickly as possible. I've started hallucinating.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Then see if Lieutenant Torres's last program is active.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I think I have it. B'Elanna was writing a program to open a symmetrical warp field.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: All right. You'll have to sequence the magnetic plasma constriction to the following formula. T equals C sub-one over theta times P sub-E.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Er, how do I do that?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I'm not sure. Wait a minute. I'll see if I can access Starfleet's interactive database.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Sweeting! Thank goodness I found you. Are you all right?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Where have you been?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: In the mess hall, trying to help the poor souls there.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Why didn't you answer the Doctor's hails?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I didn't hear them. The comm. system must be down. And frankly, I was a little busy. Ashmore thought I was a Kazon. Tried to kill me with a carving knife.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: How do I know you're really Neelix?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Who else would I be? Kes, all I want to do is protect you, to keep you safe. We have to get away from here, get to my shuttle.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Doctor, have you figured out how I can enter that sequencing code?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: It's quite simple, really. Do you know where the command module is?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Of course.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Activate it and select magnetic plasma sequencing.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: You're becoming annoying.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I've got it. It's activated. Now it's asking me to enter the core temperature.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Move away from that console.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Now, we need a temperature high enough to emit the resonance burst, but not so high as to irradiate everyone on the ship. Try three million Kelvins.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Kes, look at him.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: It hurts!

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Look at him. Focus.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I can't.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Yes, you can. The mirror, remember?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: It hurts too much!

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Kes, look at him.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: What's the matter, Kes? Can't lift your head?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Focus.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Stop it!

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I'm all right now, Doctor, and I've entered a temperature of three million Kelvin.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Then all you have to do is activate the warp field.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: All right. Here we go.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Kes to the Captain. If you can hear me, please report to Engineering.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: What happened?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: It's a long story, but I think everything's all right now.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Is that who's responsible for all this?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Apparently. He looks so harmless. It's hard to believe he almost destroyed us.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: You're a powerful little thing. I must say, you surprised me.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Why did you do this to us?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Because I can.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Is it just telepathy, or is there technology involved?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Does it matter?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Oh, it matters to me, because I don't intend to let you continue preying on others.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: How would you propose to stop me?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: We could destroy your technology. Or adjust your brain wave patterns to prevent telepathy. And then we could turn you over to the government of Mithren. We could even keep you confined in our brig behind a force field.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I'm sure you're very well-intentioned, Captain, and I'd like to be able to accommodate you but you see, I'm not really here. Captain's log, supplemental. We have no explanation for the mysterious disappearance of the telepathic alien. We can't even be certain that he was actually here. He seems to have left us with any number of unanswered questions.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I'm surprised to see you here, Captain. Isn't this the day that you're usually in the holodeck with your novel?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I thought, after our recent experience, that I'd take a break from fantasy for a while.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I don't blame you. I think it had quite an impact on all of us. Do you think it's true? That the alien was reading our minds, creating images from our own experiences?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: It seemed that way. He had uncanny ability to bring buried thoughts out into the open. Why?

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Oh, it's just, I experienced something I'd rather not admit.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I know. Me too. But, in a way, maybe he did us all a favor. Maybe it's better to look those feelings in the eye than to keep them locked up inside.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: I guess. I'll have to think about that. I have an early watch tomorrow, so I'd better turn in. Good night, Captain.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Good night, B'Elanna. Sweet dreams.

title: Persistence of Vision
line: Thanks. You too.

line: Anything?

title: Tattoo
line: Not really. The polyferranide deposits are contaminated with astaline.

title: Tattoo
line: Commander, there's something over here I think you should see.

title: Tattoo
line: Pack it up. We'll find better quality somewhere down the line.

title: Tattoo
line: That line is going to be cut short when our nacelles burn themselves up if we don't find it soon.

title: Tattoo
line: What have you got, Lieutenant?

title: Tattoo
line: There have been other visitors to this moon recently.

title: Tattoo
line: What do you think this is? Some kind of message?

title: Tattoo
line: I don't want you to go wandering off.

title: Tattoo
line: I'm not. I'm just looking at something.

title: Tattoo
line: Antonio.

title: Tattoo
line: He says you're quite a scout, a kep-o-ne.

title: Tattoo
line: I was just looking at a lizard when I saw it.

title: Tattoo
line: Well, it was your eyes that saw it. No one else's did. That's the important thing. Come. I want you to understand this. It's a blessing to the land, an ancient healing symbol. A chamozi. They probably cut this down for firewood.

title: Tattoo
line: The Rubber Tree People?

title: Tattoo
line: Well, the closest thing to the ancient Rubber Tree People that we'll ever see. The people in this tribe are their descendants, just like we are. But they never left this jungle, and they rarely intermarry with other tribes.

title: Tattoo
line: And they still use firewood instead of magnesite fuel like everyone else.

title: Tattoo
line: Chakotay, they have chosen to live like this for centuries. That's why we are traveling on foot and not using a transporter. We honor the Sky Spirits who led our ancestors to this sacred land.

title: Tattoo
line: Sacred land?

title: Tattoo
line: Yes.

title: Tattoo
line: Huh. The Sky Spirits must have taken a wrong turn somewhere.

title: Tattoo
line: Maybe it's a blessing to the land, for damaging it with the campfire.

title: Tattoo
line: What is your basis for that conclusion, Commander?

title: Tattoo
line: Oh, just something somebody told me once.

title: Tattoo
line: Describe the nature of your pain.

title: Tattoo
line: In the lower back. It's tight.

title: Tattoo
line: Choose the word that would best describe your pain. Burning, throbbing, piercing, pinching, biting, stinging, shooting

title: Tattoo
line: Shooting. It even goes down my legs.

title: Tattoo
line: Hmm.

title: Tattoo
line: Is the baby all right?

title: Tattoo
line: Hmm? Oh, certainly. Fine. Nothing to worry about.

title: Tattoo
line: Well, that makes me feel better.

title: Tattoo
line: The position of the baby is simply putting pressure on your sciatic nerve. You may return to your post.

title: Tattoo
line: The pain makes it difficult to sit for any period of time. It's really quite uncomfortable.

title: Tattoo
line: Elevating your legs when you sit should provide all the relief you need.

title: Tattoo
line: Perhaps a day of rest, off duty.

title: Tattoo
line: Mmm. Ensign Wildman, according to your medical history, this is your first pregnancy, correct?

title: Tattoo
line: Yes.

title: Tattoo
line: Well, Ensign, unfortunately, pregnancy causes its fair share of discomforts, and you'll have to learn to live with them. That's just the way it is. We'll schedule her for follow-up in two days. If the pain has not subsided on its own by then, we'll attempt to decrease the sensitivity of the nerve in that region.

title: Tattoo
line: Thank you, Doctor.

title: Tattoo
line: Call me day or night if this gets any worse.

title: Tattoo
line: Don't you have any compassion for the way she feels?

title: Tattoo
line: Every member of this crew is an adult. I will not coddle them. Compassion can be your department. Fortunately, you have enough for both of us.

title: Tattoo
line: You've never been sick or in pain. I just wish once in your life you could know what it's like, how it makes you feel vulnerable and a little afraid. Then you'd understand.

title: Tattoo
line: I don't have a life. I have a program.

title: Tattoo
line: I hated every minute of it. My father had dragged me all the way from our colony near the Cardassian border on this quest of his. Away from my friends, my home, and here we were in the middle of a brutal Central American jungle looking for the descendants of the ancient Rubber People.

title: Tattoo
line: It must have been very important to him.

title: Tattoo
line: Believe me, it was. And he was very disappointed that I didn't share his enthusiasm. He'd been tracking down the origins of our tribe for years.

title: Tattoo
line: The one on the right is the one I found today.

title: Tattoo
line: And now something you saw on that trip years ago shows up again on a moon's surface almost seventy thousand light years away. I don't suppose you have any theories that might explain this.

title: Tattoo
line: I can give you an official Rubber Tree People theory if you like. Sky Spirits.

title: Tattoo
line: Sky Spirits?

title: Tattoo
line: It's an ancient myth. Sky Spirits from above created the first Rubber People in their own image and led the way to a sacred land where the Rubber People would live for eternity.

title: Tattoo
line: You obviously don't put a great deal of faith in this explanation.

title: Tattoo
line: How much faith do you put in Adam and Eve? Hasn't science proved that all humans developed from a single evolutionary process?

title: Tattoo
line: That's what I was always taught. On the other hand, none of my teachers ever spent much time in the Delta Quadrant. B'Elanna tells me we've picked up a warp signature heading away from the moon. Think we should follow it?

title: Tattoo
line: I don't know that it's fair for me to put my own personal curiosity ahead of the ship's priorities.

title: Tattoo
line: We still haven't found the polyferranide we need to seal the warp coils. If these people have warp technology, they might be able to help us. Besides, we are in the business of exploring, aren't we?

title: Tattoo
line: My father would put on his expedition hat and shout, let's go. I guess that's good enough for me.

title: Tattoo
line: Showing no life signs.

title: Tattoo
line: Mister Paris, are you certain the warp signature ended here?

title: Tattoo
line: Positive, Captain. Harry, check your sensors. That look like some kind of power source to you?

title: Tattoo
line: That is an unusually high EM reading for a natural occurrence.

title: Tattoo
line: Could be some kind of cloaking technology.

title: Tattoo
line: Mister Kim, transmit a continuous message on all frequencies identifying who we are, where we're from, and make it clear our intentions are peaceful.

title: Tattoo
line: Torres to Bridge.

title: Tattoo
line: Go Ahead.

title: Tattoo
line: We're in luck, Captain.

title: Tattoo
line: My readings are showing high concentrations of polyferranide about ten kilometers below the surface.

title: Tattoo
line: Acknowledged. We'll send down an away team to continue the survey. Report to Transporter room three.

title: Tattoo
line: On my way.

title: Tattoo
line: Commander, if we meet any resistance, abort the mission. I have no intention of disturbing an alien race that would rather be left alone.

title: Tattoo
line: Understood.

title: Tattoo
line: On the other hand, if we can make contact, our goal is to get permission to begin excavation as soon as possible.

title: Tattoo
line: Tuvok, you're with me. Mister Neelix, please report to Transporter room three for an away mission.

title: Tattoo
line: I'll meet you there, Commander.

title: Tattoo
line: We may be out of luck.

title: Tattoo
line: Problem?

title: Tattoo
line: I'm not sure we can transport down. Every time we try to lock onto a transport site, a storm begins.

title: Tattoo
line: Storm?

title: Tattoo
line: We've tried seven different sites and as soon as we lock on, an electrical storm forms right above the location. When we change sites, a new storm forms and the old one dissipates.

title: Tattoo
line: Might the transporter beam itself be causing an electrostatic charge in the atmosphere?

title: Tattoo
line: That's as good a guess as any. I can't explain it. We just can't transport.

title: Tattoo
line: Fine. We'll take a shuttle.

title: Tattoo
line: Once again, the storm seems to have formed as a direct result of our interaction with the atmosphere. The meteorological conditions changed radically when we began our entry sequence.

title: Tattoo
line: Shields are holding.

title: Tattoo
line: It takes more than a little thunderstorm to bother one of your mighty Starfleet ships, huh?

title: Tattoo
line: Nothing we can't handle. Relax, Neelix.

title: Tattoo
line: That's why they call it a rain forest.

title: Tattoo
line: Why do your Sky Spirits choose a place where it rains all the time? And it's hot, and there are so many bugs.

title: Tattoo
line: It's said the Sky Spirits honored the land above all else. Maybe it's because this land yields so many different kinds of life. Maybe they wanted us to become friends with everything in nature, including the bugs.

title: Tattoo
line: Sorry, Sky Spirits, I will never make friends with bugs.

title: Tattoo
line: Maybe that's why they keep biting you. You're miserable. It was a mistake to bring you. I'm sorry.

title: Tattoo
line: I'm sorry I can't be what you want me to be.

title: Tattoo
line: From the day you came out of your mother, upside down, I knew the Spirits had chosen you to be a contrary.

title: Tattoo
line: No one chooses for me. I choose my own way. And if that makes me a contrary, I'll have to live with it.

title: Tattoo
line: If you have no spirits to guide you, I fear you will lose your way.

title: Tattoo
line: Altitude, five thousand meters.

title: Tattoo
line: Decreasing speed to seven hundred twenty kph. Entering terminal approach phase.

title: Tattoo
line: Visibility still zero. Switching to enhanced terrain scanning.

title: Tattoo
line: Touchdown site scanned. Continuing descent.

line: Computer, activate the Emergency Medical Holographic program.

title: Tattoo
line: Please state the nature of the medical emergency.

title: Tattoo
line: I thought we changed your program so you wouldn't have to say that anymore.

title: Tattoo
line: We did. But I became so uncomfortable trying to find new ways to break the ice, as it were, that I restored it. Let's just say it works for me.

title: Tattoo
line: Doctor.

title: Tattoo
line: Ah, you noticed.

title: Tattoo
line: Are holograms supposed to sneeze?

title: Tattoo
line: Generally, no, but I have accepted your challenge. I've programmed myself with the symptoms of a twenty nine hour Levodian flu. Thus, I will gain the experience that you suggest would be beneficial to the performance of my duties. A-choo.1 Holographic tissue paper for the holographic running nose. Don't offer them to patients. Hmm. Interesting sensation, blowing one's nose. It's my first time.

title: Tattoo
line: I think this is very brave of you.

title: Tattoo
line: Nothing of the sort. I intend it to be an educational experience.

title: Tattoo
line: I'm sure you'll learn a lot.

title: Tattoo
line: I meant for the crew. I'm tired of the whiny, cranky attitudes we see around here. I intend to serve as an example of how one's life and duties do not have to be disrupted by simple illness.

title: Tattoo
line: Doc, I don't feel so good.

title: Tattoo
line: Neither do I, and you don't hear me complaining.

title: Tattoo
line: We are not making any progress locating the source of that unusual power reading, Commander.

title: Tattoo
line: Then I guess we'll have to search for these people the old fashioned way, with our eyes and ears.

title: Tattoo
line: Is something bothering you, Commander?

title: Tattoo
line: No. It just reminds me of another jungle that I visited once. The Central American rain forest on Earth. It's the only other place in the universe that I've ever seen this flower.

title: Tattoo
line: It appears to be a rare variety of Cypripedium, of the Asiatic genus Paphiopedilum.

title: Tattoo
line: I never knew you had such horticultural expertise, Mister Vulcan.

title: Tattoo
line: In fact, I am, or more accurately I was, a breeder of prize Vulcan orchids.

title: Tattoo
line: Then we have something in common. I breed orchids too. Don't they make the most exquisite salad? A touch of Baldoxic vinegar, pure heaven.

title: Tattoo
line: I hereby designate the two of you the team's botanical surveyors. Collect a sample of that flower. B'Elanna?

title: Tattoo
line: It's just what we've been looking for. Almost pure polyferranide. But there's a problem with crust reactivity. If we can't solve it before excavation, we might contaminate the entire yield.

title: Tattoo
line: Have Ensign Kim run an analysis from the ship. We should be able to.

title: Tattoo
line: I'll be damned.

title: Tattoo
line: What?

title: Tattoo
line: It almost looks like a hawk, doesn't it?

title: Tattoo
line: Listen to him, Chakotay. What does he say to you? He says, you are home, eh?

title: Tattoo
line: I'm leaving the tribe, Father.

title: Tattoo
line: What?

title: Tattoo
line: I got to know a lot of the Starfleet officers patrolling the Cardassian border. I asked Captain Sulu if he would sponsor me at Starfleet Academy.

title: Tattoo
line: And he would do such a thing without even discussing it with me?

title: Tattoo
line: I told him I had your approval.

title: Tattoo
line: Ah.

title: Tattoo
line: I kept him as far away from you as I could.

title: Tattoo
line: I take it you've been accepted by the Academy? Well, you've never fully embraced the traditions of our tribe, I know that. And you've always been curious about other societies, and that is why I allowed you to read about them. Because I believe that ignorance is our greatest enemy. But to leave the tribe?

title: Tattoo
line: Our tribe lives in the past. A past of fantasy and myth.

title: Tattoo
line: That past is a part of you, no matter how hard you try to reject it.

title: Tattoo
