title: Alliances
line: Actually that's a good idea.

title: Alliances
line: You've got to be kidding!

title: Alliances
line: Not at all. Seska has been trying to forge an alliance among the Kazon. She would jump at the chance to get our support.

title: Alliances
line: She's right. If we went through Seska at least we could ally ourselves with the Nistrim.

title: Alliances
line: I think it's a bad idea.

title: Alliances
line: You can't have it both ways Commander. If you want to get in the mud with the Kazon you can't start complaining that you might get dirty.

title: Alliances
line: Fine. I'll talk with Seska.

title: Alliances
line: No, you've been through too much with her. Mister Neelix, prepare to take your shuttle to Sobras. In the meantime, I'll make contact with Seska. Dismissed.

title: Alliances
line: Captain's log, stardate 49337.4. After sending a subspace message to Seska and the Nistrim Maje Culluh, we have received a quick response.

title: Alliances
line: Captain Janeway, Commander Chakotay, I must say we were surprised to hear from you.

title: Alliances
line: Are you willing to meet with us?

title: Alliances
line: You've made an interesting proposal. I've discussed it with Seska and she assures me that you would not make this gesture unless you were sincere. I will talk with you.

title: Alliances
line: I suggest we rendezvous. We'll transmit coordinates to you.

title: Alliances
line: If you don't mind, Captain, we'd prefer to choose the coordinates.

title: Alliances
line: Fine. Transmit them to us.

title: Alliances
line: We'll meet in approximately twenty hours. I must say, Captain, I look forward to this opportunity.

title: Alliances
line: Hello my friends. Please, don't let me interrupt. I was hoping to find my good friend Jal Tersa here. Has he been in tonight?

title: Alliances
line: Thank you. Tersa, my friend!

title: Alliances
line: It could be dangerous, sneaking up on a man like that.

title: Alliances
line: I'd never dream of sneaking up on you, but you were so engrossed in whatever it is you're doing.

title: Alliances
line: A puzzle. What brings you here, Talaxian?

title: Alliances
line: I'm good at puzzles, perhaps I can help?

title: Alliances
line: The dancer showed it to me. By moving only two rods this dodecahedron can become an icosahedron. She said she'd spend the night with the man who could solve it.

title: Alliances
line: Oh, a splendid motivation, to be sure. I might just be able to make your night a memorable one.

title: Alliances
line: You know how to solve this?

title: Alliances
line: I might, if you'll hear me out first. My fortunes have changed since we last met, Tersa. I've become a person of some influence aboard a starship known as Voyager.

title: Alliances
line: You must think us very isolated. Everyone knows that. It's probably the only reason you were allowed in here. Especially after last time.

title: Alliances
line: A simple misunderstanding. Tersa, I know you have the ear of your First Maje, as I do with our Captain. We could be quite useful to both of them.

title: Alliances
line: Go on.

title: Alliances
line: My Captain is interested in talking to your Maje, to discuss a possible alliance. Do you think he'd have any interest in such a meeting?

title: Alliances
line: An alliance? Between the Kazon Pommar and the Federations?

title: Alliances
line: An interesting thought, isn't it?

title: Alliances
line: You're coming with us.

title: Alliances
line: Tersa! Explain to them we're friends!

title: Alliances
line: I have no idea who this person is. Some lunatic who sat down and started babbling.

title: Alliances
line: I guess you'll be spending the night alone.

title: Alliances
line: You've made a good choice. The Nistrim will be a potent ally.

title: Alliances
line: We want to make sure the Nistrim will also be an honorable ally. That you'll adhere to the conditions we establish. You can let all the Kazon factions know that Voyager has formed a coalition with you and will be an ally to any Nistrim ship or outpost we encounter. In addition, we're prepared to provide emergency supplies when needed. Food, medicine, clothing.

title: Alliances
line: What we will not provide is any of our technology or weaponry.

title: Alliances
line: Understood. Just one other detail. An exchange of crewmembers.

title: Alliances
line: An exchange?

title: Alliances
line: Yes. I'm sure you'll agree that our alliance should represent a genuine partnership.

title: Alliances
line: Perhaps you should define that.

title: Alliances
line: It's obvious. Federation crew on my ship, Nistrim crew on yours.

title: Alliances
line: Maje, I think that's a detail we could work out later.

title: Alliances
line: I can assure you that I would never agree to that.

title: Alliances
line: It seems a natural extension of your own proposal.

title: Alliances
line: We don't have to decide everything right now.

title: Alliances
line: I will determine what we decide, and when.

title: Alliances
line: Yes, Maje.

title: Alliances
line: I won't have a woman dictate terms to me.

title: Alliances
line: Culluh, I found the idea of an alliance with you distasteful. I was willing to explore the possibility, but now I see my instincts were dead on.

title: Alliances
line: Talk to her. Tell her to be reasonable.

title: Alliances
line: This meeting is over.

title: Alliances
line: Once your Maje learns I'm being imprisoned he'll be outraged!

title: Alliances
line: Hurry up.

title: Alliances
line: He won't look kindly on anyone who's made such a egregius error. What are you charging me with? How long will I be held?

title: Alliances
line: Go.

title: Alliances
line: Well, I assume you'll at least let me confer with counsel. I have the ability to reward handsomely anyone who shows me a bit of understanding. Is that a baby?

title: Alliances
line: My name is Neelix. I'm Talaxian.

title: Alliances
line: I'm Mabus. My friends and I are Trabe. They hurt you.

title: Alliances
line: I wasn't walking quickly enough for them.

title: Alliances
line: Let's get the bleeding stopped, then I'll clean it.

title: Alliances
line: Why are they holding you?

title: Alliances
line: They seem to be detaining anyone who isn't Kazon. Several of our group have been taken for questioning, but so far none of them have come back.

title: Alliances
line: How long have you been here?

title: Alliances
line: Five days. They attacked us in space. Twenty of our group died. We've lost nine more since they put us in prison, including most of the governing council. I'm the only one left.

title: Alliances
line: The Kazon won't be satisfied until you've all been annihilated.

title: Alliances
line: If we've learned anything, it's how to survive. Did you notice how many guards they have posted at the entrance to the prison?

title: Alliances
line: Only two. I guess they assume this place is so secure that they don't need anymore. Why do you ask?

title: Alliances
line: We don't plan to sit here while they kill us one by one. We were able to get a message through to another Trabe vessel before we were boarded. Help is on the way. Can we count on you?

title: Alliances
line: Captain's log, supplemental. We're on our way to rendezvous with Mister Neelix. I can only hope that he had more luck with the Kazon than we did.

title: Alliances
line: Captain, we're approaching the coordinates.

title: Alliances
line: All stop.

title: Alliances
line: I don't see any trace of him.

title: Alliances
line: Long range sensors indicate no sign of Mister Neelix's shuttle within a radius of two light years.

title: Alliances
line: The Kazon have him.

title: Alliances
line: We cannot jump to conclusions. He may simply have been delayed.

title: Alliances
line: We'll hold position here for two hours. If he hasn't shown up by then, we'll go to Sobras.

title: Alliances
line: Lieutenant, could you fill us in a little? Well, there are all kinds of rumors flying around about what's going on with the Kazon.

title: Alliances
line: Nothing's going on yet. The Captain's talk with Seska fell apart pretty quickly.

title: Alliances
line: Nothings going to come of all this. B'Elanna, you were Seska's friend. Couldn't you get word to her, try to work things out?

title: Alliances
line: No, I couldn't.

title: Alliances
line: I don't understand how.

title: Alliances
line: Hogan, it's gone too far. Seska isn't the person we thought she was. I don't trust her any more.

title: Alliances
line: Even if it means us getting home in one piece? Or do you agree with our Captain that holding on to our technology is worth dying for.

title: Alliances
line: Who are you to be second guessing Captain Janeway? The hardest thing you have to think worry is keeping that dilithium chamber filled. She os doing the best she can to get us home and if you don't like the way she's doing it, I really don't want to hear about it. Is that clear?

title: Alliances
line: Perfectly.

title: Alliances
line: Some of the children are too weak to run. We'll have to carry them. We can use another pair of strong arms.

title: Alliances
line: You can count on me.

title: Alliances
line: I can't promise we'll get out of here alive, but if we stay here we'll die anyway.

title: Alliances
line: I'd rather go out fighting, myself.

title: Alliances
line: That one might be a problem. He's the kind who'll start shooting at the first sign of trouble.

title: Alliances
line: I'll keep an eye on him.

title: Alliances
line: This may be it. Be ready. Stay back.

title: Alliances
line: Get back against the walls.

title: Alliances
line: Now! Let's go! Let's go! Come on! Come on, everyone! Let's go. Come on, out. Let's go. Come on. Nice work, my friends. Let's go.

title: Alliances
line: All right, that's it. We're going after him. Mister Paris, set a course for Sobras, full impulse.

title: Alliances
line: Aye, Captain.

title: Alliances
line: Tuvok, arm the phaser banks and load the forward torpedo bays. We don't know what the Kazon have in store for us.

title: Alliances
line: Shields at full power.

title: Alliances
line: Yellow alert, all hands at the ready.

title: Alliances
line: Captain.

title: Alliances
line: What is it?

title: Alliances
line: Ships. Kazon ships on long range sensors, closing fast.

title: Alliances
line: Confirmed, Captain.

title: Alliances
line: On screen.

title: Alliances
line: It appears to be an armada, and the weapons are powered.

title: Alliances
line: Red alert!

title: Alliances
line: Power all weapons systems and stand ready. Mister Kim, hail the lead ship.

title: Alliances
line: They're hailing us, Captain. I'll put it on screen.

title: Alliances
line: Hello, Captain. I'd like you to meet my good friend Mabus. We've just escaped from the Kazon Pommar.

title: Alliances
line: What are you doing on a Kazon ship?

title: Alliances
line: They're Trabe vessels, actually. Everything the Kazon have, they stole from the Trabe. Mabus will tell you all about it over a sumptuous dinner. The food hasn't been very good where we've been.

title: Alliances
line: I look forward to it.

title: Alliances
line: I was eight years old when it started. I wasn't even particularly aware of the Kazon. They lived in restricted areas that children weren't allowed to go near. I didn't know they lived in poverty and filth. I didn't know they were persecuted by the Trabe police. I was told they were violent and dangerous, and had to be kept isolated so they wouldn't get loose and kill us. Which is exactly what they did, but we brought it on ourselves. The Trabe treated them like animals, fenced them in, encouraged them to fight amongst themselves so they wouldn't turn on us, and sat by while they turned into a violent, angry army. When they finally realized we were their true enemy, we didn't stand a chance. I was luckier than most. A friend's father grabbed me and took me with his family to one of the starships that managed to escape. I can still remember it happened so fast. One minute I was a happy child playing in a field, the next an orphan exiled in space.

title: Alliances
line: It strikes me that in many ways we're in the same predicament. Separated from the lives we knew, searching for a home.

title: Alliances
line: A goal you may well achieve, Captain, but the Kazon have refused to allow us to find a new homeworld. Every time we try to settle somewhere, they attack and drive us away. We're scattered, like nomads, with no home and little hope.

title: Alliances
line: It happened over thirty years ago and the Kazon are still trying to punish you?

title: Alliances
line: Remarkable, isn't it? Most of the Trabe who persecuted the Kazon are either dead or old men by now. Most of us were children when the uprising occurred, and our children are innocent, but the Kazon's desire for revenge is as strong as ever.

title: Alliances
line: How can you transmit to us without your crew knowing it?

title: Alliances
line: Well, that's for me to worry about. Let's just say I'm very familiar with communications protocols. Now, will you let me talk to Seska?

title: Alliances
line: Not without some proof you can be trusted.

title: Alliances
line: She and I knew each other for a long time. She knows that I can be trusted. Just let me talk to her.

title: Alliances
line: I'll convey your message. Contact me tomorrow and I'll let you know if she's willing to talk to you.

title: Alliances
line: Before the uprising, the Trabe were known as a highly evolved species. They produced scholars and artists who were widely admired and their technology was among the finest in the quadrant. No one really knew about the Kazon and how they were being treated.

title: Alliances
line: Why not? Holding another culture in virtual slavery isn't the kind of thing that could go unnoticed.

title: Alliances
line: You have to understand. The Trabe were rich and powerful. They manipulated information about the conditions on their planet. And no one wanted to risk offending them, and losing opportunities for trade.

title: Alliances
line: It seems to me that they've learned their lesson. Mabus and his people have freely acknowledged that they were responsible for what happened to them.

title: Alliances
line: Still, I do not see that it is a particularly good idea to form an alliance with the blood enemies of the Kazon. We risk uniting all the factions against us.

title: Alliances
line: The only thing the Kazon agree on now is that we are their common enemy. It's hard to imagine it getting much worse.

title: Alliances
line: The Trabe have a lot of ships and a lot of weapons in that convoy. I think this alliance would be better than none at all.

title: Alliances
line: I'd rather not be in the position of making an alliance at all, but that may be a luxury we simply don't have. My gut tells me we don't have any friends among the Kazon. As for the Trabe, I believe that people have a capacity to change. It's always been Starfleet's policy to deal with new species on a basis of openness and trust until proven otherwise.

title: Alliances
line: Captain, I'm glad to see you. I want to thank you for the use of your medical facilities. We have very few doctors.

title: Alliances
line: Everyone seems to be in generally good condition. Malnutrition is the most common problem, but it's easily alleviated with bio-nutrient supplements.

title: Alliances
line: Thank you, Doctor. How much longer do you need?

title: Alliances
line: I'd say less than an hour.

title: Alliances
line: Will you walk with me?

title: Alliances
line: Of course.

title: Alliances
line: I've been thinking about our conversation at dinner, about the things we share, and it seems to me we could be of mutual benefit to each other.

title: Alliances
line: Go on.

title: Alliances
line: What would you say to the possibility of our joining forces. My starship and your convoy.

title: Alliances
line: It clearly would be a stronger force if we did that.

title: Alliances
line: We could travel together for as long as it's advantageous to both of us. Maybe we'll find our way out of Kazon territory and you could settle on a new home world.

title: Alliances
line: It's a reasonable idea Captain. I have no objection. But it would only benefit your group and mine. There are other Trabe who wouldn't enjoy the same protection. I wonder if you might consider a somewhat more bold plan.

title: Alliances
line: Tell me.

title: Alliances
line: Together, the Voyager and the Trabe would be a force to be reckoned with. Suppose we took advantage of that and asked the representatives of all the Kazon factions to join us at the bargaining table.

title: Alliances
line: In order to achieve what?

title: Alliances
line: Peace. Together we would represent a stabilizing force in this corner of the quadrant. Bring the factions together, convince them that an end to violence would be in everyone's best interest. Think about it. I believe it could work.

title: Alliances
line: It's a message from Voyager. They've formed an alliance with the Trabe!

title: Alliances
line: The Trabe?

title: Alliances
line: They're calling for a conference of all first Majes. How could this have happened?

title: Alliances
line: It happened because you let Voyager slip away right into the hands of the Trabe, by insisting on that ridiculous exchange of crews!

title: Alliances
line: I could not let the negotiations be dictated by that woman!

title: Alliances
line: That's becoming a tired refrain, Culluh. One day that attitude will be your undoing.

title: Alliances
line: Watch your tongue.

title: Alliances
line: Or what? I'm carrying your child. I don't think you'd do anything to jeopardize him. We can still turn this to our advantage. We have a crewman on Voyager who's willing to provide information to us. There's long term potential in that arrangement. We mustn't lose sight of it.

title: Alliances
line: You're not suggesting we go to this conference? That we come running like a Calogan dog when the Federations call?

title: Alliances
line: Could you risk being the only Maje who doesn't attend? Of course you'll go, and listen. Nothing should be negotiated there, not at the point of a Federation weapon. But you can learn a great deal. Assess the mood of the other Majes, find out the strength of the Trabe convoy.

title: Alliances
line: You may be right.

title: Alliances
line: You can come out of this a hero. You can use this conference to unite the factions, eradicate the Trabe once and for all, and take Voyager as a trophy.

title: Alliances
line: Captain's log, stardate 49342.5. Neelix has returned from Sobras where he learned a disturbing piece of information that may require us to rethink our plans.

title: Alliances
line: He was a Takrit, a band of mercenaries that operates in this system,

title: Alliances
line: What was he doing when the Kazon Pommar arrested him?

title: Alliances
line: My contact on the planet said that he was making a sketch of the conference site, and believe me the Takrid are not known for their art.

title: Alliances
line: Who sent him?

title: Alliances
line: That's as much information as I got.

title: Alliances
line: So someone wants to sabotage this conference.

title: Alliances
line: One of the Majes.

title: Alliances
line: Why miss a chance to wipe out your rivals while they're together in one room?

title: Alliances
line: If that is true, then one of them will undoubtedly try to leave before the meeting is finished.

title: Alliances
line: Captain, I think you should consider not going to the conference.

title: Alliances
line: No. If I can help bring stability to this quadrant, I'm not going to walk away because of a rumor.

title: Alliances
line: A rumor that must be taken seriously nonetheless.

title: Alliances
line: Agreed. Commander, monitor all the Kazon vessels carefully, and look out for any suspicious ship movement near the surface. Keep us on a constant transporter lock so we can beam out at the first hint of trouble. Tuvok, Neelix, you're with me.

title: Alliances
line: I gave a great deal of thought to the shape of the table. I finally decided on a triangle. Your group will sit on one side, the Majes will occupy the other two. Does that seem appropriate?

title: Alliances
line: Have you heard anything more about the matter we discussed?

title: Alliances
line: Don't talk about that here. It could mean my head. Does the table shape seem acceptable?

title: Alliances
line: Tersa, this time I am here with a powerful starship. You'd better be telling me everything you know.

title: Alliances
line: I am, I swear. I want to thank you for making it possible to have the conference here on Sobras. My Maje has rewarded me handsomely for the prestige it affords him. If there is any further way I can be of service, please let me know.

title: Alliances
line: He hasn't heard anything more, but he's frightened. He must believe something's going to happen.

title: Alliances
line: The First Majes of the Kazon Order. Minnis of the Pommar. Surat of the Mostral. Loran of the Hobii. Valek of the Oglamar. And Culluh of the Nistrim.

title: Alliances
line: Captain. We seem destined to encounter each other.

title: Alliances
line: This is Mabus, a governor of the Trabe.

title: Alliances
line: Maje Culluh. I'm gratified to be meeting you like this. I hope we'll be able to come to terms.

title: Alliances
line: I never thought I'd see the day when any of us would sit at a table with the Trabe.

title: Alliances
line: Times change, Maje.

title: Alliances
line: Perhaps.

title: Alliances
line: Shall we?

title: Alliances
line: Our gracious host Jal Minnis has provided food and drink to make our discussions more pleasant.

title: Alliances
line: We appreciate your coming. We hope this will lead to a new climate of peace.

title: Alliances
line: Peace? With the Trabe? Forgive me if I'm a bit skeptical.

title: Alliances
line: I understand. After decades of antagonism you're bound to be suspicious. But surely everyone here is tired of constant violence.

title: Alliances
line: Aren't you really trying to get us to relax our guard so the Trabe can conquer us again?

title: Alliances
line: How can we do that? We're scattered and disparate. All we ask for is a chance to find a new homeworld and settle peacefully.

title: Alliances
line: Excuse me.

title: Alliances
line: Captain Janeway, I'm curious as to the nature of this alliance you've struck with the Trabe. Especially since you refused my offer of a similar pact.

title: Alliances
line: I found the goals of the Trabe to be compatible with our own. I represent an organization which is devoted to peaceful co-existence among people. The Trabe want nothing more than that.

title: Alliances
line: The Trabe have always wanted peace for themselves, but we paid the price. They lived in luxury and we lived in squalor and misery.

title: Alliances
line: What I fear, Captain, is that this union you've made with the Trabe is an effort to force us to capitulate. If so, we assure you, it is doomed to failure.

title: Alliances
line: I won't pretend that our alliance wasn't an attempt to make a show of strength. Separately, we and the Trabe are vulnerable. Together, we are stronger.

title: Alliances
line: Are you threatening us, Captain?

title: Alliances
line: It is important that you understand our determination, but it's not a threat, it's an offer. A negotiated peace among all of us would provide a greater stability in this quadrant. How could that do anything but benefit us all?

title: Alliances
line: I can't speak for all of you, but I for one don't think we can trust this proposal. A woman and a Trabe. How can we listen to them? I find you nothing but a hypocrite, Captain, allying yourselves to the greatest villains this quadrant has ever known. If this is where your revered Federation values have taken you, I want no part of it.

title: Alliances
line: Gentlemen. Allow me to confer with my Federation colleagues. Please, have some refreshments and let us continue in a few moments. Captain, would you please join me?

title: Alliances
line: Captain, I really need to talk to you now!

title: Alliances
line: Get down!

title: Alliances
line: What is this, Captain?

title: Alliances
line: It's a trap! Take cover!

title: Alliances
line: Voyager, red alert!

title: Alliances
line: We're on it.

title: Alliances
line: You've ruined what would have been the greatest step towards peace in decades.

title: Alliances
line: Peace? A massacre?

title: Alliances
line: I could have decimated the Kazon leadership. It would have taken them years to recover.

title: Alliances
line: You planned this whole thing and used our good will to make sure you were successful.

title: Alliances
line: You don't know the Kazon. There's no dealing with them. Violence is all they understand.

title: Alliances
line: Or perhaps it's all you understand.

title: Alliances
line: You're naive, Captain. It's clear you have no understanding of the harsh realities of this part of space. What I tried to do was done as much for you as it was for us.

title: Alliances
line: I'm not grateful, and I want you off my ship. Chief, beam our former guest back to his vessel.

title: Alliances
line: Captain, don't do this. You're going to need us.

title: Alliances
line: I don't think so.

title: Alliances
line: The Kazon will be determined to seek revenge. How can this one ship hope to survive?

title: Alliances
line: Not by making deals with executioners. Energize.

title: Alliances
line: I would suggest we depart before the Kazon have a chance to return to their ships.

title: Alliances
line: Janeway to Paris. Get us out of here.

title: Alliances
line: Aye, Captain.

title: Alliances
line: There's no question we're more vulnerable now than ever. We have to take every measure to make sure we're prepared for an attack. I want continual diagnostics on all ship's systems.

title: Alliances
line: I will schedule additional battle drills for all hands.

title: Alliances
line: Mister Neelix, what about our food supplies?

title: Alliances
line: We're in good shape, Captain. We shouldn't have to stop anywhere for several weeks.

title: Alliances
line: Good. Lieutenant, what's the condition of our propulsion systems?

title: Alliances
line: We have a reasonable supply of anti-matter. Barring any major problems, we should have maximum performance of both warp and impulse engines.

title: Alliances
line: There's just one more thing I want to say. I hope there's a lesson for all of us in this. Although some of the species we've encountered here have been peaceful, others seem governed only by their own self-interests. This appears to be a region of space that doesn't have many rules. But I believe we can learn something from the events that have unfolded. In a part of space where there are few rules, it's more important than ever that we hold fast to our own. In a region where shifting allegiances are commonplace we have to have something stable to rely on. And we do. The principles and ideals of the Federation. As far as I'm concerned, those are the best allies we could have.

title: Threshold

title: Threshold
line: More coffee? Ah, you look like a happy bunch.

title: Threshold
line: We've hit a wall.

title: Threshold
line: Oh. Well, maybe I can help.

title: Threshold
line: Great. Do you know anything about quantum warp theory or multi-spectral subspace engine design?

title: Threshold
line: No. But I'm a quick study. What are we working on?

title: Threshold
line: Do you have anything to eat?

title: Threshold
line: Sure. There's some Kalavian biscuits, somewhere in the kitchen.

title: Threshold
line: I guess I'll go find them myself. Fill him in.

title: Threshold
line: What are you saying? I'm not smart enough? I'll have you know I did two years as an engineer's assistant aboard a Trabalian freighter. I'm well-versed in warp theory.

title: Threshold

title: Meld

line: I could be. Just like Suder. You know, Captain, I don't mind telling you something the other Tuvok never would. You are wrong. Sparing Suder's life is a sign of weakness. You disgust me. All you humans do. Admit it! Part of you feels as I do. Part of you wants him to die for what he did.

title: Meld
line: Liar! He has killed and you know he deserves to die! On behalf of the victim's family, Captain, I beg you to reconsider. Give them the satisfaction of his execution. title: Meld
line: You'll be all right, Tuvok. This'll be over in thirty seconds.

title: Meld

title: Meld

title: Meld

title: Meld

title: Meld
line: It's over.

line: He might be able to fool the sensors. Sedate him again. Computer, remove the forcefield.

title: Meld
line: I wish I knew, Captain. In a sense, Mister Tuvok's mind is fighting a classic battle between good and evil. The battle may be won in a day, a year, or it may never be won.

line: Tuvok? I wondered what happened to you. They wouldn't tell me anything.

title: Meld

title: Meld

title: Meld

title: Meld

title: Meld

title: Meld

title: Meld
line: I will take no comfort in this.

title: Meld
line: A most logical use of violence, to punish the violent.

title: Meld
line: We both know that I am prepared to die, but are you prepared to kill?

title: Meld
line: It needs to be done.

title: Meld
line: To release your violent impulses?

title: Meld
line: To serve justice.

title: Meld
line: Justice or vengeance? Understand one thing, Tuvok. I can promise you this will not silent your demons. If you can't control the violence, the violence controls you. Be prepared to yield your entire being to it, to sacrifice your place in civilized life for you will no longer be a part of it, and there's no return.

title: Meld
line: I seek no return!

title: Meld
line: Of course, you would not be able to live with yourself. Then we are both to die, and that will end the torment.

title: Meld

line: There is no reason to be afraid. I will take care of you now and see that you get home safely.

title: Innocence
line: Captain's log, supplemental. I've sent out scouting parties to analyze the mineral deposits in the moons around Drayan Two. Meanwhile, I've arranged to meet with the planet's leader.

title: Innocence
line: According to Neelix, nobody's had direct contact with the Drayans for decades. All he's heard are rumors.

title: Innocence

title: Innocence
line: That's something. Deck four. My diplomacy professor used to say the opening twenty minutes of a first contact situation are the most crucial.

title: Innocence
line: I'd feel better about this particular twenty minutes if we had some idea what to expect.

title: Innocence
line: Sometimes you have to go in blind. That's the exciting part. When I was a science officer I always envied the Captain's privilege of making first contact with new races.

title: Innocence
line: I envied it so much I almost got myself shipped back to the academy for remedial training. On my first assignment we were sent to make contact with the Tarkannans. When we came face to face with the Tarkannan delegation I very proudly made the traditional gesture for hello, not realizing that males and females of their race use different styles of movement, and I was actually propositioning the Ambassador.

title: Innocence

title: Innocence
line: I'm Captain Kathryn Janeway. I'd like to welcome you aboard the Federation Starship Voyager.

title: Innocence
line: First Prelate Alcia. May this day find you at peace and leave you with hope. That's a traditional blessing from our ancient scrolls.

title: Innocence
line: Om-nah-hoo-pez-nyeetz. That's from the spirits of my people. It means, peace in your heart, fortune in your steps.

title: Innocence

title: Innocence
line: We don't often engage in dialogue with alien races, but your story of crossing the galaxy intrigued me.

title: Innocence
line: I'd be glad to tell you all about our journey and my crew. Perhaps you'd like to see more of our ship as well.

title: Innocence

title: Innocence
line: Our warp core is designed to operate for up to three years before refueling.

title: Innocence

title: Innocence
line: I'm sorry my Chief Engineer isn't here to meet you. She's leading one of the away teams surveying the moons around Drayan.

title: Innocence
line: I find it interesting that you chose this to show me first. Do your people consider advanced technology to be their highest achievement?

title: Innocence
line: Not as an end in itself. The purpose of all this is to help up gain knowledge about the universe and the people in it.

title: Innocence
line: Our ancestors were brilliant scientists and engineers. They were continually developing better, smarter, more efficient machines, until the technology became more important than the people. I believe our society would have self-destructed if it weren't for the reformation. My great-grandfather helped to return us to ourselves, and since that time we've remained isolated to avoid the influence of those who might lead us back down the wrong path.

title: Innocence
line: Some human cultures have done the same.

title: Innocence
line: Will your friend be all right in there?

title: Innocence
line: Yes. I have secured his body within a stasis field. You were all very fortunate to have escaped the crash with only a few bruises.

title: Innocence
line: The attendants protected us.

title: Innocence
line: Can't you fix it?

title: Innocence
line: I believe so. However, I am more concerned with getting through the electrodynamic turbulence in the ionosphere.

title: Innocence
line: What's electro-turbulence?

title: Innocence
line: A thermal inversion gradient is causing unusually strong and unpredictable currents in the upper levels of the atmosphere. Those currents caused my shuttle to crash, and I assume yours as well. I must find a way to safely navigate through the turbulence before we can attempt to leave.

title: Innocence
line: Will that take a long time?

title: Innocence
line: It may. You must be patient.

title: Innocence
line: I don't want to stay here any more. I don't like it here.

line: Your displeasure doesn't change our situation. Nor does it bring us any closer to a solution

title: Innocence
line: It isn't my intention to be mean. I only wish to provide you with a realistic assessment. Vulcan parents never shield their children from the truth. Doing so would only hinder their ability to cope with inevitable difficulties.

line: I'm hungry.

line: There is a supply of Starfleet rations in the shuttle.

title: Innocence
line: I want takka berries.

title: Innocence

title: Innocence
line: We have only rations. Now, I must begin working on my shuttle. By my estimate we have fewer than four hours of daylight remaining.

line: I'm not detecting any life forms other than ourselves.

title: Innocence

line: I believe your anxiety about our situation is causing you to imagine the presence

line: The Federation consists of over one hundred and fifty different worlds who have agreed to share their knowledge and resources in peaceful cooperation.

line: Ah, visitors! Welcome to sickbay. I'm the Chief Medical Officer.

line: This is First Prelate Alcia of Drayan Two.

title: Innocence
line: It's an honor to meet you. We don't often receive such distinguished guests here, unless there's been some sort of accident. We are fully equipped to provide a wide variety of treatments here from removing a splinter to re-sequencing the base pairs in a strand of DNA, and our research facilities are the most advanced in Starfleet.

title: Innocence
line: Very impressive.

line: You may be even more interested to learn that this man isn't really a biological lifeform. He's a computer generated holographic projection.

line: My people believe that physical matter is only an illusion. The body is not the true self, only a representation.

title: Innocence
line: One of our greatest philosophers, Plato, wrote that what we see around us are only poor shadows of ideal objects which exist on a higher plane.

title: Innocence
line: That is similar to our teachings. Our connection to what you call a higher plane is more important than our attachment to this brief existence, however real it may seem.

line: Our next step will be to open negotiations. Find out what they might be interested in getting from us in exchange for the polyferranide.

line: It's been our custom for generations to avoid close contact with outsiders. I choose to honor that tradition. Goodbye, Captain. I hope you find your way home.

title: Innocence
line: You think they wandered off and got lost, but they didn't. The Morrok took them. They're gone.

line: You don't understand. We have to get away from here.

line: Please can we go?

title: Innocence
line: Children, you are allowing your fears to guide you. You must learn to exercise control over your own imagination.

title: Innocence

line: Yes, the existence of such a creature is one possibility. However, your emotional reactions are preventing you from accurately judging how unlikely that is to be true.

title: Innocence

line: I believe you can help it. Vulcan children learn to detach themselves from their emotions at an early age.

title: Innocence

line: First, you must focus on the object of your fear. Picture the Morrok clearly in your minds. That image is accompanied by an emotional response. Describe for me what that feeling is like.

title: Innocence
line: Then imagine a strong wind is pushing that cloud away. Watch as your fear grows more distant. It is no longer a part of you. Once you begin to detach yourselves from your emotional responses, you come closer to controlling them. Eventually, they will be eliminated altogether.

line: Do you live your whole life without feeling anything?

title: Innocence
line: The circumstances are irrelevant. A Vulcan approaches every situation logically. Now I must begin work on my shuttle. We will resume the search for the other children once the sensors are operational. I expect each of you to sit quietly and not touch any of the equipment.

line: It helps prepare you to attain a meditative state. Now, close your eyes and imagine all the energy in your body is flowing to the point where your fingertips meet. Nothing else you hear or feel is important. Let the outside world fade away. You exist only inside your mind.

title: Innocence
line: Tuvok?

line: Yes.

line: Do you have any children?

line: Be quiet. We're trying to attain a meditative state.

title: Innocence

line: I have four children. Now you must concentrate.

line: If Vulcans don't feel anything, does that mean you don't love them?

line: My attachment to my children cannot be described as an emotion. They are part of my identity, and I am incomplete without them.

line: I bet they miss you too.

title: Innocence
line: Yes.

line: When I was younger, I accepted it without question. In recent years I have experienced doubts. I do believe there is more in each of us than science has yet explained.

line: This type of disturbance is exactly why we avoid contact with outsiders. I was wrong to respond to your communication. I should have known better than to indulge my curiosity.

line: What's the status of the transporters?

title: Innocence
line: I'll keep working on it.

title: Innocence
line: I don't see how you can be thirsty again after four drinks of water.

line: Aren't you going to sleep?

line: I can go several days without rest if necessary. You cannot. It's warmer by the fire. Go back and try to sleep. Do not worry. I have run several thorough scans of the area. There are no other life forms present, inside the cave or anywhere within five kilometers.

title: Innocence
line: Maybe the Morrok doesn't show up on the scanners.

line: I am also keeping watch on all of you from here. If there is any indication of trouble I will come immediately.

line: I'd like to hear a story. Tell us one about the fire beast of Sullus.

line: It was the Morrok. Why don't you believe me?

line: I will take every possible precaution. I believe you can be responsible with this. Aim like this and press here to fire. I'll seal the shuttle's door while I am gone.
