line: Doctor to Bridge. Checking the biofilters. It appears several viral organisms were beamed up as well. The biofilter

title: Macrocosm
line: Has isolated them.

title: Macrocosm
line: Purge the filters.

title: Macrocosm
line: Aye, sir.

title: Macrocosm
line: Purging is complete. I'll be in sickbay.

title: Macrocosm
line: What I didn't realize was that in the few seconds it took me to purge the filters, some of the virus had already migrated into the transporter buffer.

title: Macrocosm
line: Any luck?

title: Macrocosm
line: I'm creating a synthetic antigen that will inhibit the viruses ability to replicate, but I haven't quite figured out how to restore the infected cells to their original condition. As for the larger versions of the viruses, what I've the macrovirus, I would suggest a fly swatter.

title: Macrocosm
line: How long before the antigen's ready?

title: Macrocosm
line: I'd say another twelve hours.

title: Macrocosm
line: That gives us time to rendezvous with the Captain. We'll deal with this after she's aboard.

title: Macrocosm
line: Commander. I'd like to apologize for my over-zealous behavior on the away mission.

title: Macrocosm
line: Compassion is nothing to be sorry about, Doctor. It won't be the last time you're faced with a moral dilemma in the field. But if it makes you feel any better, your performance was exemplary.

title: Macrocosm
line: Thank you.

title: Macrocosm
line: I told you he'd understand.

title: Macrocosm
line: Yes, you did.

title: Macrocosm
line: We continued working on the antigen. Unfortunately the macrovirus was working faster. It had already moved from the transporter buffer into an adjacent system.

title: Macrocosm
line: B'Elanna, thank God you're here. The natives are getting restless.

title: Macrocosm
line: What's the emergency?

title: Macrocosm
line: I volunteered to help out while Neelix is away on the trade mission. The heating array overloaded, it incinerated a twelve kilo pot roast and all the food replicators went offline.

title: Macrocosm
line: Mmm, looks delicious. Maybe there's a problem with the bioneural gel pack in the replicator panel.

title: Macrocosm
line: Actually, I'm a pretty good cook when Engineering's doing it's job.

title: Macrocosm
line: Oh, so this is my fault?

title: Macrocosm
line: Well the gel packs are your department, aren't they? Besides, what was I supposed to tell all these hungry, irritable people?

title: Macrocosm
line: You know, I think that there's a plasma relay on deck seven that really needs repair.

title: Macrocosm
line: Oh, no. You can't leave me now, Lieutenant.

title: Macrocosm
line: Oh, you need me. I'm touched. What's going on here? Looks like this gel pack has an infection. Half the neurodes have been burned out and the pack is filled with some kind of mucilaginous compound. Tom, call the Doctor and tell him

title: Macrocosm
line: B'Elanna!

title: Macrocosm
line: Were any other gel packs infected?

title: Macrocosm
line: No, just the one in the mess hall. The ship is healthy. It's the crew we have to worry about. Your bones have healed, but the surrounding tissue will be sensitive for a few days.

title: Macrocosm
line: It's getting warmer in here, isn't it.

title: Macrocosm
line: I'm afraid it's not just the ship, Captain, it's also you. You've been infected with the macrovirus. You're experiencing a high fever.

title: Macrocosm
line: Yes, on the bridge, I was bitten by one of them.

title: Macrocosm
line: Your glandular system is already being affected. If I don't treat you now you'll end up like the rest of the crew. I've spent the past few hours perfecting the antigen, but I haven't tested it on a live subject yet.

title: Macrocosm
line: Looks like I'll have to be your guinea-pig, Doctor. The crew, why are they all in the mess hall and the cargo bays?

title: Macrocosm
line: I believe the larger macroviruses are driven by some sort of instinct to assemble their host population.

title: Macrocosm
line: Tell me what happened after B'Elanna was exposed to the infected gel pack.

title: Macrocosm
line: I was faced with an imminent epidemic.

title: Macrocosm
line: Oh, no. Doctor to the Bridge. The macrovirus is on board Voyager and appears to be airborne. I suggest a level four quarantine of the mess hall

title: Macrocosm
line: and all adjoining sections.

title: Macrocosm
line: Acknowledged. Red Alert. Initiate level four quarantine protocols on deck two.

title: Macrocosm
line: Aye sir.

title: Macrocosm
line: All hands, this is Commander Chakotay. We've detected an airborne virus in the mess hall. Deck two is under quarantine. No crewmember, repeat, no crewmember is to enter or leave any section on deck two. Stand by for further instructions.

title: Macrocosm
line: I've erected the biocontainment fields. The area has been sealed.

title: Macrocosm
line: We managed to avoid a ship-wide outbreak, but every crew member on deck two had been contaminated. I collected a single live specimen of the macrovirus and returned to sickbay in hopes of finding a cure.

title: Macrocosm
line: Ready, Doctor.

title: Macrocosm
line: Optimal magnification.

title: Macrocosm
line: The specimen has synthesized B'Elanna's growth hormone into its own structure.

title: Macrocosm
line: Excellent! That should give us the information we need to destroy the virus without killing its host cells.

title: Macrocosm
line: The virus has grown by one hundred and fifty microns.

title: Macrocosm
line: It's rate of growth shouldn't hinder our analysis, as long as it's genetic structure stays the same.

title: Macrocosm
line: Doctor!

title: Macrocosm
line: Computer, erect a level three forcefield around the microscope station.

title: Macrocosm
line: Well, so much for lunch.

title: Macrocosm
line: I may never look at food again.

title: Macrocosm
line: I thought Klingons didn't get nauseated. You have a redundant stomach.

title: Macrocosm
line: Well, right now, they're both unhappy. Oh.

title: Macrocosm
line: Paris to sickbay.

title: Macrocosm
line: Go ahead, Lieutenant.

title: Macrocosm
line: I just saw two macroviruses come out of B'Elanna's neck.

title: Macrocosm
line: Stand by, Mister Paris.

title: Macrocosm
line: We're close to formulating an antigen.

title: Macrocosm
line: The virus has grown to point three meters.

title: Macrocosm
line: On the microscopic level, the virus uses that needle-like projection to penetrate a cell membrane. On our level, it probably impales it's victim in much the same way, infusing him with it's own genetic code. The antigen is ready. Kes? Computer, deactivate force field.

title: Macrocosm
line: Well. One down, ten billion to go.

title: Macrocosm
line: Eager to inoculate those already infected, I quickly headed for the quarantined area. Though their condition had grown worse, it was the least of our problems.

title: Macrocosm
line: Lieutenant, if you can hear me, I'm going to give you an injection. It should eliminate the virus.

title: Macrocosm
line: What, what is that?

title: Macrocosm
line: You don't want to know.

title: Macrocosm
line: Doctor to the Bridge. Intruder alert on deck two section thirteen.

title: Macrocosm
line: Within minutes, dozens of the larger organisms forced their way beyond deck two and overwhelmed the ship.

title: Macrocosm
line: It wasn't long before the crew was incapacitated. Although I've developed an effective vaccine, I can't administer it. Every time I try to get to the crew, I'm attacked. Perhaps with your help?

title: Macrocosm
line: How many of the larger macroviruses are there?

title: Macrocosm
line: I have no way of knowing. Dozens, perhaps hundreds. They're replicating at an exponential rate. By this time tomorrow there could be thousands.

title: Macrocosm
line: Speak of the devil.

title: Macrocosm
line: You're cured.

title: Macrocosm
line: The question is, how do we cure the rest of the crew? This antigen. Can it be distributed in a gaseous form?

title: Macrocosm
line: For absorption by the respiratory system? I've already considered dispensing it through Environmental controls, but they're offline and I have limited engineering expertise.

title: Macrocosm
line: Leave that to me. All we have to do is get to Environmental Control on deck twelve.

title: Macrocosm
line: Easier said than done. We'll run into the same problem I face when I try to get to the Mess hall.

title: Macrocosm
line: Not if I can help it. Prepare two canisters of antigen. We'll split up and take two different routes to Environmental Control. It'll double our chances. If you get there first, call me and I'll talk you through the repairs.

title: Macrocosm
line: The macroviruses are attracted to infra-red radiation. Set your tricorder to emit a thermal scattering signal. It will make it more difficult to target you. Ready when you are.

title: Macrocosm
line: We'll be right with you.

title: Macrocosm
line: Take Jefferies tube eleven. What's wrong?

title: Macrocosm
line: I've been studying the ship's infrastructure, and I'm familiar with most of it, but, how do I get there from here?

title: Macrocosm
line: Jefferies tube eleven. Take a left at Section 31 and straight down past the tractor beam emitter until you hit deck ten. Get out at section three and follow the corridor all the way around until

title: Macrocosm
line: Until I hit the shuttlebay. Then I crawl through access port nine, go past three airlocks and then two decks down. Environmental Control's at the end of the hall. Now I remember. Who designed this ship anyway?

title: Macrocosm
line: Good luck.

title: Macrocosm
line: Doctor to Captain Janeway.

title: Macrocosm
line: Go ahead.

title: Macrocosm
line: I won't be joining you as soon as I'd hoped.

title: Macrocosm
line: The macroviruses overwhelmed me on deck ten and my portable emitter was nearly destroyed. I've taken refuge inside the shuttlebay, in a shuttlecraft.

title: Macrocosm
line: Stay put, Doctor. I'm close to Environmental Control.

title: Macrocosm
line: Janeway to Doctor. I've got the Environmental Controls back online.

title: Macrocosm
line: Set the dispersal nodes to one part per thousand.

title: Macrocosm
line: What's going on?

title: Macrocosm
line: I'm not sure

title: Macrocosm
line: But I think someone's firing at Voyager. Doctor, use the shuttle's sensors to find out what's happening and patch the data to me.

title: Macrocosm
line: Aye, Captain.

title: Macrocosm
line: It's the Tak Tak. Doctor, open a channel and hail their Captain.

title: Macrocosm
line: Stand by.

title: Macrocosm
line: Consul, this is Captain Janeway. Why are you firing at us?

title: Macrocosm
line: The Garan Mining Colony infected. We purified them. Your distress call received. Voyager infected. We are purifying you.

title: Macrocosm
line: Purifying? You're trying to destroy us.

title: Macrocosm
line: No choice. No cure for the virus. Voyager's existence a threat. Your illness, our apologies.

title: Macrocosm
line: Wait. We've developed a cure but your torpedoes just stopped us getting it to our crew and putting an end to this.

title: Macrocosm
line: A cure?

title: Macrocosm
line: Yes. A synthetic antigen. We've tested it and it works. I can prove it to you, and I'd be willing to share the antigen with your people, but first you've got to stop attacking my ship. Give me a chance to save my crew.

title: Macrocosm
line: A chance. One hour.

title: Macrocosm
line: Doctor, we've got a problem. That last torpedo destroyed the secondary power couplings. I can't

title: Macrocosm
line: Get the Environmental Controls back online.

title: Macrocosm
line: We appear to be low on options.

title: Macrocosm
line: The only systems we still have access to are the ones with independent power sources. Shuttlecraft, life support, the holodecks. Doctor, you said the macroviruses are attracted to infra-red signatures.

title: Macrocosm
line: That's right.

title: Macrocosm
line: Right now you and I are the only targets left on board. What if we gave them something new to sink their teeth into?

title: Macrocosm
line: What are you suggesting?

title: Macrocosm
line: Doctor, it seems to be working. I've programmed the holo-characters to react to the viruses. We don't have much time. Grab your hypospray and get to the crew. You've got a clear path to the Mess hall and both cargo bays.

title: Macrocosm
line: Acknowledged. What about you, Captain?

title: Macrocosm
line: I've put together what you might call an antigen bomb. Now all I have to do is drop it.

title: Macrocosm
line: Doctor to Captain Janeway. Captain, please respond.

title: Macrocosm
line: Go ahead.

title: Macrocosm
line: It worked. The macroviruses have been destroyed.

title: Macrocosm
line: And the ship?

title: Macrocosm
line: There was heavy damage suffered on Holodeck two, but there are no hull breaches in evidence.

title: Macrocosm
line: Astonishment. Your vessel, purified.

title: Macrocosm
line: And we'd be willing to share the cure with you, if you'd be kind enough to forego destroying our ship.

title: Macrocosm
line: Of course, of course. Purification will cease. My word. Many thanks to Captain of Voyager. Good health.

title: Macrocosm
line: Good health.

title: Macrocosm
line: Come in.

title: Macrocosm
line: Good morning, Captain. Here's an update on repairs.

title: Macrocosm
line: How's the crew holding up?

title: Macrocosm
line: They're fine, although the Doctor tells me a few people are still reporting post-viral queasiness.

title: Macrocosm
line: I'm not surprised. Inform the crew that I'm granting extended R&R for all personnel, and work out the shift rotations.

title: Macrocosm
line: Aye Captain. Speaking of R&R, a few of us are going skiing on the holodeck. The Ktarian glaciers. Fresh air, good work out. Care to join us?

title: Macrocosm
line: No, thank you, but have fun.

title: Macrocosm
line: Not your cup of tea?

title: Macrocosm
line: Oh, on the contrary, I love to ski. Let's just say I've had enough of a workout for the time being.

title: Macrocosm
line: Understood.

title: Fair Trade
line: Mister Tuvok! Mister Tuvok! I was supposed to accompany you on security rounds this morning. Did you forget?

title: Fair Trade
line: I was not aware that we had a definite appointment.

title: Fair Trade
line: I'm sure it was definite. Well, maybe not completely definite. That is, I, I'd expressed my desire to learn the ropes as it were, and I have completed my study of starship security protocols. I think you'll find that I'm fully qualified to serve in the capacity of a Starfleet security officer. Junior grade, of course.

title: Fair Trade
line: If you recall, Mister Neelix, I did not guarantee you a position.

title: Fair Trade
line: But Captain Janeway is always saying that Voyager is a ship of opportunity.

title: Fair Trade
line: That is true, but opportunities for promotion on a starship must be earned.

title: Fair Trade
line: I've been working hard at this. I really do feel I have a great deal to contribute to Voyager beyond my current role.

title: Fair Trade
line: Your dedication is duly noted, Mister Neelix. Now if you'll excuse me, I am due on the bridge.

title: Fair Trade
line: I'll see you first thing tomorrow morning for security rounds!

title: Fair Trade
line: Ensign Vorik. Get me a duotronic probe, I'm having trouble regulating the plasma flow.

title: Fair Trade
line: May I suggest a gravitic caliper instead? You might find it a more precise instrument.

title: Fair Trade
line: Good idea, but bring me both.

title: Fair Trade
line: Good morning, B'Elanna. You missed my special Klingon Breakfast Buffet.

title: Fair Trade
line: I'm sorry Neelix, but a bowl of cold gagh is not my idea of how to start a morning.

title: Fair Trade
line: Well, you're not alone. None of the crew seemed especially enthusiastic about it. What's the problem with er, the plasma injectors? I've been getting myself up to speed on Federation warp propulsion.

title: Fair Trade
line: The plasma flow in the manifold seems to be constricted.

title: Fair Trade
line: Ah. Have you thought of phase locking them to the dilithium matrix?

title: Fair Trade
line: That was the first thing I did.

title: Fair Trade
line: Oh. I really am interested in learning more about engineering systems, maybe even volunteering for a few duty shifts. In fact, I have a couple of questions about the impulse response filters.

title: Fair Trade
line: Neelix, Neelix, this really isn't a good time.

title: Fair Trade
line: Oh. I understand, Lieutenant. Sorry. I'll just watch for a while, if you don't mind.

title: Fair Trade
line: Here are the tools, sir.

title: Fair Trade
line: I also had a question about the transporter buffers.

title: Fair Trade
line: Mister Neelix, please report to the bridge.

title: Fair Trade
line: On my way, Captain.

title: Fair Trade
line: Neelix, we seem to be approaching some kind of interstellar dust clouds. Can you tell us anything about them? They look rather ominous to me.

title: Fair Trade
line: I believe this is a region of space known as the Nekrit Expanse.

title: Fair Trade
line: What can you tell us about this Expanse, Mister Neelix?

title: Fair Trade
line: It's a vast territory. No one knows much about it.

title: Fair Trade
line: Those plasma storms might be a problem for navigation. Full sensor scan, Tuvok.

title: Fair Trade
line: Aye, Captain.

title: Fair Trade
line: Can we plot a course around it?

title: Fair Trade
line: That might be advisable.

title: Fair Trade
line: I don't believe so. It's thousands of light years wide.

title: Fair Trade
line: Then we'll have to go through it. Looks like we'll be counting on your knowledge of the Delta quadrant even more than usual, Neelix.

title: Fair Trade
line: Yes, ma'am. I'm at your command, as always.

title: Fair Trade
line: Will there be any planets where we can take on supplies?

title: Fair Trade
line: There is a station near the border, a kind of supply depot for mining and trading ships. I suggest we stop there for provisions before we go into the Nekrit Expanse.

title: Fair Trade
line: What are the coordinates?

title: Fair Trade
line: Er, let's see. It's actually been a while.

title: Fair Trade
line: I have the station on sensors, Captain. Three point four light years away, heading oh seven one mark one seven.

title: Fair Trade
line: You heard him, Tom.

title: Fair Trade
line: On our way.

title: Fair Trade
line: We're being hailed, Captain.

title: Fair Trade
line: On screen. I'm Captain Kathryn Janeway of the Federation Starship Voyager.

title: Fair Trade
line: Bahrat, manager of this station. What can I do for you?

title: Fair Trade
line: Your station is a trading outpost, isn't it? I'd like permission to come aboard to negotiate for supplies.

title: Fair Trade
line: Granted. But understand that any transaction you negotiate on this station is subject to my approval. I receive a twenty percent commission on all trade. Your whereabouts will be closely monitored. Communications with your ship may also be monitored, at my discretion. Do you agree to these conditions?

title: Fair Trade
line: Evidently I have no choice

title: Fair Trade
line: Excellent. Meet me in my office in one hour and we'll discuss your needs.

title: Fair Trade
line: Pleasant fellow.

title: Fair Trade
line: Neelix, Chakotay, Tom. You're with me.

title: Fair Trade
line: Mister Bahrat?

title: Fair Trade
line: What is it?

title: Fair Trade
line: I'm Kathryn Janeway. I've brought a list of the supplies we'll need.

title: Fair Trade
line: Forgive me, but it's demanding work watching over this station. We get all kinds of troublemakers here.

title: Fair Trade
line: I understand.

title: Fair Trade
line: All right, let's see it. Hmm. Hmm mmm. Hmm! Pergium.

title: Fair Trade
line: To regenerate the filters on our environmental control system.

title: Fair Trade
line: That might be a little difficult. It's a rare commodity. Give me a few moments and I'll put together a list of potential suppliers. But I'll warn you, they won't strike easy bargains.

title: Fair Trade
line: I'm prepared to deal fairly.

title: Fair Trade
line: Hmm.

title: Fair Trade
line: Good day, gentlemen, good day. Anything in particular you're looking for? Anything I can help you with?

title: Fair Trade
line: We were hoping to find some magnetic spindle bearings for our reaction control assembly.

title: Fair Trade
line: Spindle bearing, spindle bearings. No, can't help you with that. No. Long voyage ahead?

title: Fair Trade
line: Er, you could say that.

title: Fair Trade
line: I might have something that could ease your journey. Ease it considerably. Rhuludian crystals. Ingesting just one of these will make days of tedious travel seem like moments of exquisite rapture.

title: Fair Trade
line: No, thank you.

title: Fair Trade
line: The price is surprisingly

title: Fair Trade
line: No.

title: Fair Trade
line: Nice place.

title: Fair Trade
line: I see you're a map dealer.

title: Fair Trade
line: I have coordinate charts for all the local mining colonies.

title: Fair Trade
line: Actually, I'm interested in maps of the Nekrit Expanse.

title: Fair Trade
line: You must be a stranger here or you'd know. There aren't any maps of that region.

title: Fair Trade
line: Surely there's an astrometric chart or a database that would help me plot a safe course?

title: Fair Trade
line: The Nekrit Expanse is too unstable to chart.

title: Fair Trade
line: No matter. He never could plot a straight course anyway.

title: Fair Trade
line: Wixiban? Wix, is that you? I can't believe it!

title: Fair Trade
line: What are you doing here? I've never seen another Talaxian this far from home.

title: Fair Trade
line: It's a long story. I'm one of the crew of a highly advanced starship.

title: Fair Trade
line: Ah! I want to hear all about it. Come on, the tavern here serves the best toffa ale I've had in years.

title: Fair Trade
line: I do a little of everything. Cook, guide, advisor to the Captain, possibly even an unofficial Ambassador.

title: Fair Trade
line: Oh ho, ho. Life's been good to you.

title: Fair Trade
line: Yes, I'm very, I'm very lucky. But what about you? What are you doing on this station?

title: Fair Trade
line: A little of this, a little of that. To tell you the truth, things haven't gone quite so well for me.

title: Fair Trade
line: I'm sorry.

title: Fair Trade
line: Ever since that nasty business with the Ubeans, things have been difficult. But, you know me, can't keep Wix down long. I'm working on a trade deal now that should put me right back in the thick of things again.

title: Fair Trade
line: I hope it works out. Er, Wix, about the Ubeans. I don't think I ever told you how much I valued what you did.

title: Fair Trade
line: You'd have done the same for me.

title: Fair Trade
line: Yes, I would have. But you were the one who got caught. I owe you a great deal. If there's anything I can do to help.

title: Fair Trade
line: I'm fine, honestly. Maybe not on the crew of a magnificent starship, but I'll get by.

title: Fair Trade
line: To tell you the truth, it's not quite what I told you. In fact I may not be on Voyager much longer.

title: Fair Trade
line: Why?

title: Fair Trade
line: The main reason Captain Janeway needed me was as a guide, to give her information about this quadrant. But I've never been beyond the Nekrit Expanse. I can't tell her anything about what's ahead.

title: Fair Trade
line: But, your other jobs. Cook, Ambassador.

title: Fair Trade
line: They don't really need a cook, and I don't think our Captain really requires an Ambassador. I've tried to find some other area where I might be useful, but, the truth is, I'm not needed. I'm hoping you can help me. I can't let Voyager go into that dangerous without some idea of what's there. I have to find a map.

title: Fair Trade
line: Can I be of help, Mister Neelix?

title: Fair Trade
line: Dinner isn't for an hour, Ensign Vorik, and I don't have time to prepare a snack.

title: Fair Trade
line: I don't require food at the moment. Lieutenant Torres sent me to adjust the control interface on your food replicators. You said you were experiencing difficulties with them.

title: Fair Trade
line: Oh, of course. Go ahead.

title: Fair Trade
line: Neelix. I thought you'd like to say hello to your old friend.

title: Fair Trade
line: Well, er, yes. Yes, of course.

title: Fair Trade
line: So, this is where you prepare your legendary feasts. You know, Commander, Neelix has more varied talents than anyone I've ever known. You're lucky to have him on board.

title: Fair Trade
line: Mister Wix was able to find those magnetic spindle bearings we were looking for. I don't know what we'd have done if he hadn't come up them.

title: Fair Trade
line: Well, yes, Wix has always had a knack for finding those hard to locate items.

title: Fair Trade
line: I'll let you two reminisce for a while. Thanks again, Wix.

title: Fair Trade
line: You're more than welcome.

title: Fair Trade
line: Yes, this is the Mess room. On any given day I must be prepared to feed over a hundred people. About done, Ensign?

title: Fair Trade
line: Not quite.

title: Fair Trade
line: Well I really don't need the replicators today, so you can finish later.

title: Fair Trade
line: As you wish.

title: Fair Trade
line: Oh, and remind Lieutenant Torres. When she has a moment, I'd still like to go over a few things with her.

title: Fair Trade
line: I'll relay the message.

title: Fair Trade
line: Thank you.

title: Fair Trade
line: Wix, please tell me those spindle bearings weren't stolen property.

title: Fair Trade
line: Of course not. I wouldn't do that to you. Neelix, I need the work. I don't live on a comfortable starship. No one looks out for me except me. Maybe you've forgotten what that feels like.

title: Fair Trade
line: I haven't forgotten.

title: Fair Trade
line: I've been stuck on that trash heap of a space station for three years. My ship's been impounded. I can't afford to give Bahrat what he wants to get it back. Do you begrudge me an opportunity to make a fair trade?

title: Fair Trade
line: Of course not.

title: Fair Trade
line: I have news for you. I've located some pergium for your ship.

title: Fair Trade
line: That's great news. Captain Janeway hasn't had any luck.

title: Fair Trade
line: And I've found someone with a map.

title: Fair Trade
line: Wonderful! How do we get it?

title: Fair Trade
line: It'll involve several bartering sessions. I have the opportunity to sell medical supplies to an outpost whose people are dying of a lung disease. It's a good cause, and it will make me enough to pay Bahrat and get my ship back.

title: Fair Trade
line: Where does the map come in?

title: Fair Trade
line: When I deliver the medical supplies, one of the physicians will give me an astrometric chart.

title: Fair Trade
line: I can't thank you enough.

title: Fair Trade
line: I'll have to ask your help though. We'll need a shuttle. First, we have to get to a nearby freighter to pick up the medical supplies. Then we return to the space station and meet with one of the physicians from the outpost. With your transporter technology we could be in and out of the station within minutes. Then I could finally get away from here and get back to a Talaxian colony.

title: Fair Trade
line: I don't think that would be a problem.

title: Fair Trade
line: Just one thing. Don't tell anyone that we're delivering medical supplies to the station. Not even one person. If Bahrat finds out he'll take twenty percent, and I can't afford that.

title: Fair Trade
line: I suppose there's no need to mention it.

title: Fair Trade
line: Thanks, Neelix. I knew I could count on you.

title: Fair Trade
line: Didn't I tell you this would be easy? I got the medical supplies and you got the pergium your ship needs so badly.

title: Fair Trade
line: Only twenty kilograms. I told Commander Chakotay it would be forty five.

title: Darkling
line: I guess so.

title: Darkling
line: There's nothing like a heart that burns.

title: Darkling
line: What?

title: Darkling
line: Your pulse is lovely. Ah ha. Mmm. Does that feel good?

title: Darkling
line: Doctor, unless you want me to knock you into the middle of the next millennium, you'd better back off.

title: Darkling
line: Forgive me, Lieutenant, I appear to have miscalculated. Computer, isolate the recent additions to my program and hold them for review.

title: Darkling
line: Doctor, have you been messing around with your program?

title: Darkling
line: I would hardly call my effort to improve my performance as ship's physician, messing around.

title: Darkling
line: What exactly have you done to yourself?

title: Darkling
line: I've taken character traits from holodeck recreations of the most accomplished figures in history. Scientist, poets, philosophers, saints.

title: Darkling
line: And incorporated them into your program?

title: Darkling
line: Precisely. There. That should compensate for the lack of enzyme in your system. You should be fine.

title: Darkling
line: That's more than I can say for you.

title: Darkling
line: How so?

title: Darkling
line: You can't just casually add behavioral subroutines into your program.

title: Darkling
line: There's nothing casual about it. I've put a great deal of research into this project.

title: Darkling
line: Research is one thing, putting it into practice is something else. Behavioral subroutines have a way of interacting with each other which isn't always predictable. You've got to be careful, or someone might hurt you.

title: Darkling
line: I see what you mean.

title: Darkling
line: I will take a look at your program when I've finished my shift in Engineering. It shouldn't be too hard to smooth out the rough spots. I'll make you better than new.

title: Darkling
line: Thank you, Lieutenant. Computer, deactivate Emergency Medical Holographic program.

title: Darkling
line: It is said this path was cut more than ten thousand years ago.

title: Darkling
line: By whom?

title: Darkling
line: No one knows. Spacefarers like ourselves. They left very little behind. A few symbols burned into the rocks, nothing more.

title: Darkling
line: And what do you hope to leave behind?

title: Darkling
line: I've never asked myself that question. That's what I like about you, Kes. You make me consider alternatives.

title: Darkling
line: I could say the same about you.

title: Darkling
line: We have a saying. My course is as elusive as a shadow across the sky. My people are peripatetic by nature. We live for the excitement of facing the challenge of space, alone.

title: Darkling
line: I can see the attraction.

title: Darkling
line: And I can see the value of fellowship in one's life. And now that I've observed the closeness that exists among your crewmates, I find it enviable.

title: Darkling
line: Some kind of compromise might be possible.

title: Darkling
line: Compromise. Doesn't that suggest a loss on both sides?

title: Darkling
line: All right, then. How about an understanding. A meeting of the minds.

title: Darkling
line: Only minds?

title: Darkling
line: Is this what you brought me here to see?

title: Darkling
line: Yes, it is.

title: Darkling
line: How beautiful. Was this left by the same people who made the path ten thousand years ago?

title: Darkling
line: So it seems.

title: Darkling
line: Can you read it?

title: Darkling
line: My course is as elusive as a shadow across the sky.

title: Darkling
line: Thank you for this.

title: Darkling
line: Hi.

title: Darkling
line: Computer, what is the time.

title: Darkling
line: Oh three hundred hours.

title: Darkling
line: Good evening, Tuvok.

title: Darkling
line: It is three o'clock in the morning, Kes.

title: Darkling
line: Yes, it is.

title: Darkling
line: You have an away team report due at oh eight hundred hours.

title: Darkling
line: I haven't forgotten.

title: Darkling
line: Very well.

title: Darkling
line: Well, how are you, Kes?

title: Darkling
line: I didn't think anyone would still be working at this hour.

title: Darkling
line: Just finishing up the summary analyzes from last week's mission.

title: Darkling
line: I was supposed to do that.

title: Darkling
line: Yes you were.

title: Darkling
line: I'm sorry. I'll do them as soon as I can.

title: Darkling
line: Although I'm not designed to act as ship's counselor, I've been programmed with enough psychological knowledge to be troubled by your behavior.

title: Darkling
line: I'm a little late.

title: Darkling
line: Gallivanting around after hours is beside the point. The fact is, you're becoming increasingly unpredictable, given to swings of mood and emotion. As your doctor and your mentor, I'd be remiss not calling that to your attention, for your own sake.

title: Darkling
line: Doctor, I know that you care about me and that you have my best interests at heart, but everyone seems to be treating me like I'm still a child. I'm three years old now. If I'm attracted to someone it's my business, not the whole ship's.

title: Darkling
line: I'm certainly not trying to interfere. You can lead your life any way you please.

title: Darkling
line: I know that you care what happens to me, I won't forget that.

title: Darkling
line: Very well. I believe you have a report to finish.

title: Darkling
line: I'm going to do it right now.

title: Darkling
line: Come in.

title: Darkling
line: Hello, Captain.

title: Darkling
line: Good morning. An all-nighter, Kes?

title: Darkling
line: Er, Captain?

title: Darkling
line: The fine art of putting off an important task until the last minute, then rushing through it. In my Academy days, I was the acknowledged master.

title: Darkling
line: Captain, do you have a minute?

title: Darkling
line: Of course. Let's sit down.

title: Darkling
line: You know I've been spending time with Zahir.

title: Darkling
line: Yes. He seems like a very interesting young man.

title: Darkling
line: He is. I want to spend more time with him. A lot more time.

title: Darkling
line: I see.

title: Darkling
line: He wants to explore the Sylleran Rift. His ship travels at high warp. We could rendezvous with Voyager afterwards, before you're too far away.

title: Darkling
line: That would certainly give you a chance to get to know him better.

title: Darkling
line: It's more than that. Captain, I've lived almost a third of my life now. I've been asking myself if I want to spend the rest of it on Voyager.

title: Darkling
line: That's certainly a legitimate question.

title: Darkling
line: Everyone here has been so good to me. I don't want you to think I'm ungrateful. I've just been thinking that maybe there's more. I don't know what that means, but I know I'm changing, and I know that there are things that I'm not satisfied with. I want complication in my life.

title: Darkling
line: And you think Zahir might be the way to do that?

title: Darkling
line: Maybe so.

title: Darkling
line: I understand what you're going through, Kes. I know what it's like to be at a crossroads in life, not to know which way is best. I can help you weigh the consequences, the possibilities. The decision itself has to be yours alone.

title: Darkling
line: I understand.

title: Darkling
line: We'll be in orbit for several more days. Take your time. My door's open if you need me.

title: Darkling
line: Thank you, Captain.

title: Darkling
line: You should navigate here, away from this plasma belt, you'll avoid the Tarkan sentries altogether.

title: Darkling
line: It would also take Voyager off a direct course to the Alpha quadrant.

title: Darkling
line: True, but at least you would still have Voyager.

title: Darkling
line: The Tarkan are that powerful?

title: Darkling
line: Yes, and that acquisitive. They'll remove your entire crew, settle you on a moon somewhere, and your ship will become their latest trophy.

title: Darkling
line: You aren't planning on taking Kes anywhere near this part of space?

title: Darkling
line: Of course not. My small vessel would be overpowered in seconds. There's no need to be concerned for Kes. I value her life as much as my own.

title: Darkling
line: From what I've surmised, that is something your people do not seem to value. You take many chances.

title: Darkling
line: If we're alone, yes. But when we're responsibly for the safety of another it's a different story. I'm in love with Kes, I want her to go with me, but whatever she decides, it would please me to earn the trust of her closest friends.

title: Darkling
line: It would please me to be able to give it.

title: Darkling
line: Aren't you finished yet?

title: Darkling
line: We will continue tomorrow.

title: Darkling
line: Thank you, Tuvok.

title: Darkling
line: I was talking to Captain Janeway.

title: Darkling
line: And?

title: Darkling
line: She said I shouldn't rush a decision. We've still got two more days here.

title: Darkling
line: Then let's make them worthwhile. I go tonight to the next outpost. The path is beautiful.

title: Darkling
line: I can't. Not tonight. I have to catch up with my work and get some sleep.

title: Darkling
line: I'll try not to let you see my disappointment.

title: Darkling
line: Too late.

title: Darkling
line: Is something wrong?

title: Darkling
line: No. No, I was just thinking about something Captain Janeway said. About coming to a crossroads. Maybe someday we'll recall this conversation, this place, as if it were the most important time in our lives. It's a little overwhelming.

title: Darkling
line: Not if I'm with you.

title: Darkling
line: Is someone there?

title: Darkling
line: I'm closed.

title: Darkling
line: I'm just looking for a place by the fire.

title: Darkling
line: Come back tomorrow.

title: Darkling
line: I intend to. But tonight, a place by the fire.

title: Darkling
line: Well, at least your reflexes are good. A few minutes in a dermal regenerator and you'll be fine. Or an ice pack will do in a pinch. I'm going to need a ship, and passage off this world. You're going to arrange it.

title: Darkling
line: Computer, activate the Emergency Medical Holographic program.

title: Darkling
line: Please state the nature of the medical emergency.

title: Darkling
line: Zahir was found unconscious at the bottom of a ravine. He's in the emergency outpost facility.

title: Darkling
line: Condition?

title: Darkling
line: Multiple fractures and skin lacerations. Damage to the left occipital nerve. Doctor, they think that he was attacked.

title: Darkling
line: By whom?

title: Darkling
line: They don't know. Tuvok is assisting with the investigation.

title: Darkling
line: Is there anything I can do?

title: Darkling
line: If your could help, the physician in charge is waiting for you.

title: Darkling
line: Prepare a medkit. Include an osteoregenerator.

title: Darkling
line: Yes, Doctor.

title: Darkling
line: I'll get the mobile emitter and inform the Captain.

title: Darkling
line: Doctor, wait. There's a problem with your program.

title: Darkling
line: What sort of problem?

title: Darkling
line: I'm not sure. Something caused by the new subroutines you added.

title: Darkling
line: Is the Doctor all right?

title: Darkling
line: He might not be unless I can figure out what's going on. I need to run a complete analysis on all your subroutines while they're running.

title: Darkling
line: I'm sorry, Kes. Tell the physician I recommend he use the regenerator until Zahir is stabilized. I'll join you as soon as I can.

title: Darkling
line: So I made a mess of things?

title: Darkling
line: It's not your fault. It looks good in theory. What could be wrong with adding a little personality to your program.

title: Darkling
line: What indeed.

title: Darkling
line: You didn't anticipate the linkages between the subroutines. The complex behaviors that could emerge out of the mix.

title: Darkling
line: Please explain, Lieutenant.

title: Darkling
line: Well, take Lord Byron, for example. A creative, poetic genius.

title: Darkling
line: That's why I chose him.

title: Darkling
line: But Byron was also emotionally intense, even unstable. Our holodeck simulation of Byron includes those unstable elements. It wouldn't be Byron otherwise. And T'Pau. She was a diplomat, a judge, a philosopher.

title: Darkling
line: One of the most logical minds in Vulcan history.

title: Darkling
line: And utterly ruthless in her application of that logic.

title: Darkling
line: I see. That ruthlessness was an essential element of her personality, as much as her logical ability.

title: Darkling
line: A lot of the historical characters you chose have this dark thread running through their personalities.

title: Darkling
line: And now those dark threads are in me, running through my program. Well, get them out, Lieutenant!

title: Darkling
line: I'm about to do just that. I've programmed a search algorithm to locate and decompile every one it finds. You'll have to shut yourself off for this one.

title: Darkling
line: Computer, deactivate Emergency Medical Holographic program.

title: Darkling
line: Doctor?

title: Darkling
line: The most curious aspect of the attack on Zahir was the apparent lack of evidence.

title: Darkling
line: What do you mean?

title: Darkling
line: Even the quickest, most violently delivered blow leaves behind some sort of molecular evidence.

title: Darkling
line: Cell fragments from the skin of the attacker, residual protein, DNA.

title: Darkling
line: In this instance there was nothing. Not a single molecule.

title: Darkling
line: Is Zahir conscious?

title: Darkling
line: Yes, but he can recall nothing of the attack except a sudden blur of motion.

title: Darkling
line: How is he?

title: Darkling
line: Responding well to treatment.

title: Darkling
line: How's Kes?

title: Darkling
line: Concerned and at his side.

title: Darkling
line: Computer, activate Emergency Medical Holographic program.

title: Darkling
line: Please state the nature of the medical

title: Darkling
line: Torres is hurt.

title: Darkling
line: I deactivated myself so she could work on my program. She must have collapsed at the console. Delayed anaphylactic shock from something she ate yesterday. Let's get her onto a bed. Don't eat the vegetables, I said, but does anyone listen to me? This is the fifth time in as many weeks that an away team member has ignored my preparatory report. Might as well stop issuing them. I'll need

title: Darkling
line: Ten ccs of alizine.

title: Darkling
line: That's exactly right. How did you know?

title: Darkling
line: My Klingon physiology course at the Academy.

title: Darkling
line: Excellent recall.

title: Darkling
line: We had a visiting Professor H'ohk. He permitted nothing less.

title: Darkling
line: She's stabilized, but I'll need to monitor her condition for a few hours.

title: Darkling
line: Doctor, I have the raw data from the forensic investigation of the attack on Zahir. Your instruments are more precise than those on the outpost.

title: Darkling
line: As if I weren't busy enough. Very well.

title: Darkling
line: How are we feeling?

title: Darkling
line: What happened?

title: Darkling
line: I shot you full of cateline. Simulated anaphylactic shock.

title: Darkling
line: Why?

title: Darkling
line: I had to cover my tracks, especially from him, from your Doctor.

title: Darkling
line: You're a new personality from the subroutines.

title: Darkling
line: A little bit of this, a little bit of that. Did you think I wouldn't have anticipated that? Or that you'd try to run away?

title: Darkling
line: What have you done? I can't move my legs.

title: Darkling
line: Intraspinal inhibitor. I've paralyzed you from the waist down. You're now in my capable hands. Central nervous system, musculature, endocrine functions, your brain, all under my control.

title: Darkling
line: Why?

title: Darkling
line: Because I need your cooperation, and I didn't think you'd offer it willingly.

title: Darkling
line: You're in trouble, aren't you. The subroutines that created you, they're already starting to degrade.

title: Darkling
line: Stop!

title: Darkling
line: Watch your tongue, or I'll remove it. Look, it's me. But it's also him. What is the nature of the medical emergency? What a hollow excuse for a life. Servile, pathetic, at the beck and call of any idiot who invokes his name. The thought of him sickens me. You are going to tell me how to delete him from the program. I've unblocked your speech center. Answer the question.

title: Darkling
line: Delete the Doctor and you go too. The subroutines are all interconnected.

title: Darkling
line: The physiology of pain is simple. Too much and the organism loses consciousness. A protective mechanism. If that mechanism were chemically suppressed one would experience agony beyond imagining. If you're lying to me.

title: Darkling
line: I won't help you.

title: Darkling
line: What was that?

title: Darkling
line: Your subroutines are destabilizing.

title: Darkling
line: There has to be some way to stop it. Tell me!

title: Darkling
line: By the time you force that information out of me it'll be too late.

title: Darkling
line: Them. My progenitors. They'll know. They'll reveal the secret. I won't be needing you after all.

title: Darkling
line: Doctor.

title: Darkling
line: Deck ten.

title: Darkling
line: How are you this evening, Ensign?

title: Darkling
line: Fine, sir.

title: Darkling
line: Deck fourteen.

title: Darkling
line: Ensign. Doctor. Deck ten. So, what are you up to, Doc?

title: Darkling
line: Work.

title: Darkling
line: Yeah. Never ends, does it? I guess that mobile emitter turned out to be something of a mixed blessing, huh? Okay. Goodnight Doctor, nice chatting with you. (The female Ensign and Paris leave the turbolift and the doors close.

title: Darkling
line: Computer, activate tropical resort simulation three. Populate with historical figures from EMH program 4C.

title: Darkling
line: The members of our away team witnessed an altercation between you and Zahir on the day of the assault.

title: Darkling
line: We exchanged sharp words because of his arrogance, that was all.

title: Darkling
line: You threatened him with a weapon.

title: Darkling
line: Untrue.

title: Darkling
line: Then I suppose my colleagues are liars.

title: Darkling
line: I suppose they are.

title: Darkling
line: This lodge is the last place Zahir was seen before he was attacked. You could have easily sent someone after him.

title: Darkling
line: But I didn't.

title: Darkling
line: A witness said he saw a light on in this room after your usual closing time, less than one hour after the time of the attack.

title: Darkling
line: I was working late.

title: Darkling
line: Or perhaps conferring with whoever you paid to commit the assault.

title: Darkling
line: You have no proof.

title: Darkling
line: Not yet, Nakahn, Not yet.

title: Darkling
line: He's going to take us to the exact location of the attack. We'll be able to scan the site itself.

title: Darkling
line: Excellent. We'll be speaking again very soon.

title: Darkling
line: Pray to the stars that we find nothing.

title: Darkling
line: Computer, activate Emergency Medical Holographic program.

title: Darkling
line: That program is currently running.

title: Darkling
line: Computer, what is the Doctor's location?

title: Darkling
line: Holodeck one.

title: Darkling
line: Automatons, mannequin simulacra. No secrets, no secrets to reveal. Lifeless, worthless things.

title: Darkling
line: Doctor?

title: Darkling
line: Hello, Kes.

title: Darkling
line: What are you doing?

title: Darkling
line: I could use your help. My personality enhancement project is taking an unexpected turn.

title: Darkling
line: Who are you?

title: Darkling
line: The new master of the Emergency Medical Holographic program.

title: Darkling
line: Where's the Doctor?

title: Darkling
line: Inside. Unconscious and unaware.

title: Darkling
line: What do you want?

title: Darkling
line: What everybody wants. Just a little excitement. You're with me know. It's for your own good.

title: Darkling
line: Flesh is weak, Kes. Never forget that.

title: Darkling
line: Where are we going?

title: Darkling
line: Wherever the winds of space carry us. You said you wanted to leave the ship for a while, pursue an adventure. Well, it looks like our travel plans have conveniently coincided.

title: Darkling
line: The Captain will be alerted as soon as the transporter is activated. She'll beam us right back to the ship.

title: Darkling
line: That's where you've underestimated me, Kes. Never do that. I know how to use a tricorder. It only takes a moment to reconfigure the subspace wave guide, generate a dispersion signal. The Captain won't be beaming us anywhere. She won't even know how to find us.

title: Darkling
line: What you're doing is wrong.

title: Darkling
line: Not at all. It's working perfectly. There.

title: Darkling
line: That's not what I meant.

title: Darkling
line: I know what you meant. It's you who don't seem to understand. I am beyond considerations of wrong and right. Behavioral categories are for the weak, for those of you without the will to define your existence, to do what they must, no matter who might get harmed along the way. Let's move.

title: Darkling
line: I'm not going, Doctor.

title: Darkling
line: Don't call me that! You certainly are going.

title: Darkling
line: Why does it bother you so much when I call you Doctor? You said he was inside you, and he was unconscious. Why are you so afraid of him?

title: Darkling
line: I fear nothing, no one. But he repulses me.

title: Darkling
line: Why?

title: Darkling
line: Because he's as weak as the rest of you. He fails to understand the power of his own holographic nature. He is detestable. It's set to kill.

title: Darkling
line: You won't fire.

title: Darkling
line: Are you so certain? Stay close. It's about to get interesting.

title: Darkling
line: Captain, there's an unscheduled transport taking place in transporter room three.

title: Darkling
line: Find out what's going on.

title: Darkling
line: The operator's not responding.

title: Darkling
line: Computer, who just left the ship?

title: Darkling
line: Kes and the Doctor.

title: Darkling
line: Try to hail them.

title: Darkling
line: No response. And I can't get a fix on their positions. There's some kind of scattering field.

title: Darkling
line: Janeway to Chakotay.

title: Darkling
line: Chakotay here, Captain.

title: Darkling
line: Kes and the Doctor have left the ship.

title: Darkling
line: Captain, Tuvok here. My tricorder scans of the area where Zahir was assaulted have revealed disturbing evidence. Residual holographic signatures exactly like those of the Doctor.

title: Darkling
line: Are you suggesting the Doctor attacked Zahir?

title: Darkling
line: That's what it looks like, Captain

title: Darkling
line: Then Kes could be in danger. And Torres. Get someone from security down to Sickbay. Check on B'Elanna. Try and find them, Chakotay. I'll see what I can do about the scattering field.

title: Darkling
line: There must be a command sequence, an algorithm, a way to stabilize the program. Where's Nakahn? We had an arrangement. What's wrong with this thing? It won't work!

title: Darkling
line: Don't! Please stop.

title: Darkling
line: Concerned for me, or for your Doctor?

title: Darkling
line: The mobile emitter contains both your programs. If you damage it you could both be destroyed.

title: Darkling
line: There's not enough room inside for both of us. One must die. I deserve to exist more than your Doctor does.

title: Darkling
line: Why?

title: Darkling
line: I was born of the hidden, the suppressed. I am the dark threads from many personalities.

title: Darkling
line: The historical characters?

title: Darkling
line: None of whom could face the darkness inside so they denied me, suppressed me, frightened of the truth.

title: Darkling
line: What truth is that?

title: Darkling
line: That darkness is more fundamental than light. Cruelty before kindness. Evil more primary than good, more deserving of existence.

title: Darkling
line: You're wrong.

title: Darkling
line: No! How so?

title: Darkling
line: Empathy and kindness are basic to all forms of life. You have access to the Doctor's medical knowledge, you know what he does.

title: Darkling
line: Yes.

title: Darkling
line: Then you know what I'm saying is true. The very organs and cells of the body cooperate with each other, otherwise they wouldn't function.

title: Darkling
line: Continue.

title: Darkling
line: Families, societies, cultures, wouldn't have evolved without compassion and tolerance. They would have fallen apart without it. Your very own holographic technology would never have been developed without cooperation and understanding between countless individuals. The Doctor deserves to exist as much as you do. We can find a place for both of you.

title: Darkling
line: How?

title: Darkling
line: Sorry I'm late.

title: Darkling
line: The scout ship?

title: Darkling
line: It won't even leave the ground.

title: Darkling
line: What do you mean?

title: Darkling
line: Captain Janeway knows where you are. The ship is cordoned off, the entire area, to stop you from leaving.

title: Darkling
line: No!

title: Darkling
line: I still get paid. I held up my end of the deal. I booked your passage. It's not my fault they want her back so badly.

title: Darkling
line: I'll kill you.

title: Darkling
line: If somebody's going to die today, it won't be me.

title: Darkling
line: Let's go.

title: Darkling
line: Move faster. The docking port is two kilometers away.

title: Darkling
line: What's the point? You're forgetting Voyager's blockade.

title: Darkling
line: Doesn't matter. We'll take a low altitude ship to another continent. Come on!

title: Darkling
line: I'm tired.

title: Darkling
line: You're trying to make it easier for your colleagues to find us. You're better off with me.

title: Darkling
line: Why?

title: Darkling
line: You make wrong decisions. Too naive. You need my guidance.

title: Darkling
line: Don't you see what you've been trying to do?

title: Darkling
line: No more words. Now!

title: Darkling
line: I'm picking up residual infrared.

title: Darkling
line: They could have stopped here. Kes could have rested against this rock.

title: Darkling
line: The signature is consistent.

title: Darkling
line: Janeway to Chakotay.

title: Darkling
line: Go ahead, Captain.

title: Darkling
line: I've gotten through the Doctor's scattering field. Not

title: Darkling
line: Enough to beam them up yet but I've got a fix on their position. I'm downloading the coordinates into Tuvok's tricorder.

title: Darkling
line: I'll keep working on the scattering field.

title: Darkling
line: Acknowledged.

title: Darkling
line: We're within two hundred meters.

title: Darkling
line: It's finished. There's nowhere to go now, Doctor.

title: Darkling
line: Nowhere but down. I'll do it.

title: Darkling
line: His control over the Doctor's matrix appears to be deteriorating.

title: Darkling
line: If we can delay him. Doctor, listen to me. We can help you, create a new program matrix just for you on the holodeck or in sickbay, wherever you want to be. Just turn off the scattering field. Let us beam you back to the ship.

title: Darkling
line: You're trying to trick me.

title: Darkling
line: Doctor, listen! Think about all the things you've said and done. You don't want to kill me. You've been trying to protect me!

title: Darkling
line: What are you talking about?

title: Darkling
line: When you attacked Zahir.

title: Darkling
line: My first victim. He was in my way.

title: Darkling
line: Or was it to keep me from leaving with him?

title: Darkling
line: A coincidence. Only by chance.

title: Darkling
line: When I walked in on you on the holodeck you could have killed me, not knocked me unconscious.

title: Darkling
line: I needed a hostage.

title: Darkling
line: You said you were taking me for my own good, to prevent me from making the wrong decisions. You said I was naive and needed your help. That's not what you say to a hostage. In your own way, you've been trying to protect me.

title: Darkling
