line: I am the son of K'vok! And you, what House are you from?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Is this some kind of a joke?

title: Infinite Regress
line: You wear the uniform of a Starfleet P'Cha! What kind of a warrior are you?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Tom put you up to this, didn't he? Well, it didn't work.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Come, warrior, let me look at you.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Enough, Seven.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Your blood is sweet!

title: Infinite Regress
line: Torres to Security. Get somebody down here right now.

title: Infinite Regress
line: You are strong. You will make an excellent mate.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Get the hell away from me!

title: Infinite Regress
line: You wish to prove yourself in battle.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Report.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Seven of Nine attacked B'Elanna in Engineering. She's on deck nine, section twenty three.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Forcefields. Don't tell me those two have actually come to blows.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Bridge to Tuvok. Seven's been contained. Deck ten, section thirty two.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Acknowledged. We're nearing her position.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Seven?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Somebody's hurt and he needs help. Did I do something bad?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Who are you?

title: Infinite Regress
line: My name's Maryl. Are you a Vulcan?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Computer, deactivate forcefield. Give me the phaser.

title: Infinite Regress
line: You are not a physician, Commander. The logical course of action would be to take him to the infirmary.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Maryl?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Subaltern Lorot, Vulcan High Command. May I be of assistance?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Yes. Please accompany me to Sickbay.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Certainly. Clearly he was attacked. I suggest we use caution. PetaQ! You will drown in your own blood.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Keep moving.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Seven.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Captain, why am I here?

title: Infinite Regress
line: You've been unconscious for nearly two hours. We believe you're experiencing a neurological disorder.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Voices, I hear voices. They are agitated, chaotic. Too many voices.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Too many voices.

title: Infinite Regress
line: The cortical inhibitor is destabilizing. I'm increasing the neurotransmitter levels. It's working. Do you still hear the voices?

title: Infinite Regress
line: They are fading. They are gone.

title: Infinite Regress
line: All right. Let's see what we can do to keep them from coming back. What's the last thing you remember?

title: Infinite Regress
line: I was in Engineering, assisting Lieutenant Torres.

title: Infinite Regress
line: You have no recollection of a confrontation with B'Elanna?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Confrontation?

title: Infinite Regress
line: I'm not sure why, but you seem to be manifesting personalities other than your own.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Naomi Wildman claims the two of you played together for nearly an hour this afternoon.

title: Infinite Regress
line: You also attacked Lieutenant Torres. She told us you called yourself Son of K'vok and that you initiated a Klingon mating ritual.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I have no memory of those events.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Come look at this.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Doctor.

title: Infinite Regress
line: This is your neural pattern. The memory engrams and synaptic pathways that define you as an individual. Unfortunately, you're not alone. Thirteen new neural patterns have emerged in your cerebral cortex. Klingon, Vulcan, Terrelian, Human and several others I can't identify.

title: Infinite Regress
line: How?

title: Infinite Regress
line: They're coming from within you. During your time with the Borg, the Collective assimilated hundreds of different species. All of those neural patterns were integrated into the Hive Mind.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Of course.

title: Infinite Regress
line: That means they're in your mind too, stored within your cortical implants. Dormant until now.

title: Infinite Regress
line: From what we can tell, the various neural patterns are surfacing randomly.

title: Infinite Regress
line: In essence, you've developed the Borg equivalent of Multiple Personality Disorder.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Can you correct the malfunction?

title: Infinite Regress
line: The cortical inhibitor is suppressing the effect, but it's only a temporary measure.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Lieutenant Torres detected a Borg interlink frequency. It could be causing my cortical implants to malfunction.

title: Infinite Regress
line: The signal appears to be emanating from the Borg debris field we discovered this morning.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Maybe we should jump to warp, try to get out of range.

title: Infinite Regress
line: The signal permeates subspace. We cannot avoid it.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Our only hope is to terminate the signal at its point of origin.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Set a course for the debris field. When we arrive we may need your help. Feel up to it?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Yes, Captain.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Keep a close eye on her, Doctor, in case she has any more unexpected visitors.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Has any drone ever experienced symptoms like these before?

title: Infinite Regress
line: The Collective does not tolerate imperfection. Any drone with a malfunction as serious as mine would be destroyed immediately.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Lucky for you, this crew is a little more tolerant.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Oh, there you are. Lieutenant Torres tells me you're under the weather.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Correct.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Well, is there anything your Morale officer can do to help? Assignments you need me to finish while you recuperate?

title: Infinite Regress
line: No.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I have some wonderful medicinal teas. Maybe I could prepare one for you?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Talaxian homeopathy. I don't think we're quite that desperate yet.

title: Infinite Regress
line: How about if I make one of your favorite nutritional supplements?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Your concern has been noted. The Doctor will inform you when I am functional again.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Right. Sorry. Oh! Ah, I almost forgot. It's from Naomi Wildman. It's a drawing of Voyager, or maybe it's an asteroid belt. I'm not sure. Naomi thought it might make you feel better.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Tell her thank you.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I suspected as much. There were several interruptions in your regeneration cycle. Eighteen minutes, five minutes, one hour.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I don't recall them.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Let's examine your neural function logs. Low serotonin levels during regeneration, that's normal. But look at these spikes in the pre-frontal synapses. They appear only seconds before you left the alcove. You were sleepwalking.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I don't remember entering this data file.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Looks like we found the identity of the Midnight Snacker. I'm sure Mister Neelix will be relieved.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Personal log, Ensign Stone, Stardate 52188.7. I just completed my first week of active duty. It was a nightmare. After four years at the Academy I thought I was ready for anything, but Captain Blackwood runs a tight ship, and he seems to take special pleasure in tormenting new recruits. The First Officer tells me not to take it personally, but it's hard to be objective when

title: Infinite Regress
line: Blackwood. Captain of the Federation Starship Tombaugh. The Borg assimilated that vessel thirteen years ago.

title: Infinite Regress
line: The individual who made this recording must have been a member of the crew.

title: Infinite Regress
line: One of my victims.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Here's another log entry. This one encoded for transmission.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Hi. Guess who? I know I promised to write you every day but that's simply not enough. How about once in the morning when I resuscitate and once at night before I go into torpor, and I'll think about you non-stop in between. Wait, I've got a better idea. Why don't you leave your circle and visit the colony? You'd love it here, so

title: Infinite Regress
line: Anything familiar?

title: Infinite Regress
line: I helped to assimilate thousands of individuals. I do not remember each of their names.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Seven, you were a Borg drone who's now becoming an individual. That's practically unheard of. There's bound to be rough spots along the way. We just have to get past them.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Bridge to Seven of Nine. We're approaching the debris field.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Acknowledged.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Survivors?

title: Infinite Regress
line: None.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Any sign of Borg vessels?

title: Infinite Regress
line: No, sir. We're the first ones here.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I'm picking up the source of the interlink frequency. Bearing oh two seven mark three.

title: Infinite Regress
line: On screen. Magnify.

title: Infinite Regress
line: It's a Borg vinculum.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Vinculum?

title: Infinite Regress
line: The processing device at the core of every Borg vessel. It interconnects the minds of all the drones. It purges individual thoughts and disseminates information relevant to the Collective.

title: Infinite Regress
line: It brings order to chaos.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Precisely.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Looks like this one has established a link to your cortical implant.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I believe it has identified me as an errant drone. It is attempting to reintegrate me into the Collective. The Vinculum is malfunctioning. It is sending me erratic commands.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Bringing chaos to order.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Yes.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Can you sever the link?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Not without risking permanent damage to my own systems. The Vinculum must be taken offline. Permission to beam it aboard for analysis. I have worked with this technology before. I may be able to disable it.

title: Infinite Regress
line: We're talking about the heart of a Borg cube. I'd rather not take it inside my ship. Can you disable it remotely?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Yes, but I would need several days. The Borg may return by then. I recommend we take the Vinculum and leave this region immediately.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Tuvok, prepare to beam it to Engineering. Erect a level ten forcefield and maintain constant surveillance. The moment it poses a threat, send it back into space. Tom, as soon as it's aboard, get us out of here. Warp nine.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Aye, Captain.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I understand what you're going through, and I want to help you in every way I can, but the safety of this crew is my first responsibility. We haven't had the best of luck with the Borg.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Nor have I.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Let's keep an eye on those antigrav struts. Boylen, lock out all primary command consoles and reroute transporter controls to main Engineering.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Yes, Lieutenant.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Seven?

title: Infinite Regress
line: The voices. I hear them.

title: Infinite Regress
line: It's your proximity to the Vinculum. The link is stronger here. I'm adjusting your neurotransmitter levels. You'd better get started.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Don't worry, Lieutenant. The Son of K'vok will not be joining us.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Glad to hear it. Does this qualify as our second date?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Just think of me as your chaperone.

title: Infinite Regress
line: So, where's the off switch?

title: Infinite Regress
line: The Vinculum is equipped with many safeguards. I will need to access its transneural matrix and disable it directly.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I'm reading a power surge.

title: Infinite Regress
line: It's a normal response to my intrusion. Don't be alarmed. Curious. I'm detecting an organism within the Vinculum. It appears to be a viral agent.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Let's see it. It's a synthetic pathogen. The virus was originally a biological agent but it's mutated. It's attacking the Vinculum's programs as it would living cells.

title: Infinite Regress
line: An organism that attacks technology?

title: Infinite Regress
line: The Cube was infected three days ago, shortly after assimilating an alien shuttlecraft. Species 6339. They were the last ones to come in contact with the cube.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Looks like we found our Typhoid Mary.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Species 6339, Humanoid. Warp-capable. Origin, grid one two four, octant twenty two theta. They first encountered the Borg approximately four years ago. Since that time, eleven billion individuals have been assimilated. Three days ago, the Collective detected one of their last surviving shuttlecraft. A Cube was sent to intercept it.

title: Infinite Regress
line: We believe the virus was carried within their bodies. Once they were assimilated, it spread to the Vinculum.

title: Infinite Regress
line: The drones aboard no doubt experienced symptoms similar to my own. It is no surprise they destroyed themselves.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I'd like to find species 6339. They may be able to help us treat you. Begin long range Astrometric scans. See if they have any more vessels in this region.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Yes, Captain. I've already begun a spatial diagn. My, my, my, look at the size of that thing. This viewscreen. It's got to be one of the biggest I've ever seen. I'll give you twenty bars of latinum for it.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I think the inhibitor's gone offline. Would you come here, please?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Be quiet. Can't you see I'm in the middle of a deal? Name your price, Captain?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Janeway. And you are?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Daimon Torrot.

title: Infinite Regress
line: You're Ferengi.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Of course I'm Ferengi. Is that some kind of insult about the size of my ears?

title: Infinite Regress
line: No, not at all. I'd be happy to negotiate with you, but first we have to get you to Sickbay.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Sickbay? What for?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Because you're ill.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I've never felt better.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Doctor.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I'm afraid you've contracted a nasty strain of the Ankaran flu. We've been treating you several days. Remember?

title: Infinite Regress
line: No.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Short term memory loss. It's one of the symptoms. Don't worry, it isn't life threatening, but we'll need to treat you. In Sickbay.

title: Infinite Regress
line: What is this treatment going to cost me?

title: Infinite Regress
line: It's free of charge.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Free?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Yes.

title: Infinite Regress
line: You know, I have been having a nagging pain in my lower left lobe, and while you're at it why don't you run a complete tricardial diagnostic. The Ferengi Health Commission's trying to revoke my trading license.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Impressive vessel, Captain. Galaxy class?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Intrepid.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Ah. Ah, and here we are in the much talked-about Sickbay. Not exactly state of the medical art now, is it?

title: Infinite Regress
line: What do you mean?

title: Infinite Regress
line: You're low on biobeds, terrible lighting, obsolete instruments. Lucky for you, I know a medical supplier that can spruce this place up in a nanosecond, and I'll even drop my commission to a mere thirty percent?

title: Infinite Regress
line: How generous of you. Computer, activate forcefield.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Forcefield? You said I wasn't contagious.

title: Infinite Regress
line: It's for your own safety. I've set the cortical inhibitor to maximum but it is no longer suppressing the effects. These personalities are going to keep surfacing.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I've been kidnapped!

title: Infinite Regress
line: Even more reason to shut down the Vinculum as soon as we can.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Even if we do break the link, it may be too late. Seven's own neural pattern is destabilizing. It could be lost.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Please help me. I'm looking for my son Gregory Bergan, Lieutenant Bergan. Have you seen him?

title: Infinite Regress
line: No, I'm afraid not.

title: Infinite Regress
line: From the starship Melbourne.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Melbourne?

title: Infinite Regress
line: I was supposed to meet him at Wolf 359, but Starfleet sent out a warning that the Borg were attacking that sector. It was too late for us to turn back. We were caught in a terrible battle. My ship was badly damaged. We had to leave on escape pods. I never found out what happened to Gregory. Please, I haven't heard from him in over three days. Could you check with Starfleet Headquarters?

title: Infinite Regress
line: I'll see what I can do.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Thank you, Captain. If you do speak with him, could you tell him that his mother is all right and if he could pos... Captain.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Seven?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Yes. The Vinculum?

title: Infinite Regress
line: We're preparing to shut it down right away. I'll give the order as soon as Torres is ready.

title: Infinite Regress
line: How long was I absent?

title: Infinite Regress
line: About twenty minutes.

title: Infinite Regress
line: How many?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Two. One of whom wanted to acquire half the items on the ship. Daimon Torrot, I believe.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Species 180, Ferengi.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Yes. The other was a woman whose son was lost in a Borg attack. You'll get through this, Seven.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I do not share your optimism.

title: Infinite Regress
line: When you took me from the Borg and began to turn me into an individual, I found the silence of my own mind difficult to bear. I missed the voices of the Collective. But now that I am an individual, those same voices frighten me. Captain, I don't know if I can tolerate this condition much longer. My courage is insufficient.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Your job is to keep trying to hold on even when you think you can't. Leave the rest to me and the crew.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Meet anyone interesting?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Just finished swapping jokes with a Bolian manicurist. Before that, I was debating the finer points of temporal physics with a Krenim scientist. Twelve new personalities have surfaced in the past hour alone. Seven's having a rough time of it. The Doctor had to sedate her.

title: Infinite Regress
line: How's the Captain holding up?

title: Infinite Regress
line: I've been better, Chakotay. In fact, I'm starting to wonder if my First Officer was right all along.

title: Infinite Regress
line: About what?

title: Infinite Regress
line: You always said that bringing Seven into the fold might be impossible.

title: Infinite Regress
line: You can take the Borg out of the Collective, but. I don't believe that. Not anymore. I didn't think she'd last a day, much less a year. I'd say you've proven me wrong.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Torres to Bridge. We're ready to begin disabling the Vinculum.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Proceed.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Target the transneural matrix. Stand by to initiate the dampening field on my mark. Three, two, one, mark. Its power output is dropping.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Doctor to bridge. It seems to be working. Her neural pattern is stabilizing.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Power output is down to seventy seven percent. Seventy one percent. Wait a second. It's increasing.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I'm refocusing the dampening field.

title: Infinite Regress
line: It's still increasing.

title: Infinite Regress
line: The Vinculum is rerouting its internal circuitry. It's adapting.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Engineering! Her synaptic pathways are destabilizing. Abort the procedure!

title: Infinite Regress
line: Help me!

title: Infinite Regress
line: Abort!

title: Infinite Regress
line: Stand by, Doctor. Power output at ninety eight percent. The forcefield is collapsing.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Transfer emergency power.

title: Infinite Regress
line: It won't work, Lieutenant. We must abort. Tuvok to bridge.

title: Infinite Regress
line: The procedure was unsuccessful. The Vinculum has returned to full power.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Acknowledged. Doctor, report.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Seven's neural pattern has disappeared, Captain. It appears that the other patterns have taken over completely. We've lost her.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Captain's log, supplemental. Long range sensors have detected a vessel belonging to species 6339. We've set a course to intercept them in the hopes they can help us restore Seven of Nine.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I've managed to stabilize her primary cortical functions but the woman in Sickbay is not Seven of Nine. Not any more. New personalities are emerging every few seconds now. She can't finish a sentence before the next one rears its head. It's creating an incredible strain on her cerebral cortex. If we don't deactivate the Vinculum soon, we may never get her back.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Tuvok?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Lieutenant Torres is taking measures to prevent the Vinculum from adapting, but there's no guarantee she'll succeed.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Captain, I've exhausted every viable treatment in my database.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Then logic dictates we go beyond medical science. I will attempt to mind meld with Seven of Nine.

title: Infinite Regress
line: A mind meld? You consider that a viable treatment?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Seven's neural pattern, her sense of self, is immersed in chaos. I will attempt to isolate her true self and guide it to the surface.

title: Infinite Regress
line: It's dangerous enough to meld with one person, let alone hundreds of different personalities.

title: Infinite Regress
line: It's too risky.

title: Infinite Regress
line: The risk is mine to take.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I'm aware of that, but is this our only option?

title: Infinite Regress
line: I believe it is, Captain.

title: Infinite Regress
line: How long would you need to prepare?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Captain, you can't actually be considering this Vulcan mumbo jumbo.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I will require two hours of meditation.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Begin immediately. Report to Sickbay when you're ready.

title: Infinite Regress
line: You said it yourself. We've exhausted every medical treatment.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I just hope I don't find myself with a second patient.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Captain to the bridge.

title: Infinite Regress
line: On my way.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Commander?

title: Infinite Regress
line: It's them. Species 6339.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Their vessel is well-armed, Captain. I'm picking up twenty two phaser cannons on the aft section alone.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Hail them.

title: Infinite Regress
line: They're responding.

title: Infinite Regress
line: On screen. I'm Captain Janeway of the Federation Starship Voyager. We recently found a piece of Borg technology. It's been infected with a viral agent we believe was transmitted by your

title: Infinite Regress
line: The Vinculum, you have it?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Yes.

title: Infinite Regress
line: You've made a terrible mistake, Captain.

title: Infinite Regress
line: A weapon?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Yes. Since the Borg decimated our world, we've been looking for ways to retaliate.

title: Infinite Regress
line: So you created a virus to infect their technology.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Thirteen of my people were injected with the virus. They allowed themselves to be assimilated so that the virus would spread to this Vinculum. Once another Borg ship had retrieved it they would be infected as well. Then another Cube, and another. We had the opportunity to infect dozens, even hundreds of Borg vessels until you interfered. Why?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Your virus has had one unexpected casualty. A member of my crew.

title: Infinite Regress
line: It wasn't designed to infect other species.

title: Infinite Regress
line: She's Borg.

title: Infinite Regress
line: We liberated her from the Collective over a year ago. She's an individual now.

title: Infinite Regress
line: We were hoping you could help us treat her.

title: Infinite Regress
line: We designed that virus to destroy Borg, Captain. We never considered a treatment. I'm afraid your drone won't survive. But we must return the Vinculum to the debris field immediately. If the Borg arrive first, we'll have lost our chance, and those thirteen people will have died in vain.

title: Infinite Regress
line: All right. We'll return it to you, but first we need to try to save our crew member. We think we have a way to counteract the Vinculum's effects. B'Elanna?

title: Infinite Regress
line: I'm going to try to remodulate our dampening field to compensate

title: Infinite Regress
line: We don't have time for this. The Vinculum, Captain.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I can't give it to you. Not yet.

title: Infinite Regress
line: You scanned our vessel, you're aware of our firepower.

title: Infinite Regress
line: You could undoubtedly do significant damage to Voyager, and to the Vinculum. Is that what you want?

title: Infinite Regress
line: The Vinculum survived the destruction of one ship. What makes you so sure it won't survive another?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Doctor.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Seven. A necessary precaution. A few of your guests have been violent.

title: Infinite Regress
line: The Vinculum.

title: Infinite Regress
line: It keeps adapting. We haven't been able to shut it down. Your own neural pattern was nearly destroyed in the process. I wasn't sure I'd find you again.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I am damaged.

title: Infinite Regress
line: One of your personas didn't appreciate the restraints. She seemed intent on forcing her way to freedom.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I apologize.

title: Infinite Regress
line: It was hardly your fault. You're ill.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Irrelevant. I am Borg. I should be able to adapt.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Surprise. You aren't invincible. I suppose that's something we'll have to tackle in our next social lesson. Voices?

title: Infinite Regress
line: They're getting louder.

title: Infinite Regress
line: It won't be long before I lose you again. It's my duty as your physician to inform you of an alternative treatment.

title: Infinite Regress
line: What treatment?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Commander Tuvok has proposed a mind meld to help stabilize your neural pattern. I had a similar reaction. If you don't approve.

title: Infinite Regress
line: What is the probability of success?

title: Infinite Regress
line: I don't know. A mind meld is hardly a standard medical practice.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Are there any risks to Tuvok?

title: Infinite Regress
line: He could suffer brain damage, but he's confident he'll be able to break the meld before that happens.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Even if we do shut down the Vinculum, it may not be enough. If Tuvok can do anything to help me.

title: Infinite Regress
line: I understand.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Doctor, you have shown a great deal of patience.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Not at all.

title: Infinite Regress
line: Inform the crew that I am also grateful for their efforts.

title: Infinite Regress
line: You'll be able to tell them yourself, afterwards. Seven?

title: Infinite Regress
line: Voices!

title: Infinite Regress
line: Concentrate! Focus on the sound of my voice!

title: Infinite Regress
line: Get them out, please! I can't, I can't! No!

title: Infinite Regress
line: Report.

title: Infinite Regress
line: The alien vessel is coming about.

title: Infinite Regress
line: They're charging weapons.

line: You stood by me when most people would have run for the nearest airlock. You were willing to see past my shortcomings, and to take all the bumps and bruises that came along with it. You made me a better person, even though I put up one hell of a fight. I look forward to our journey together.

title: Course: Oblivion
line: You may not want to know. Captain's log, stardate 52586.3. We've had a lot to celebrate lately. Tom and B'Elanna's wedding, Ensign Harper's new baby, and the continued health of our warp drive, which has taken us within striking distance of home.

line: Here's a lovely program modeled after a mountain resort on the fifth moon of Cytax. Just you, B'Elanna, and the crickets.

line: Cytaxian crickets. Their song is reputed to be an auditory aphrodisiac.

line: Let me let you in on a little secret, Neelix. Earth has the best vacation spots in the galaxy. It's got the cultures, the climates, the history, the people. It has everything you ever want in a planet.

line: I guess I am being a little overcautious. I've just, er, never been away from Engineering for more than a couple of days. Certainly never a week.

line: It's our warp field. The enhanced drive is emitting some form of subspace radiation that's affecting Voyager's infrastructure.

title: Course: Oblivion
line: It's beginning to break down the molecular bonds in all surrounding sections.

line: We're seeing early stages of the effect in the warp core. Reaction chamber, injector ports, they're all showing signs of de-cohesion.

line: It doesn't make any sense. We knew about the subspace radiation and we ran dozens of simulations before we brought the new drive online.

line: Try to isolate the cause of this, and stabilize the sections that have already been affected. Dismissed.

line: We haven't been able to narrow the time frame precisely, but it appears that anything brought on board over the past thirty to forty weeks is immune.

line: Ten months, eleven days ago. Voyager was forced to land on a class Y planetoid in the Vaskan sector.

title: Course: Oblivion
line: The Demon class planet. One of our more interesting missions. We set down looking for deuterium and ended up helping a new form of life to be born.

title: Course: Oblivion

title: Course: Oblivion
line: The silver blood. It sampled our DNA and created duplicates of the entire crew.

title: Course: Oblivion
line: I've often wondered what happened to them. Are they flourishing? Have they continued to evolve?

title: Course: Oblivion

title: Course: Oblivion

line: That wasn't B'Elanna. It was a duplicate. A biomimetic copy.

title: Course: Oblivion

title: Course: Oblivion
line: I was born on Earth in Indiana. I remember growing up there. I remember graduating from the Academy. I have no memory of being a copy.

line: Apparently, the original Kathryn Janeway's memories were duplicated as well. Somehow, after the real Voyager left, we began to forget we were duplicates.

title: Course: Oblivion
line: Eventually, we assumed their lives and set a course for Earth.

title: Course: Oblivion
line: And now the warp core is breaking down our cellular structure. We didn't think the radiation would hurt us because it isn't harmful to humanoids.

title: Course: Oblivion

title: Course: Oblivion
line: Duplicate or not, I'm still the same person I was yesterday and so are all of you, and that means we're going to do everything possible to complete our mission, which is to reach Earth. Is that clear?

title: Course: Oblivion
line: I want you to adjust the environmental controls to simulate a class Y planet. That should slow the rate of degradation.

title: Course: Oblivion

title: Course: Oblivion
line: I realize that. That's why we're going to try and find a safe harbor till we can figure out a way to stop the degradation. Scan for the nearest class Y planet and set a course. In the meantime, I'll explain our situation to the crew.

title: Course: Oblivion
line: There's still a great deal we don't know about this phenomenon, and I have every confidence we'll find a way to reverse it.

line: So you're saying all our experiences before we were duplicated, none of it's real?

title: Course: Oblivion
line: I don't pretend to understand it myself, Harry, but the way I choose to look at it is this. title: Course: Oblivion
line: But there is another crew out there, right? The real Voyager.

line: The same as it's always been, Tom. To reach the Alpha Quadrant safe and sound. The less you exert yourselves, the slower the cellular decay. Duplicates or not, you're still my crew. Dismissed.

title: Course: Oblivion

line: I've spent the past five years trying to get this crew home. I'm not about to quit now.

line: There's only one thing I know how to be, Chakotay, and that's Kathryn Janeway.

line: I've tried everything I could think of. Biomolecular enhancers, gene splicing with replicated DNA, and I'm no closer to finding a cure. But I do have an idea.

line: I'm only asking because I'm curious how much they're paying? Maybe we can do better.

title: Think Tank
line: Doubtful.

title: Think Tank
line: We're far from defenseless. Why don't you save yourself some trouble.

title: Think Tank
line: It's no trouble.

title: Think Tank
line: Charge phaser banks to full power.

title: Think Tank
line: Fire and you'll ignite the gas cloud. You'll be destroyed.

title: Think Tank
line: You've left me no choice. I suggest you back off if you want to save your own ship. End transmission.

title: Think Tank
line: They are moving closer. They've locked on a tractor beam.

title: Think Tank
line: Looks like they're calling your bluff, Captain. It was a bluff, wasn't it?

title: Think Tank
line: Seven, do we still have warp power?

title: Think Tank
line: Yes, but it's useless while we remain in the gas cloud.

title: Think Tank
line: Maybe not. Reroute every spare gigawatt to the shields. Prepare to fire phasers.

title: Think Tank
line: Our target?

title: Think Tank
line: The gas cloud.

title: Think Tank
line: Do you believe the impact will throw us clear?

title: Think Tank
line: If our shields hold.

title: Think Tank
line: That's a big if.

title: Think Tank
line: Go to warp one on my command. Fire.

title: Think Tank
line: Shields are holding. We're approaching the perimeter of the gas cloud.

title: Think Tank
line: We're out.

title: Think Tank
line: Warp speed.

title: Think Tank
line: No sign of pursuit.

title: Think Tank
line: They weren't that heavily damaged. Why aren't they following us?

title: Think Tank
line: There's the reason they didn't come after us. They've got reinforcements throughout the sector.

title: Think Tank
line: Twenty three ships.

title: Think Tank
line: And long range scans show more on the way.

title: Think Tank
line: Must be one hell of a reward.

title: Think Tank
line: The size of the bounty is immaterial. According to Seven of Nine, the Hazari pride themselves on honoring their agreements.

title: Think Tank
line: Great. Bounty hunters with a work ethic.

title: Think Tank
line: There's got to be a way out, something they haven't anticipated. Download the data for the Captain. She wants to see what she can come up with on her own.

title: Think Tank
line: Should I have the Doctor prepare a hypospray?

title: Think Tank
line: Excuse me?

title: Think Tank
line: So you can absorb the caffeine more directly. Save time.

title: Think Tank
line: Point well taken. I'll make this my last cup.

title: Think Tank
line: How about trying a sounding board?

title: Think Tank
line: Oh, you don't want that job.

title: Think Tank
line: Try me.

title: Think Tank
line: It's these Hazari. They're like jackals, circling, feinting to draw us out while they cut off every route of escape.

title: Think Tank
line: You make them sound worse than the Borg.

title: Think Tank
line: At least the Borg come straight at you. The Hazari wait, invite you to make mistakes. They've anticipated almost every move we can make, and the few things they seem to have missed, I'm convinced are traps. You still glad you volunteered?

title: Think Tank
line: We've faced tough odds before. You'll get us through. Goodnight.

title: Think Tank
line: Goodnight.

title: Think Tank
line: There is nothing like a good problem to spark the synapses, is there? To open the mind to new possibilities, new ways of seeing things. Of course, one must always confront self- doubt and fear, but that is a small price to pay for the exhilaration of finding the perfect solution.

title: Think Tank
line: Who are you and what do you want?

title: Think Tank
line: You have a problem, Captain. I am the solution.

title: Think Tank
line: Security to the Mess hall. Intruder alert

title: Think Tank
line: I've deactivated your communications device, Captain, but do not worry. I am not an intruder. In fact, I am not really here.

title: Think Tank
line: A hologram.

title: Think Tank
line: Nothing so crude. An isomorphic projection.

title: Think Tank
line: You actually enjoy this?

title: Think Tank
line: It's an acquired taste.

title: Think Tank
line: It bears a resemblance to an Alkian confection we acquired several years ago.

title: Think Tank
line: We?

title: Think Tank
line: I am a member of a small group. Explorers, like you. But we seek out challenges, problems to be solved. Technological, biological, social, even artistic.

title: Think Tank
line: A Think Tank.

title: Think Tank
line: I like that. It's very apt. Our Think Tank is nearby. A modest vessel. I have come to offer our help with your Hazari paradox.

title: Think Tank
line: Paradox?

title: Think Tank
line: That is right. Is it an escape route or is it a trap? Do they know that you know that they know? It is the best kind of puzzle. Pure tactics, psychology.

title: Think Tank
line: Something tells me your help comes with a price tag.

title: Think Tank
line: Whatever your culture has to offer that is unique. Technology perhaps, or maybe something you would not even think to value. I would need a closer look at your database.

title: Think Tank
line: And how do I know you aren't an Hazari trap? Maybe they're trying to lure us into an ambush, like before.

title: Think Tank
line: You are wise to be suspicious, Captain. We have done some preliminary analysis on their maneuvers. It does suggest some more likely ambushes. I've downloaded the data onto your computer.

title: Think Tank
line: All right. You've got my attention. But I want to meet you face to face. And the rest of your crew.

title: Think Tank
line: Naturally. Our coordinates are in here, too. But we have our own security concerns, Captain. Please, bring only one crewman and no scanning equipment.

title: Think Tank
line: Fair enough.

title: Think Tank
line: Then I look forward to meeting you in person.

title: Think Tank
line: We're approaching the coordinates.

title: Think Tank
line: Full stop.

title: Think Tank
line: Looks like there's nothing here.

title: Think Tank
line: Maybe they're cloaked.

title: Think Tank
line: I'm reading a subspace flux.

title: Think Tank
line: The vessel's hull is composed of a neutronium-based alloy.

title: Think Tank
line: Starfleet's theorized about such materials, but we've never come close to producing them.

title: Think Tank
line: Neither have the Borg. The Think Tank's technology is advanced.

title: Think Tank
line: Well, you and I will have the chance to evaluate it first hand. Mister Kim, you have the transport coordinates.

title: Think Tank
line: The universal translator must be inoperative.

title: Think Tank
line: Or his speech patterns are too complex to process.

title: Think Tank
line: They must be studying it.

title: Think Tank
line: Actually, she is studying you. Our resident expert on temporal physics. Perhaps the most gifted member of our group. She finds you interesting.

title: Think Tank
line: How do you communicate?

title: Think Tank
line: One of my most gifted crewmen, Seven of Nine.

title: Think Tank
line: Bionetic implants, neural transceivers? A Borg? I've never seen one outside the Collective.

title: Think Tank
line: I am an individual now. You may address your comments to me.

title: Think Tank
line: Forgive me. I am Kurros, and this is Fennim. In answer to your earlier question, this device allows the members of our group to communicate telepathically.

title: Think Tank
line: Impressive.

title: Think Tank
line: It sounds as if another member of our crew is anxious to meet you.

title: Think Tank
line: A bioplasmic lifeform.

title: Think Tank
line: His name is Bevvox. He prefers a variable gravity environment.

title: Think Tank
line: What's his specialty?

title: Think Tank
line: At the moment exo-sociology and quantum mechanics, but his interests vary from time to time. Bevvox founded our group more than one hundred years ago, after wandering the galaxy on his own for a few millennia.

title: Think Tank
line: How old is this creature?

title: Think Tank
line: If you please, that is a sensitive topic with him. And there is one other individual who rounds out our group.

title: Think Tank
line: An artificial intelligence.

title: Think Tank
line: The mind of mathematician and the soul of an artist. I'm afraid he'd much rather be modeling a fractal sculpture than analyzing the data of our latest astronomical scan. And now you have met us all. A small group of minds, but we have helped hundreds of clients. We turned the tide in the war between the Bara Plenum and the Motali Empire. Re-ignited the red giants of the Zai Cluster. Just recently, we found a cure for the Vidiian phage.

title: Think Tank
line: The Vidiians?

title: Think Tank
line: You would hardly recognize them now. Just last month we helped retrieve a Lyridian child's runaway pet. A subspace mesomorph, I might add. We had to invent a whole new scanning technology just to find it.

title: Think Tank
line: And what did you ask for as compensation?

title: Think Tank
line: One of their transgalactic star charts. The best map of the known galaxy ever created. When we helped the citizens of Rivos Five resist the Borg, all we asked for was the recipe for their famous zoth-nut soup. Care for a taste?

title: Think Tank
line: Another time, perhaps.

title: Think Tank
line: Tell me, is there any job you won't do?

title: Think Tank
line: What do you mean?

title: Think Tank
line: Well, we have a non-interference protocol, our Prime Directive. I'm curious where you draw the line.

title: Think Tank
line: As you know, there is no shortage of conflict in what you call the Delta Quadrant. Many of our clients are at war. To be frank, we will assist in the neutralization of fleets, starbases, even planets. But we will not participate in the decimation of an entire species, nor will we design weapons of mass destruction. My colleague here wishes to speak to Seven of Nine about her bionetic technology. May he interface with you?

title: Think Tank
line: I am in direct telepathic communication with this individual. It is requesting information about integrating organic components into its technology.

title: Think Tank
line: Feel free to give him some pointers.

title: Think Tank
line: You're welcome.

title: Think Tank
line: To business, Captain. I believe we can solve the Hazari paradox without firing a single weapon.

title: Think Tank
line: That's just what I'm looking for.

title: Think Tank
line: Then there is only the matter of payment.

title: Think Tank
line: Voyager's schematics and an overview of its database. Specify what you want and I'll see what I can do. I recommend the replicators. They're very popular this year.

title: Think Tank
line: I'll contact you with our requests.

title: Think Tank
line: I take it First Contact was a success?

title: Think Tank
line: I have some qualms about their morality, but I believe they can help us.

title: Think Tank
line: It was an interesting experience.

title: Think Tank
line: Glad to hear it. We don't have much good news of our own. Every escape route we've considered is clearly a trap, and more Hazari ships keep joining the search.

title: Think Tank
line: Then we have no choice. We'll put our own plans on hold and see what the Think Tank comes up with.

title: Think Tank
line: Come in.

title: Think Tank
line: You have a visitor. Mister Kurros has returned in isomorphic form.

title: Think Tank
line: Send him in. Welcome back.

title: Think Tank
line: Captain, we have compiled a short list of items we would like. It was not easy. Voyager has a great deal to offer.

title: Think Tank
line: Quantum slipstream technology. I should warn you. We never got that to work reliably.

title: Think Tank
line: It is still intriguing, theoretically.

title: Think Tank
line: Neelix's recipe for Chadre'kab?

title: Think Tank
line: Yes.

title: Think Tank
line: An ancient Olmec figurine. I guess Commander Chakotay can be persuaded to part with it.

title: Think Tank
line: I am pleased to hear that.

title: Think Tank
line: You can't be serious.

title: Think Tank
line: I realize the next item may seem unorthodox, but I believe it can be beneficial to both of us.

title: Think Tank
line: You never mentioned anything about bartering my crew members.

title: Think Tank
line: She will have an extraordinary opportunity to explore the galaxy as one of us.

title: Think Tank
line: I'm afraid the answer is no.

title: Think Tank
line: I understand your feelings, Captain, but have you thought to ask Seven of Nine herself?

title: Think Tank
line: A curious proposition.

title: Think Tank
line: To say the least.

title: Think Tank
line: How do you wish to proceed?

title: Think Tank
line: I want your opinion.

title: Think Tank
line: They are offering us the assistance we require, I am the payment they require. The solution is obvious.

title: Think Tank
line: This isn't a puzzle, Seven. There is no solution. What's at issue here is your future.

title: Think Tank
line: The issue is Voyager's survival.

title: Think Tank
line: Sit. Please. While I still question this Think Tank's way of doing things, there is a genuine opportunity for exploration. It could be the chance of a lifetime.

title: Think Tank
line: You're saying I should go?

title: Think Tank
line: I don't want you to go, but it's not my right to tell you what to do. Until now, I've kept a close eye on your progress, helped you with decisions but, I think you've learned enough as an individual to make this decision yourself. Would you like to join them?

title: Think Tank
line: I am intrigued. They are an unusual Collective with a compelling mission. But I require more data.

title: Think Tank
line: That's why I want you to talk to Kurros yourself. See if he can answer your questions.

title: Think Tank
line: Captain, I appreciate your giving me this choice.

title: Think Tank
line: You've earned it. And remember, if you do choose to go, make sure it's what you want, not what you think is best for Voyager. We're getting out of this, with or without the Think Tank's help.

title: Think Tank
line: Why me?

title: Think Tank
line: I admire your humility. The collective knowledge of the Borg contained within a single mind. When we factor in your innate intelligence and the enhancements afforded you by your bionetic implants, we concluded you are an ideal candidate. The first we have recruited in seventeen years.

title: Think Tank
line: When did you arrive at this assessment?

title: Think Tank
line: During your interview.

title: Think Tank
line: My dialogue with the artificial intelligence.

title: Think Tank
line: It was the most efficient way to evaluate your abilities. I am sure you can appreciate that.

title: Think Tank
line: How much do you know about me?

title: Think Tank
line: Enough to know that you are tapping into only a fraction of your potential as a member of Voyager's crew. You were adjusting the deflector array to improve shield harmonics. Do you find such duties challenging?

title: Think Tank
line: No.

title: Think Tank
line: Without problems that test the limits of your abilities, you cannot expand them. Perfection will always be beyond your reach. Seven, you could become one of the greatest intellects in the galaxy, but that will not happen here among these limited lifeforms.

title: Think Tank
line: The crew of Voyager has accepted me, integrated me into their Collective.

title: Think Tank
line: They are your family. It was hard for me to leave my family, too. And I was only a child. Not much older than you when you were first assimilated.

title: Think Tank
line: Why did you leave?

title: Think Tank
line: To help them and my world solve a cataclysmic problem.

title: Think Tank
line: The Think Tank requested you as payment.

title: Think Tank
line: I did not realize it at first. I was too young. But they gave me a remarkable opportunity, and now I am offering the same to you.

title: Think Tank
line: Your group can assist many Collectives, and yet you often use that ability as a means of coercion to obtain what you want. How many have suffered because they were unwilling to agree to your conditions?

title: Think Tank
line: We have a singular mission, to perfect our knowledge. Perfection sometimes necessitates selfishness. It is your life. Not Voyager's, not Captain Janeway's or anyone else's. It is up to you to achieve the goals you have set for yourself.

title: Think Tank
line: I agree, but I can do that here.

title: Think Tank
line: Please, take more time to think about this. We will remain nearby in case you change your mind.

title: Think Tank
line: I doubt that will happen.

title: Think Tank
line: Seven of Nine, report to the bridge.

title: Think Tank
line: Acknowledged.

title: Think Tank
line: May I accompany you?

title: Think Tank
line: As you wish.

title: Think Tank
line: Do you have a problem, Captain?

title: Think Tank
line: Two Hazari ships are approaching.

title: Think Tank
line: I have declined their offer.

title: Think Tank
line: Our first offer.

title: Think Tank
line: Glad you're sticking around. Take your station.

title: Think Tank
line: They are dropping out of warp, flanking our position.

title: Think Tank
line: Which one fired?

title: Think Tank
line: The ship to starboard. Shields down to sixty percent.

title: Think Tank
line: Evasive maneuvers. Target their weapons systems and return fire.

title: Think Tank
line: Their shields are holding.

title: Think Tank
line: I can't get away. They're right on top of us.

title: Think Tank
line: Hull integrity's been compromised on decks seven and twelve.

title: Think Tank
line: Captain, when the Hazari strike in pairs, one ship always remains behind to reinforce the shields of the attacking vessel.

title: Think Tank
line: So we should target the support ship. How much is this tip going to cost me?

title: Think Tank
line: This one is free.

title: Think Tank
line: I'll take it. Tuvok.

title: Think Tank
line: Retargeting. Firing photon torpedoes. They are disengaging.

title: Think Tank
line: Get us out of here, maximum warp. Thanks for the help.

title: Think Tank
line: Consider it a friendly gesture of goodwill in the hopes that Seven will change her mind.

title: Think Tank
line: I have not.

title: Think Tank
line: You are making a fatal mistake. We have already analyzed hundreds of scenarios. Voyager will not survive without our help.

title: Think Tank
line: Your scenarios, not mine.

title: Think Tank
line: Your confidence is unfounded, Captain. Reconsider. Order Seven of Nine to join us.

title: Think Tank
line: We have an old expression, Kurros. Don't call us, we'll call you. Remodulate the shields to a phase variance frequency.

title: Think Tank
line: His ship is vanishing from sensors. It's being absorbed into subspace.

title: Think Tank
line: I get the distinct feeling they won't take no for an answer.

title: Think Tank
line: Same here. Looks like we're facing two threats now. The Hazari and our would-be saviors.

title: Think Tank
line: Our offer was denied. How shall we proceed?

title: Think Tank
line: We are already proceeding.

title: Think Tank
line: Our offer was refused. We must let the scenario continue.

title: Think Tank
line: Our calculations indicate a ninety six percent chance the Borg will still be ours.

title: Think Tank
line: Then it is decided. We will wait and let our problem solve itself.

title: Think Tank
line: Duranium hull fragments, a thruster assembly, human organic residue. We were supposed to disable their ship, not destroy it.

title: Think Tank
line: They've entered the debris field.

title: Think Tank
line: Detonate the spatial charges.

title: Think Tank
line: Their vessel has taken heavy damage. Shields and weapons are offline.

title: Think Tank
line: Move us into position. Lock on a tractor beam and pull them into the shuttlebay.

title: Think Tank
line: We're in transporter range.

title: Think Tank
line: I've got a lock. Two lifeforms.

title: Think Tank
line: Energize.

title: Think Tank
line: Any luck?

title: Think Tank
line: I'm still trying to access their primary database.

title: Think Tank
line: Let me guess. They're the strong but silent types.

title: Think Tank
line: Very silent.

title: Think Tank
line: Did you try a mind meld?

title: Think Tank
line: Without success. They are unusually resistant.

title: Think Tank
line: Well, hold off on the torture till we see what we can dig up here.

title: Think Tank
line: I've found something. A series of encoded transmissions.

title: Think Tank
line: They've been discussing Voyager. Our coordinates, our defenses.

title: Think Tank
line: Whoever hired the Hazari know a lot about us.

title: Think Tank
line: Check these sensor logs. See if they had any visitors recently.

title: Think Tank
line: I've got some bioreadings, but they're pretty scrambled.

title: Think Tank
line: If they are bioreadings, perhaps the Doctor can unscramble them.

title: Think Tank
line: Tell him to give it a try.

title: Think Tank
line: I've created a forensic reconstruction from the bioreadings, using the holoemitters. Brace yourselves.

title: Think Tank
line: Malon. Huh, they must really hold a grudge. We haven't run into them for months. I'm sorry, Doctor, something doesn't feel right.

title: Think Tank
line: The Malon are economically motivated.

title: Think Tank
line: And there's no profit in revenge. Take a look at this. Isomorphic signatures embedded in the bioreadings. This was no Malon, it was only a projection.

title: Think Tank
line: You mean that's a hologram of a hologram?

title: Think Tank
line: In a manner of speaking. I believe I can restore the original biosignal parameters. Brace yourself.

title: Think Tank
line: Well, it appears our Hazari paradox is more complex than we thought.

title: Think Tank
line: I believe we're both being manipulated by the same person. Recognize him?

title: Think Tank
line: No.

title: Think Tank
line: His name is Kurros, The Malon you met with was nothing more than a projection.

title: Think Tank
line: My sensors would have detected a hologram.

title: Think Tank
line: Not this one. Kurros is a member of a Think Tank. They solve problems for a price. Oh, you have heard of them.

title: Think Tank
line: They're notorious in this sector. They've made quite a few enemies.

title: Think Tank
line: Enemies who might be willing to pay a hell of a bounty.

title: Think Tank
line: Their technology is very advanced. It makes them difficult to track.

title: Think Tank
line: Not if we work together. You're the best hunters in the quadrant and we have the perfect lure. All we have to do now is out-think the Think Tank.

title: Think Tank
line: We've got a puzzle and we're not leaving this room until we solve it. The Think Tank is out there somewhere, hiding in subspace. How do we find them? And even if we can, their ship's hull is neutronium-based alloy, impervious to our weapons. How do we capture them?

title: Think Tank
line: What if we send out a multispatial probe?

title: Think Tank
line: It would take weeks of scanning to find them.

title: Think Tank
line: Weeks? We're not willing to wait that long.

title: Think Tank
line: We could use subspatial charges to force them into the open.

title: Think Tank
line: Where do we target the charges? We've still got to find them first.

title: Think Tank
line: Maybe we're going about this the wrong way. A direct assault seems unlikely to succeed. Pure tactics, psychology. That's how they solve problems. That's what we have to do. They've created this paradox to manipulate us into giving them Seven of Nine. How do we manipulate them? Think.

title: Think Tank
line: I thought we were onto something with B'Elanna's plan

title: Think Tank
line: Forget it. I was wrong.

title: Think Tank
line: Let him talk.

title: Think Tank
line: We're talking in circles.

title: Think Tank
line: Enough! Three hours, no progress. I should have contacted my ships by now.

title: Think Tank
line: Maybe we can't out-think them.

title: Think Tank
line: Captain?

title: Think Tank
line: We have to assume they've planned for every contingency, including anything we could come up with to undermine their plan. This thing has been driving me crazy. You said you knew the solution. Prove it.

title: Think Tank
line: Seven, how'd you do that?

title: Think Tank
line: I scanned the device. Its mechanism operates on a simple fractal regression.

title: Think Tank
line: You scanned it? That's cheating.

title: Think Tank
line: Cheating is often more efficient.

title: Think Tank
line: If you can't solve a puzzle, cheat. If you can't out-think a Think Tank, don't try.

title: Think Tank
line: Are you suggesting we give up?

title: Think Tank
line: Not at all. When you were in contact with the artificial intelligence, you were linked through their internal communications array.

title: Think Tank
line: Yes, for several seconds.

title: Think Tank
line: If you were to link with them again, we might be able to disrupt those systems. If they can't communicate, they can't function as a Think Tank. They'd be vulnerable.

title: Think Tank
line: Back to square one. How do we find them?

title: Think Tank
line: Simple. We give them what they want. You're going to join their group willingly.

title: Think Tank
line: They won't believe her.

title: Think Tank
line: We'll have to make them believe. Pull up a chair. We've got some more work to do.

title: Think Tank
line: An Hazari vessel is sending hails into subspace. It's trying to contact us.

title: Think Tank
line: Put them through.

title: Think Tank
line: They're responding.

title: Think Tank
line: Hazari vessel, we have received your hails. Can we be of assistance?

title: Think Tank
line: You deceived us.

title: Think Tank
line: I do not believe we have met.

title: Think Tank
line: Stop the pretense. You wanted us to deliver Voyager. Very well. But only if you triple our bounty.

title: Think Tank
line: My friend, regardless of the circumstances, we have a contract.

title: Think Tank
line: Pay us, or we let Voyager go.

title: Think Tank
line: All right, we will triple the bounty. But you must deliver them to us now.

title: Think Tank
line: Agreed. We'll contact the rest of our ships. We'll seize Voyager as planned.

title: Think Tank
line: Shields down to thirty percent.

title: Think Tank
line: Return fire.

title: Think Tank
line: Our phasers aren't penetrating their shields.

title: Think Tank
line: That last volley took out our shield generators and phaser banks.

title: Think Tank
line: Life support's failing, all decks.

title: Think Tank
line: Let us be honest, Captain. Things do not seem to be going your way.

title: Think Tank
line: Don't count us out just yet.

title: Think Tank
line: I admit you have been clever. You uncovered our subterfuge, but you failed to factor in all the variables. The greed of the Hazari, for example.

title: Think Tank
line: Photon torpedoes?

title: Think Tank
line: Aft launchers are still online.

title: Think Tank
line: Target a full spread at the lead Hazari ship.

title: Think Tank
line: A few torpedoes will not alter the outcome. If you do not convince Seven of Nine to join us now, the destruction of your ship is ninety nine point eight percent certain.

title: Think Tank
line: Fire.

title: Think Tank
line: Direct hit. It's been disabled.

title: Think Tank
line: Clinging to that point two percentage? Hazari reinforcements should be here any minute.

title: Think Tank
line: He's right. Sensors just picked up a half dozen ships on an intercept course.

title: Think Tank
line: Captain, I'm detecting an unauthorized shuttle launch. It's Seven of Nine.

title: Think Tank
line: What the hell is she doing?

title: Think Tank
line: I believe she's saving your ship.

title: Think Tank
line: She's not answering hails. Her shuttle's being pulled into subspace. She's gone.

title: Think Tank
line: Have a safe journey home, Captain.

title: Think Tank
line: Seven of Nine, welcome.

title: Think Tank
line: Your hospitality is irrelevant. I am here because you left me no choice.

title: Think Tank
line: You gave into your human instincts to save your crew, as we knew you would. Just another factor in our equation.

title: Think Tank
line: If Voyager is destroyed, I will not cooperate.

title: Think Tank
line: Do not worry. The solution to the Hazari paradox is quite simple.

title: Think Tank
line: We have what we want. Call off your attack.

title: Think Tank
line: Not until we've been compensated.

title: Think Tank
line: Fine, but first order your other vessels to stand down.

title: Think Tank
line: Now, or we'll destroy Voyager.

title: Think Tank
line: Why is he in such a hurry?

title: Think Tank
line: Comply.

title: Think Tank
line: If we decloak, we would be vulnerable. The Hazari could make quite a bounty on us. Far more than we are paying them.

title: Think Tank
line: Their technology is inferior to yours. They would never attack you directly.

title: Think Tank
line: I think this is a trap, a new paradox your Captain has created for us. If we call their bluff, the Hazari might destroy Voyager, and we would lose you. If we reveal ourselves, we could be destroyed.

title: Think Tank
line: You told me, without problems to test the limits of your ability, you can never expand them.

title: Think Tank

title: Juggernaut

line: I just hope your boy enjoys it as much as I do.

line: We'll make it.

line: If you and Savar had a child of your own, you'd have an excuse to play with toys more often.

line: I'm detecting a fluctuation in tank four. There's a full scale rupture in progress.

line: We have no choice!

line: Impossible.

line: Communications are down.

title: Juggernaut
line: The flame, like emotion, is a primitive force. Left unchecked, it's chaotic, destructive. But if controlled it can be a powerful tool. The lamp controls the flame, as you must learn to control your emotions.

line: I told him three times to leave Engineering, but he kept buzzing around snapping pictures for some photo essay.

title: Juggernaut
line: A day in the life of the warp core.

title: Juggernaut
line: You have a long history of emotional volatility. The point of this exercise is not to atone for past transgressions, but to prevent future ones.

title: Juggernaut
line: You can't order someone to meditate.

line: Commander Chakotay thinks otherwise.

title: Juggernaut

title: Juggernaut
line: Envision the flame burning within you.

title: Juggernaut
line: Sorry.

title: Juggernaut
line: The flame grows hotter. A point of white light. Follow it backward through the years to a time when you were younger, a child. Is there something amusing, Lieutenant?

title: Juggernaut
line: I'm sorry, an image just flashed through my mind. You as a child, those pointy little ears. You must have been cute.

title: Juggernaut
line: Indeed. Please follow my instructions or we'll discontinue this exercise.

title: Juggernaut
line: Right. Me, childhood. How old?

title: Juggernaut
line: Your earliest memories. Try to recall a time when you experienced uncontrollable anger.

title: Juggernaut
line: Daniel Byrd.

title: Juggernaut
line: I beg your pardon?

title: Juggernaut
line: He was one of my classmates in grammar school. He was always terrorizing me. He used to point at my cranial ridges and tease me about being half Klingon. He called me Miss Turtlehead.

title: Juggernaut
line: That angered you.

title: Juggernaut
line: Of course, it did. So I attacked him once, during recess, on the gyro-swing. I disengaged the centrifugal governor. He was spinning so fast, he almost flew apart. Then I yanked him off the swing and started pounding his little face! If Miss Malvin hadn't showed up, I probably would have

title: Juggernaut
line: Describe the anger you felt at that moment.

title: Juggernaut
line: I, I wanted to hurt him. To take revenge for all the humiliation he caused me.

title: Juggernaut
line: Your anger was a source of strength. It protected you, gave you courage.

title: Juggernaut
line: I suppose it did.

title: Juggernaut
line: And when the Doctor tried to take a holo-photograph of you?

title: Juggernaut
line: I was annoyed. He kept getting in the way.

title: Juggernaut
line: The rage within you runs deep. It's been with you for many years.

title: Juggernaut
line: I'm not a Vulcan. I'll survive.

title: Juggernaut
line: Whatever you say, Miss Turtlehead.

title: Juggernaut
line: What did you say!

line: You're easily provoked. You must learn to master your emotions.

title: Juggernaut
line: Captain, we're receiving an automated distress call.

title: Juggernaut
line: Malon?

title: Juggernaut
line: Possibly. Lifesigns?

title: Juggernaut
line: Two, but they're erratic.

title: Juggernaut
line: Beam them to Sickbay. Initiate bio-hazard containment procedures.

title: Juggernaut
line: Theta radiation has affected a radius of six hundred million kilometers.

title: Juggernaut
line: Source?

title: Juggernaut
line: A Malon freighter traveling at high impulse. It appears to be abandoned.

title: Juggernaut
line: I thought we'd seen the last of the Malon.

title: Juggernaut
line: I guess they're looking for new places to dump their toxic waste.

title: Juggernaut
line: Do we know what happened to their ship? Were they attacked?

title: Juggernaut
line: I'm just as curious as you are. Can you revive either of them? I'm Captain Kathryn Janeway.

title: Juggernaut
line: Fesek. Controller Fesek. Where am I?

line: You're on my vessel. We responded to your distress call.

title: Juggernaut

line: It's heavily damaged.

title: Juggernaut
line: Where?

title: Juggernaut
line: Three million kilometers from here.

title: Juggernaut
line: That's too close. We've got to get further away.

title: Juggernaut
line: Calm down, calm down. Tell me what's wrong with your ship. Why did you abandon it?

title: Juggernaut
line: We were on a waste export mission.

title: Juggernaut
line: Dumping theta radiation.

title: Juggernaut
line: Two of the theta tanks ruptured. Systems malfunctioned one by one, communications, navigation, propulsion. We had no choice. Radiation was venting from every port. Over sixty crewmen died within minutes. It was chaos. We stumbled through the gas to get to the escape pods. Only a few of us made it. Where are the others?

title: Juggernaut
line: The two of you were the only ones we found alive.

title: Juggernaut
line: Listen to me very carefully. The fact that we're still here means the ship hasn't exploded, yet. When it does, over four trillion isotons of antimatter waste is going to ignite. Everything within three light years will be destroyed.

line: Go ahead.

line: Quickly.

line: Tuvok. Without warp drive there's no chance we'll clear the blast radius.

line: Agreed.

line: If we can't outrun your ship, maybe we can disable it.

line: Every deck has been contaminated. Anyone who goes on board will liquefy within minutes.

title: Juggernaut
line: We'll find a way.

line: We? I'm not going anywhere near that vessel.

title: Juggernaut
line: You can either stay and help us or I'll send you back to your escape pod. Your choice. Clean them up, Doctor. I need them on the bridge.

line: How long until those storage tanks explode?

title: Juggernaut
line: Approximately six hours.

title: Juggernaut
line: Can we get an away team on board?

title: Juggernaut
line: The freighter's hull is intact. Life support appears to be operational. However, thirty three of forty two decks are flooded with high levels of theta radiation.

title: Juggernaut
line: Including the control room, which is where we'd have to go to reestablish containment. As I told you.

title: Juggernaut
line: We could beam on to one of the lower levels where there's less radiation, and vent the contaminated sections one by one.

title: Juggernaut
line: Clear a path to the control room.

title: Juggernaut
line: I appreciate what you're trying to do, but if what you're considering were possible, we'd have tried it before we abandoned the ship. We have years of experience aboard freighters of this gradient.

title: Juggernaut
line: Your experience is what got us into this mess in the first place.

title: Juggernaut
line: That's enough, Lieutenant.

title: Juggernaut
line: Maybe there's another way.

title: Juggernaut
line: I'm listening.

title: Juggernaut
line: Four hours from here there's a nebula that could protect us from the blast. We could alter course, wait there until after the explosion.

title: Juggernaut
line: There are at least three other ships in the sector. What about them?

title: Juggernaut
line: I don't see what we can do.

title: Juggernaut
line: So hundreds of people become contaminated because you're not willing to clean up your garbage.

line: Lieutenant. Assemble an away team. We're going over there.

title: Juggernaut
line: Wait! Tell them about the Vihaar.

title: Juggernaut
line: What's he talking about?

title: Juggernaut
line: Nothing. It's a myth.

line: What kind of myth?

line: It's an old story shared among freighter crews. Some of them say they've seen creatures in the theta storage tanks.

title: Juggernaut
line: Creatures?

title: Juggernaut
line: Created by radiogenic waste. According to the legend, they are poisonous monsters that wreak havoc aboard Malon ships. It's a common belief among our more superstitious recruits.

title: Juggernaut
line: I never believed it myself, but during the evacuation some of the crew people saw something. A form.

title: Juggernaut
line: Hallucinations are one of the first symptoms of theta poisoning. You know that.

title: Juggernaut
line: Maybe. Then how do you explain what happened? We checked every system.

title: Juggernaut
line: You'd say anything to get out of going back to that freighter.

title: Juggernaut
line: If you'd been there, you'd be afraid to go back, too.

title: Juggernaut
line: This chamber seems to be the least affected by radiation. We'll beam in there.

title: Juggernaut
line: That's fifteen decks below the control room.

title: Juggernaut
line: We'll have to work our way up.

title: Juggernaut
line: The pressurization systems, they're offline. How will we vent the gas?

title: Juggernaut
line: There are two main airlocks on each deck. We'll open them as we go. Perform a series of controlled decompressions.

title: Juggernaut
line: What's to stop us from being vented?

title: Juggernaut
line: Forcefields. I spent six years aboard a Talaxian garbage scow. I know a few things about waste management.

title: Juggernaut
line: Even low levels of theta radiation can be lethal.

title: Juggernaut
line: Our Doctor's developed an inoculation. It'll temporarily prevent our cells from absorbing the radiation.

title: Juggernaut
line: How long will it last?

title: Juggernaut
line: Two, three hours.

title: Juggernaut
line: Half of the doors and bulkheads are fused. The ascenders are offline. It could take us twice as long as that to reach the control room.

title: Juggernaut
line: Then we'll have to work quickly. We'll take phasers to cut through any obstacles.

title: Juggernaut
line: I've ordered my men to do a lot of risky things, but nothing as foolish as this.

title: Juggernaut
line: More foolish than towing around a trillion isotons of toxic waste?

title: Juggernaut
line: We take every precaution to keep it contained.

title: Juggernaut
line: Until you dump it in someone's back yard.

line: Is your crew always so diplomatic?

line: Your concerns are noted. Get them inoculated. We'll meet you in Transporter room one.

line: Lunch, and dinner, and a midnight snack have all been taken care of. This is for me. It's a Talaxian theta radiation remedy. Crushed rama leaf and katyllian clove. It helps fortify the cellular membranes.

line: I think the Doctor's inoculation might be a better way to go.

line: For sending me on such an important mission. Not that my duties in the mess hall aren't challenging.

title: Juggernaut
line: It was an easy choice. You were the best man for the job.

line: Well, our scow once ran smack into a theta radiation field. Knocked the propulsion out. We had no choice but to sit there. We were barely alive when they found us. If it hadn't been for this, nobody would have survived.

line: Once you get past the choking reflex it's really not so bad. Want to try some?

line: We'll have to crawl into an injector port. It's only big enough for two people.

line: You think we're animals, don't you?

line: I'm a waste controller half the year. Do you know what I do the rest of the time? I'm a sculptor.

line: Have you ever been to Malon Prime? It's a remarkable place. It's one of the most beautiful worlds you'll ever see. Our planet would choke with industrial wastes if it weren't for the sacrifices of people like me.

line: Do you have any idea of the trouble we go to, to locate isolated areas? Ah, manual actuators. I'll release them, you monitor the pressure variance.

line: I've been working on a contingency plan.

line: A series of carefully timed tractor pulses could alter the freighter's course. But given the vessel's weakened state, one miscalculation could set off the explosion.
